children.title: Machine Environment Coordinate
children.top_down_role: Machine counts, machine types, speed classes, and shop configurations.

assumptions_latex: A scheduling instance has a finite machine set \(M\), operation set \(O\), and a separately specified objective.
Machine descriptors are invariant under relabeling of machines and exclude job, resource, and objective data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(\alpha_M(I)\) is the machine-environment coordinate of instance \(I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard scheduling classifications separate the processing-machine environment from job characteristics and the objective
source_required: supplied locators do not support the expanded coordinate convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the machine component of an expanded environment-coordinate pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(I\), define \(\alpha_M(I)\) to be the equivalence class of its machine-side processing structure under machine relabeling. This structure specifies the number of machines, whether they are single, identical parallel, uniformly related, unrelated, or arranged in dedicated routes such as flow-shop, job-shop, or open-shop systems, and any machine capacities intrinsic to that structure. It excludes auxiliary-resource supplies, operation eligibility data, job attributes, temporal constraints, and the performance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The machine coordinate records the instance's machine topology and processing-machine type, independently of resources, jobs, timing restrictions, and the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Machine Environment Coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the machine-environment leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation supports the proposed equivalence-class coordinate, its detailed scope boundaries, or the inclusion of intrinsic machine capacities. The unrelated local inventory cannot establish this convention.

children.title: Resource Environment Coordinate
children.top_down_role: Renewable, consumable, secondary, and capacity-limited resource environments.

assumptions_latex: A scheduling instance has finite resource types \(R\) with availability functions \(B_r:\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\).
Machine structure, job data, and the objective are represented separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(\alpha_R(I)\) is the resource-environment coordinate of instance \(I\).

notation.meaning: available amount of resource type r at time t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: resource-constrained scheduling models classify renewable, nonrenewable, and cumulative capacities separately from machines
source_required: supplied locators do not establish this coordinate notation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines auxiliary-resource supply independently of the machine environment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(I\), define \(\alpha_R(I)\) as the equivalence class, under resource-type relabeling, of the auxiliary-resource supply system \(\{B_r:r\in R\}\), together with each resource's renewal regime, divisibility, and capacity law. Typical regimes include renewable, nonrenewable, doubly constrained, and cumulative resources. Operation-specific demands and machine-resource eligibility are excluded and recorded as compatibility data; machine topology, job attributes, temporal constraints, and the objective are also excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The resource coordinate records auxiliary-resource types, capacities, and renewal laws, while leaving demands and compatibility to separate coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Environment Coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the resource-environment leaf, but the equivalence-class construction and separation of supplies, demands, and compatibility require a scheduling or resource-constrained scheduling source. No cited evidence supports the stated coordinate convention.

children.title: Machine–Resource Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Eligibility, capability, and compatibility relations linking operations to resources.

assumptions_latex: The machine set \(M\), operation set \(O\), and resource-capacity system are fixed.
Each operation has a specified family of admissible machine and resource-demand assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An assignment is environment-feasible exactly when every operation receives a pair belonging to \(K_o\) and aggregate simultaneous demands respect all resource capacities.

notation.meaning: admissible machine-demand pairs for operation o

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: eligibility relations and cumulative capacity inequalities are standard compatibility predicates
source_required: supplied locators do not support the combined machine-resource formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses admissible machine-demand pairs to couple machine and resource environments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(o\in O\), let \(K_o\subseteq M\times D\) contain precisely the admissible pairs \((m,d)\), where \(m\) may process \(o\) and \(d=(d_r)_{r\in R}\) is its resource-demand vector on that machine. A scheduled assignment \((m_o,d^o)_{o\in O}\) is machine-resource compatible if \((m_o,d^o)\in K_o\) for every \(o\), and, at every time \(t\) and for every renewable resource \(r\), \(\sum_{o:\,t\in[S_o,C_o)}d^o_r\le B_r(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility requires every operation to use an allowed machine-demand pair and all simultaneous resource demands to remain within capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Machine–Resource Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate role for this compatibility leaf, but the combined eligibility-and-capacity formulation lacks supporting evidence. The statement also uses start and completion times S_o and C_o without introducing them in the assumptions or notation, and it addresses only renewable-resource capacity despite the broader resource environment.

children.title: Job Coordinate
children.top_down_role: Job-level attributes, release regimes, priorities, and due-date characteristics.

assumptions_latex: The finite operation set \(O\) is partitioned into nonempty job blocks.
Operation-level processing and machine data are represented separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equivalence class \(\beta_J(I)\) is the job coordinate of instance \(I\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scheduling instances conventionally distinguish jobs from their constituent operations
source_required: no supplied locator supports the proposed subcoordinate decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines job identity and job-level attributes, excluding operation and timing data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(I\), the job coordinate \(\beta_J(I)\) is the equivalence class, under job relabeling, of a finite index set \(J\), a partition \(O=\biguplus_{j\in J}O_j\), and all attributes attached to whole jobs rather than individual operations or times. Such attributes may include job classes, priorities, weights, and family membership. Processing durations, routes, machine eligibility, release dates, deadlines, and interoperation time lags are excluded from this coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The job coordinate records how operations form jobs and which attributes belong to whole jobs, independently of processing and timing data.
knowledge_statements.title: Job Coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the right definitional role and matches the job-coordinate leaf, but no source supports this particular decomposition, the equivalence under job relabeling, or the asserted boundary between job and temporal attributes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Job Preference Order and Transitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a coordinatewise preference relation using processing time, weight, release time, and due date.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define job \(j\) to be preferred over job \(k\) when \(p_j\leq p_k\), \(w_j\geq w_k\), \(r_j+p_j\leq r_k+p_k\), and \(d_j-p_j\geq d_k-p_k\). This preference relation is transitive: if \(j\) is preferred over \(k\) and \(k\) is preferred over \(\ell\), then \(j\) is preferred over \(\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Job j is preferred over job k when j has no greater processing time, no smaller weight, no greater release-time-plus-processing value, and no smaller due-date-minus-processing value. This preference relation is transitive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j\succeq_{\mathrm{pref}}k\iff\bigl(p_j\leq p_k,\ w_j\geq w_k,\ r_j+p_j\leq r_k+p_k,\ d_j-p_j\geq d_k-p_k\bigr),\qquad (j\succeq_{\mathrm{pref}}k\land k\succeq_{\mathrm{pref}}\ell)\Rightarrow j\succeq_{\mathrm{pref}}\ell

source_evidence.locator: More Advanced General Purpose Procedures / 15.3. Constraint Programming / Definition 15.3.1

knowledge_statements.title: Job Preference Order and Transitivity

children.title: Operation Coordinate
children.top_down_role: Operation structure, routing, divisibility, and processing characteristics.

assumptions_latex: A finite operation set \(O\) and machine set \(M\) are given.
Job membership, temporal constraints, and the objective are represented separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equivalence class \(\beta_O(I)\) is the operation coordinate of instance \(I\).

notation.meaning: processing requirement of operation o on machine m

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operation processing times, modes, and routes are standard scheduling-instance data
source_required: no supplied locator supports the exact boundary between operation and compatibility coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines operation-level processing data within the expanded second field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an instance \(I\), define \(\beta_O(I)\) as the equivalence class, under operation relabeling preserving job membership, of the operation-level processing specification. It records each operation's required processing amount, admissible modes, mode-dependent durations \(p_{om}\), and route or technological-stage labels. Machine-resource admissibility is recorded by the compatibility relation, while releases, deadlines, precedence relations, time lags, job-level attributes, and the performance criterion are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The operation coordinate records operation-level processing requirements, modes, durations, and technological roles, excluding compatibility, timing, job, and objective data.
knowledge_statements.title: Operation Coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is locally relevant, but its boundary with machine-resource compatibility and its equivalence-class convention are unsupported. Moreover, p_{om} is described as machine-indexed processing time while the statement also invokes general admissible modes, which may require a mode index distinct from a machine index.

children.title: Temporal-Constraint Coordinate
children.top_down_role: Precedence, lag, availability, synchronization, and time-window restrictions.

assumptions_latex: Operations have start times \(S_o\) and completion times \(C_o\).
All time-indexed restrictions are specified independently of the performance criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The collection \(\beta_T(I)\) defines the temporally feasible set of schedules for instance \(I\).

notation.meaning: start and completion times of operation o
release time and deadline of operation o

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: releases, deadlines, precedence constraints, and time lags are standard temporal predicates
source_required: supplied project-scheduling locator is too indirect for this full coordinate definition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects time-domain restrictions but excludes machine and resource capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The temporal-constraint coordinate \(\beta_T(I)\) is the conjunction of all predicates imposed directly on operation times. It may contain release and deadline inequalities \(S_o\ge r_o\) and \(C_o\le d_o\), precedence constraints \(C_o\le S_{o'}\), generalized lags \(\ell_{oo'}\le S_{o'}-C_o\le u_{oo'}\), calendars, and permitted time windows. A schedule is temporally feasible exactly when its start and completion vector satisfies every predicate in \(\beta_T(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The temporal coordinate is the complete set of release, deadline, precedence, lag, calendar, and time-window constraints on operation times.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal-Constraint Coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical predicates are recognizable temporal constraints, but the exact coordinate decomposition is unsupported. Because the terminal container is a coordinate and the statement defines beta_T(I), content_kind should ordinarily be definition rather than condition unless the taxonomy's convention is documented by a source.

assumptions_latex: The feasible schedule set \(\mathcal{S}(I)\) is nonempty.
Every schedule \(s\in\mathcal{S}(I)\) determines the quantities used by the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheduling problem's third coordinate is \(\gamma(I)=(\operatorname{dir},F_I)\), and its optimal value is \(\operatorname{opt}_{s\in\mathcal{S}(I)}F_I(s)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the third field of standard scheduling notation specifies the optimization criterion
source_required: supplied criterion locators do not document scheduling three-field notation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the objective field independently of feasibility coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The performance-criterion coordinate of an instance \(I\) is the pair \(\gamma(I)=(\operatorname{dir},F_I)\), where \(F_I:\mathcal{S}(I)\to\mathbb{R}\) is a scalar schedule functional and \(\operatorname{dir}\in\{\min,\max\}\). For multiple criteria, \(F_I\) must include the stated aggregation or ordering rule, such as a weighted sum or lexicographic order. Examples include makespan \(C_{\max}\), total weighted completion time \(\sum_j w_jC_j\), and maximum lateness \(L_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The performance coordinate specifies whether to minimize or maximize and gives the exact scalar objective, including any multicriteria aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Performance-Criterion Coordinate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate for this coordinate, but no scheduling source supports the proposed third-field representation. The claim also requires F_I to be real-valued while listing lexicographic order as an example; a lexicographic criterion is not represented by a scalar real-valued functional without an explicit scalar encoding.

children.title: Semi-Active Schedules
children.top_down_role: Schedules characterized by local left-shift restrictions under a fixed operation order.

assumptions_latex: The schedule is feasible, nonpreemptive, and has fixed operation assignments.
A local left shift changes only one operation's start time and preserves all other operation start times and machine sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible schedule \(s\) is semi-active if and only if no operation admits a positive feasible local left shift.

notation.meaning: start time of operation o in schedule s
schedule obtained by moving only o earlier by delta

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: absence of a feasible local left shift is the standard definition of a semi-active schedule
source_required: supplied locators do not cover schedule activity classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard nonpreemptive local-left-shift definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible nonpreemptive schedule \(s\), let \(s^{o,\delta}\) retain every assignment, machine order, and start time except that of operation \(o\), with \(S_o(s^{o,\delta})=S_o(s)-\delta\) for \(\delta>0\). The schedule \(s\) is semi-active precisely when, for every operation \(o\) and every \(\delta>0\), the schedule \(s^{o,\delta}\) is infeasible. Thus no operation can start earlier through a local left shift without violating a constraint or changing an established processing order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonpreemptive schedule is semi-active when no single operation can be moved earlier while all other starts and machine orders remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Semi-Active Schedules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local-left-shift formulation are suitable for the semi-active-schedule leaf, but no scheduling reference with a specific definition or page is cited. The supplied inventory contains no source on schedule activity classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semi-Active Schedule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the semi-active class for feasible nonpreemptive machine schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible nonpreemptive schedule S is semi-active if no operation can be completed earlier without changing the processing order on at least one machine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible nonpreemptive schedule is semi-active if no operation can be completed earlier without changing the processing order on at least one machine.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is a feasible nonpreemptive schedule}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is semi-active}\iff\text{no operation can be completed earlier without changing the processing order on at least one machine}

source_evidence.locator: Deterministic Models: Preliminaries / 2.3. Classes of Schedules / Definition 2.3.5

children.title: Active Schedules
children.top_down_role: Schedules organized around global advancement restrictions and dominance roles.

assumptions_latex: The schedule is feasible and nonpreemptive.
Operation assignments are fixed, but machine sequences may change when comparing schedules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible schedule \(s\) is active if and only if no feasible schedule globally left-shifts any operation without delaying another operation.

notation.meaning: start time of operation o in schedule s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global left-shift dominance is the standard definition of an active schedule
source_required: supplied locators do not cover schedule activity classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses componentwise start-time dominance for nonpreemptive schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible nonpreemptive schedule \(s\) is active if there is no feasible schedule \(s'\) on the same instance and with the same operation assignments such that \(S_o(s')\le S_o(s)\) for every \(o\in O\) and \(S_k(s')<S_k(s)\) for at least one \(k\in O\). Equivalently, no operation can be started earlier, even after resequencing, without forcing at least one other operation to start later.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active schedule admits no feasible global rearrangement that starts every operation no later and at least one operation earlier.
knowledge_statements.title: Active Schedules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible for active nonpreemptive schedules, but it needs an authoritative activity-class source. The restriction to comparison schedules with the same operation assignments must also be supported or scoped to a fixed-assignment model, especially where alternative-machine scheduling is allowed.

children.title: Non-Delay Schedules
children.top_down_role: Schedules organized around immediate resource use whenever eligible work is available.

assumptions_latex: The schedule is feasible and nonpreemptive.
An operation is available at time \(t\) when all constraints required for its immediate start at \(t\), except machine availability, are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule is non-delay if and only if it contains no avoidable machine-idle interval.

notation.meaning: set of operations available at time t
machines eligible to process operation o

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: absence of avoidable machine idleness is the standard non-delay condition
source_required: supplied locators do not cover non-delay schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States non-delay behavior for eligible-machine, nonpreemptive processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible nonpreemptive schedule is non-delay if, for every time \(t\) and machine \(m\in M\), machine \(m\) is not idle at \(t\) whenever there exists an unscheduled operation \(o\in A(t)\) with \(m\in M_o\) that can begin on \(m\) at \(t\) without violating resource capacities. Hence every idle interval is forced by unavailability, incompatibility, or another feasibility constraint, rather than by a scheduling choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-delay schedule never leaves a machine idle when an available, eligible operation could feasibly start on it immediately.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Delay Schedules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is the correct role, but no source supports this eligible-machine and resource-capacity variant of non-delay scheduling. The phrase 'unscheduled operation' is ambiguous at an arbitrary time t and should be replaced by a precisely defined not-yet-started or ready operation once the sourced model is fixed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Non-Delay Schedule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the non-delay class for feasible machine schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible schedule S is non-delay if no machine is kept idle while an operation is waiting for processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible schedule is non-delay if no machine is kept idle while an operation is waiting for processing.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ is a feasible schedule}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is non-delay}\iff\text{no machine is kept idle while an operation is waiting for processing}
