children.title: PERT Duration Estimation
children.top_down_role: PERT-style treatment of uncertain activity durations.

knowledge_statements.title: PERT Duration Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical three-point beta approximation used in PERT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an activity with optimistic, most-likely, and pessimistic duration estimates satisfying \(0\le a\le m\le b\), classical PERT replaces its uncertain duration by the mean estimate \[\mu=\frac{a+4m+b}{6}\] and the variance estimate \[\sigma^2=\left(\frac{b-a}{6}\right)^2.\] These formulas are a modeling approximation based on a beta-shaped duration distribution over \([a,b]\), not consequences of the three quantiles alone. Under the additional approximation that activity durations on a selected path are independent, that path’s mean and variance are obtained by summing the corresponding activity means and variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical PERT weights the most-likely duration four times in its mean and estimates variance from one-sixth of the optimistic–pessimistic range.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le a\le m\le b\).
Pathwise variance addition assumes independent activity durations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu=(a+4m+b)/6\) and \(\sigma^2=((b-a)/6)^2\) under the classical PERT approximation.

notation.meaning: optimistic, most-likely, and pessimistic duration estimates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classical PERT formulas and their approximation caveat fit the leaf, but the formulas, beta-distribution interpretation, and independence-based path aggregation have no cited source.

children.title: Project Completion-Time Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Distributional analysis of project completion timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Project Completion-Time Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact random longest-path representation for precedence-only stochastic project completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic activity-on-node network with random nonnegative activity durations \((D_i)_{i\in V}\), all defined on one probability space. When activities start as soon as their predecessors finish and no resource constraints apply, the random project completion time is \[T=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_{s,t}}\sum_{i\in P}D_i,\] where \(\mathcal P_{s,t}\) is the set of source-to-sink paths. Hence the distribution of \(T\) is generally not determined by marginal activity means and variances alone: it also depends on their joint distribution and on competition among paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With uncertain durations and precedence constraints only, completion time is the maximum random duration over all source-to-sink paths and depends on cross-activity dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic with designated source and sink.
Durations are jointly defined, nonnegative random variables, and no resource constraints apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_{s,t}}\sum_{i\in P}D_i\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The random longest-path representation is precise and fits the uncertainty leaf, but its exact stochastic completion-time claim and joint-distribution qualification lack an authoritative source locator.

children.title: Criticality Under Duration Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Path criticality when activity durations are uncertain.

knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Under Duration Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines activity criticality by membership in a longest realized project path, including ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite acyclic activity-on-arc project network with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and nonnegative random activity durations \((D_e)_{e\in E}\). For an outcome \(\omega\), define the project duration by \[T(\omega)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P_{st}}\sum_{e\in P}D_e(\omega).\] An activity \(e\) is critical at \(\omega\) when it belongs to at least one path attaining this maximum. Its criticality index is \[\kappa_e=\Pr\!\left(e\in P\text{ for some }P\in\arg\max_{Q\in\mathcal P_{st}}\sum_{a\in Q}D_a\right).\] Thus tied longest paths all contribute to criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An activity’s criticality index is the probability that it lies on at least one longest source-to-sink path under the realized random durations.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
\(D_e\ge 0\) almost surely for every \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le \kappa_e\le 1\) measures realized longest-path membership, with all ties retained.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the probabilistic criticality-index definition and its tie convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the displayed mathematics is internally coherent. However, no citation supports the particular criticality-index convention, especially counting membership in any tied longest path, so source uncertainty prevents acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Mode Resource-Constrained Projects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nonpreemptive single-mode RCPSP with renewable resources and makespan minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-mode resource-constrained project consists of activities \(V\), precedence arcs \(E\), fixed durations \(p_i\), fixed renewable-resource demands \(a_{ir}\), and capacities \(B_r\). A schedule assigns one start time \(S_i\) to each activity and is feasible when \[S_j\ge S_i+p_i\quad((i,j)\in E),\qquad \sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}a_{ir}\le B_r\quad(r,t).\] Each activity has exactly one execution mode, so its duration and demands are not decision variables. The standard RCPSP minimizes the makespan \(C_{\max}=\max_i(S_i+p_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity has one fixed duration and resource-demand vector; start times must satisfy precedence and periodwise renewable capacities, usually while minimizing makespan.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive.
The precedence graph \((V,E)\) is acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible solution is a start-time vector satisfying every precedence and renewable-capacity constraint.
review_flags: The supplied project-scheduling locator does not specifically identify the standard RCPSP formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate for this problem-family leaf, and the formulation resembles the standard nonpreemptive single-mode RCPSP. No source is cited, and the resource and time index domains are not explicitly introduced; an authoritative formulation with a specific locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Multimode Resource-Constrained Projects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nonpreemptive multimode RCPSP with renewable and nonrenewable resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multimode resource-constrained project assigns each activity \(i\) a finite mode set \(M_i\). Selecting \(m_i\in M_i\) fixes duration \(p_{im_i}\), renewable demands \(a_{im_i r}\), and nonrenewable consumptions \(q_{im_i k}\). A feasible solution chooses \((m_i,S_i)\) such that \[S_j\ge S_i+p_{im_i}\quad((i,j)\in E),\] \[\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_{im_i}}a_{im_i r}\le B_r\quad(r,t),\qquad \sum_i q_{im_i k}\le Q_k\quad(k).\] The usual objective is to minimize \(\max_i(S_i+p_{im_i})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mode is chosen for every activity, jointly determining its duration and resource use; the resulting schedule must satisfy precedence and resource limits.
assumptions_latex: Every mode set \(M_i\) is finite and nonempty.
Activities are nonpreemptive.
All durations, demands, consumptions, and capacities are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires a compatible joint choice of execution modes and start times.

notation.meaning: Available execution modes for activity i.
Project-wide capacity of nonrenewable resource k.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the multimode RCPSP formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the multimode problem-family leaf, and the renewable and nonrenewable constraints are mutually consistent. No citation supports the exact model variant, while the renewable-resource, nonrenewable-resource, and time domains remain implicit.

children.title: Renewable Resources
children.top_down_role: Period-by-period resource availability in project schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Renewable Resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodwise capacity model for resources replenished between time periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a project schedule, a resource \(r\) is renewable when its capacity \(B_r(t)\) constrains simultaneous use separately at every time \(t\), while use in one period does not reduce later capacity. For nonpreemptive activities with start times \(S_i\), durations \(p_i\), and demands \(a_{ir}\), feasibility is exactly \[\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}a_{ir}\le B_r(t)\qquad\text{for every }t.\] No project-wide sum of these demands is imposed merely by renewability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A renewable resource has a capacity restored across periods, so only the total demand of activities executing simultaneously is bounded.
assumptions_latex: Resource demand is constant throughout each activity’s execution.
\(a_{ir}\ge 0\) and \(B_r(t)\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Renewable-resource feasibility is characterized by the pointwise capacity inequalities.

notation.meaning: Per-time demand of activity i for resource r.
Available capacity of resource r at time t.

review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports the renewable-resource classification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and pointwise-capacity interpretation fit renewable resources. Acceptance requires a scheduling-specific source with a precise locator, including support for the time model and the stated characterization as exact.

children.title: Nonrenewable Resources
children.top_down_role: Project-horizon resource budgets consumed by activities.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrenewable Resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Project-wide budget model for resources consumed by executing activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A resource \(k\) is nonrenewable when each executed activity consumes an amount \(q_{ik}\) from a project-wide capacity \(Q_k\), independently of when the activity is scheduled. If all activities in \(V\) must be executed, resource feasibility is \[\sum_{i\in V}q_{ik}\le Q_k.\] In a multimode project, the consumption depends on the selected mode and the condition becomes \(\sum_{i\in V}q_{im_i k}\le Q_k\). Unlike a renewable constraint, this inequality aggregates consumption over the entire project rather than over concurrent activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrenewable resource is consumed from one project-wide budget, so feasibility depends on total activity consumption rather than simultaneous use.
assumptions_latex: All required activities are executed once.
\(q_{ik}\ge 0\) and \(Q_k\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonrenewable feasibility is the project-wide budget inequality \(\sum_i q_{ik}\le Q_k\), with mode-indexed consumption when applicable.

notation.meaning: Total consumption by activity i of resource k.

review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports the nonrenewable-resource classification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The project-wide budget definition fits this resource-class leaf and is mathematically coherent under its stated execution assumption. No cited source or inspectable locator supports the classification or its single-mode and multimode forms.

children.title: Doubly Constrained Resources
children.top_down_role: Resources subject to both periodic capacity limits and horizon budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Doubly Constrained Resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource class subject simultaneously to renewable and project-wide consumption limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A resource \(r\) is doubly constrained when the same activity uses are restricted both by an instantaneous renewable capacity and by a cumulative project budget. With per-time demands \(a_{ir}\), activity durations \(p_i\), total consumptions \(q_{ir}\), starts \(S_i\), capacities \(B_r(t)\), and budget \(Q_r\), feasibility requires simultaneously \[\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}a_{ir}\le B_r(t)\quad\text{for every }t,\qquad \sum_i q_{ir}\le Q_r.\] Satisfying only one family of inequalities does not establish feasibility for a doubly constrained resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A doubly constrained resource must obey both a capacity limit at every time and a total project-wide consumption budget.
assumptions_latex: Activities have well-defined per-time demands and total consumptions.
All demands, consumptions, capacities, and budgets are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both the pointwise renewable inequalities and the cumulative budget inequality are necessary for feasibility.
review_flags: No supplied source locator specifically supports this definition of doubly constrained resources.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is the correct role, but the term "doubly constrained resource" requires a source confirming that the same resource is modeled through both the stated instantaneous and cumulative constraints and clarifying the relation between per-time demand and total consumption.

children.title: Continuous Resources
children.top_down_role: Divisible resource capacities within project-scheduling models.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuously available renewable capacity over a real-time project horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a continuous planning horizon \(H\subseteq\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\), a resource \(r\) is continuously available when a measurable capacity function \(B_r:H\to\mathbb R_{\ge 0}\) is defined throughout \(H\). For nonpreemptive activity intervals \([S_i,S_i+p_i)\) with constant demands \(a_{ir}\), a schedule respects this resource exactly when \[\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}a_{ir}\le B_r(t)\qquad\text{for every }t\in H.\] When capacity is constant, \(B_r(t)=B_r\), this reduces to the usual continuous-time renewable-resource constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous resource has capacity throughout a real-time horizon, and concurrent activity demand may never exceed its capacity function.
assumptions_latex: The planning horizon and activity intervals use continuous time.
The capacity function \(B_r\) is measurable and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is determined by a capacity inequality at every real time in the horizon.

notation.meaning: Resource capacity at real time t.

review_flags: The intended taxonomy sense of continuous resources is not fixed by the supplied locators.
A scheduling-specific source is required to distinguish continuous availability from continuously divisible resource quantities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is coherent as continuous-time renewable capacity, but "continuous resources" can instead refer to divisibility or continuously variable allocation. A scheduling-specific source is necessary to establish the exact local taxonomy sense before the record can be accepted.

children.title: Partially Renewable Resources
children.top_down_role: Resource budgets attached to selected subsets of time periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Renewable Resources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calendar-subset budget constraints generalizing renewable and nonrenewable resource accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a discrete horizon \(T\), a partially renewable resource \(r\) is specified by a subset \(W_r\subseteq T\) and capacity \(B_r\). If activity \(i\), when scheduled at \(S_i\), uses \(a_{ir}\) units in each execution period, its charged consumption is the use occurring during \(W_r\). Feasibility requires \[\sum_i a_{ir}\,\bigl|[S_i,S_i+p_i)\cap W_r\bigr|\le B_r.\] More generally, several pairs \((W_r,B_r)\) may impose several such calendar-subset budgets. Choosing singleton subsets yields periodwise limits, while choosing \(W_r=T\) yields a horizon-wide usage limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partially renewable resource limits total activity use charged only during specified subsets of calendar periods.
assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) is finite and discrete.
Activity demand is constant in every occupied period.
\(a_{ir}\ge 0\) and \(B_r\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resource is feasible precisely when every specified calendar-subset usage sum respects its capacity.

notation.meaning: Periods whose resource use is charged to constraint r.
Capacity assigned to the charged period subset.

review_flags: No supplied locator supports the specialized partially renewable resource definition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but this specialized calendar-subset formulation has no citation. A source must also confirm the limiting-case statements: a full-horizon charged-usage constraint is not identical to every conventional nonrenewable-resource model unless its consumption convention is suitably restricted.

children.title: Calendar-Subset Resource Availability
children.top_down_role: Availability structures linking resource limits to designated calendar periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Calendar-Subset Resource Availability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility condition for a resource usable only during designated calendar periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a discrete planning horizon and let \(A_r\subseteq T\) be the periods in which resource \(r\) is available, with capacity \(B_r(t)\) for \(t\in A_r\). For activities with demands \(a_{ir}\), occupied-period sets \(X_i\subseteq T\), and no alternative resource, calendar-subset feasibility is the conjunction \[X_i\subseteq A_r\quad\text{for every }i\text{ with }a_{ir}>0,\qquad \sum_{i:t\in X_i}a_{ir}\le B_r(t)\quad(t\in A_r).\] Equivalently, capacity may be extended by setting \(B_r(t)=0\) outside \(A_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities needing a resource may occupy only its available calendar periods, and concurrent demand must respect capacity in each such period.
assumptions_latex: The planning horizon \(T\) is finite and discrete.
Each occupied-period set \(X_i\) is determined by the schedule.
Demands and capacities are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule is calendar-feasible exactly when both subset inclusion and periodwise capacity conditions hold.

notation.meaning: Calendar periods when resource r is available.
Capacity of resource r in period t.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports calendar-subset resource availability constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate mathematical role for this feasibility leaf, and the two constraints agree with the plain statement. No cited source establishes this exact calendar-availability model, including the zero-capacity equivalence and the assumptions under which occupied-period inclusion is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Precedence Project Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Project models with lower or upper time lags between activity start and completion events.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A generalized-precedence project model associates activity \(i\) with start time \(S_i\) and completion time \(C_i=S_i+p_i\). Each temporal arc specifies events \(e_i\in\{S_i,C_i\}\), \(e_j\in\{S_j,C_j\}\), and possibly finite bounds \(\ell_{ij}\) and \(u_{ij}\). Feasibility requires \[\ell_{ij}\le e_j-e_i\le u_{ij}\] for every arc, omitting either inequality when its bound is absent. The four event pairs give start–start, start–completion, completion–start, and completion–completion precedence relations. Ordinary finish–start precedence is the special case \(S_j-C_i\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized precedence permits minimum or maximum time lags between any combination of activity start and completion events.
assumptions_latex: Activity durations \(p_i\) are fixed and nonnegative.
Every specified lag bound is a real number.
A feasible model contains no inconsistent system of difference constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Temporal feasibility is exactly satisfaction of all lower- and upper-lag inequalities between designated events.

notation.meaning: Minimum and maximum permitted event lags.

review_flags: The supplied general project-scheduling locator does not specifically support generalized precedence with all four event pairs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and event-lag representation fit generalized-precedence project models. The supplied inventory contains no cited locator supporting all four event-pair conventions, lower and upper lags, or the exact terminology used in the record.

children.title: Preemptive Project Models
children.top_down_role: Project models permitting activity interruption or segmented execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Preemptive Project Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Project scheduling in which an activity may be interrupted and resumed without losing completed work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a preemptive project model over horizon \(H\), activity \(i\) is assigned a measurable processing set \(X_i\subseteq H\) satisfying \(\mu(X_i)=p_i\), where \(\mu\) is elapsed time. The activity may have several disjoint processing intervals; completed processing is retained across interruptions. With renewable demands \(a_{ir}\), capacity feasibility requires \[\sum_{i:t\in X_i}a_{ir}\le B_r(t)\qquad(t\in H).\] Under finish–start precedence, \((i,j)\in E\) additionally requires \(\sup X_i\le\inf X_j\). The activity starts at \(\inf X_i\) and completes at \(\sup X_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A preemptive activity may execute in separated intervals whose total length equals its processing requirement, while precedence and concurrent resource capacities remain satisfied.
assumptions_latex: Preemption has zero setup or restart cost.
Processing completed before an interruption is retained.
Each processing set is nonempty and measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible preemptive schedule assigns processing sets of the required measure satisfying resource and precedence constraints.

notation.meaning: Set of times during which activity i is processed.
Required processing amount of activity i.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports the preemptive project-model convention.
A source is needed to confirm the intended precedence semantics under preemption.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate, but no source supports this measurable-processing-set model or its finish-start precedence semantics. Those semantics vary under preemption, and additional regularity may be needed to ensure the stated infimum and supremum represent attained execution endpoints.

children.title: Time-Window Project Models
children.top_down_role: Project models with activity-specific temporal availability windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Window Project Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonpreemptive project models with release, start-deadline, or completion-deadline restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A time-window project model assigns each nonpreemptive activity \(i\) a release time \(r_i\) and either a latest start \(\bar S_i\) or completion deadline \(d_i\). With duration \(p_i\) and start time \(S_i\), its window constraint is \[r_i\le S_i\le\bar S_i\] in the start-window convention, or \[r_i\le S_i\quad\text{and}\quad S_i+p_i\le d_i\] in the completion-window convention. These inequalities are imposed together with all precedence and resource constraints. A fixed start window is feasible for activity \(i\) only if \(r_i\le\bar S_i\); a release–deadline window additionally requires \(r_i+p_i\le d_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity must start no earlier than its release time and must satisfy a specified latest-start or completion deadline, alongside project constraints.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive.
Durations \(p_i\) are fixed and nonnegative.
All window endpoints are finite real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Time-window feasibility requires every activity’s start and completion to satisfy its chosen window convention.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports project time-window conventions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the separate latest-start and completion-deadline conventions are clearly distinguished. No citation with a specific locator supports these conventions as the intended project time-window model.

children.title: Preemption–Window Interaction
children.top_down_role: Feasibility effects arising when interruption permissions meet time windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Preemption–Window Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility condition for continuously preemptible activities with release dates, deadlines, and renewable-resource capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each activity \(i\), let \(X_i\subseteq[r_i,d_i]\) be its measurable execution set. A preemptive window schedule is feasible exactly when \(\lambda(X_i)=p_i\) for every \(i\), all prescribed precedence constraints hold, and \(\sum_{i:t\in X_i}a_{ik}\leq R_k\) for every renewable resource \(k\) and almost every time \(t\). In particular, feasibility requires \(p_i\leq d_i-r_i\); preemption permits splitting \(X_i\) but cannot compensate for insufficient window length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity must receive its full processing time inside its window while respecting precedence and resource capacities; preemption permits splitting but cannot overcome a window shorter than its processing time.
assumptions_latex: \(0\leq r_i<d_i<\infty\) and \(p_i>0\) for every activity \(i\).
Processing is continuously divisible, costless to interrupt, and resumes without loss.
Renewable capacities \(R_k\) and activity demands \(a_{ik}\) are constant during execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda(X_i)=p_i\), \(X_i\subseteq[r_i,d_i]\), and \(\sum_{i:t\in X_i}a_{ik}\leq R_k\) characterize resource-window feasibility.

notation.meaning: Set of times at which activity i executes
Lebesgue measure, representing allocated processing time
Demand of activity i and capacity of renewable resource k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no source supports the selected continuously preemptible model. The meaning of precedence for measurable, possibly interleaved execution sets is not defined, and the conclusion calls the listed resource-window conditions a characterization while omitting the prescribed precedence constraints.

children.title: Project Crashing Decisions
children.top_down_role: Activity-expediting choices used to shorten project duration.

knowledge_statements.title: Project Crashing Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete activity-mode formulation of project crashing under a completion deadline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an acyclic activity network, and let each activity \(i\) have modes \(m\in M_i\) with duration \(p_{im}\) and direct cost \(c_{im}\). Project crashing chooses one mode per activity and start times satisfying \(s_j\geq s_i+\sum_{m\in M_i}p_{im}x_{im}\) for every \((i,j)\in E\), \(\sum_{m\in M_i}x_{im}=1\), and project completion \(C_{\max}\leq D\). A minimum-cost crashing decision solves \[\min\ \sum_{i\in V}\sum_{m\in M_i}c_{im}x_{im}\] over these constraints, with \(x_{im}\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Crashing selects one duration-cost mode for every activity and schedules the project to meet a deadline at minimum direct cost.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.
Each mode set \(M_i\) is finite and nonempty.
Mode costs and durations are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal crashing decision minimizes \(\sum_{i,m}c_{im}x_{im}\) subject to precedence, mode-selection, and deadline constraints.

notation.meaning: Binary selection of mode m for activity i

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the crashing-decisions leaf, but the cited Lawler locator does not inspectably establish this finite discrete-mode formulation. The record also uses C_max without defining how it is derived from the activity completion times. An authoritative discrete time-cost tradeoff source and a complete completion-time definition are required.

children.title: Time–Cost Tradeoff Frontiers
children.top_down_role: Project-duration versus expediting-cost alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Time–Cost Tradeoff Frontiers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto representation of attainable project duration and direct cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be the set of feasible mode selections and schedules. For \(z\in\mathcal F\), write \(T(z)\) for project completion time and \(C(z)\) for direct cost. The attainable time-cost set is \(\mathcal A=\{(T(z),C(z)):z\in\mathcal F\}\). Its minimization frontier is \[\mathcal P=\{(T,C)\in\mathcal A:\nexists(T',C')\in\mathcal A\text{ with }T'\leq T,\ C'\leq C,\ (T',C')\neq(T,C)\}.\] Equivalently, each point of \(\mathcal P\) is nondominated: no feasible project is both no slower and no more costly, with one strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The time-cost frontier consists exactly of attainable duration-cost pairs that no feasible project improves in one criterion without worsening the other.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\neq\varnothing\).
Both project duration and direct cost are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is the set of nondominated elements of \(\mathcal A\) under the componentwise order.

notation.meaning: Set of attainable project duration-cost pairs
Completion time and direct cost of feasible decision z

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and its nondominance formula are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf. However, the cited project-scheduling section has not been shown to support the attainable-set and Pareto-frontier formulation, so the exact knowledge statement remains source-dependent.

children.title: Discrete Crashing Modes
children.top_down_role: Finite execution-mode choices for project compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Crashing Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite alternatives encoding activity duration and crashing cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A discrete crashing-mode specification assigns every activity \(i\) a finite nonempty set \(M_i\). Mode \(m\in M_i\) supplies a duration-cost pair \((p_{im},c_{im})\). Binary variables satisfy \(x_{im}\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\sum_{m\in M_i}x_{im}=1\), giving selected duration and cost \[p_i(x)=\sum_{m\in M_i}p_{im}x_{im},\qquad c_i(x)=\sum_{m\in M_i}c_{im}x_{im}.\] A mode \(m\) is dominated if another mode \(n\) has \(p_{in}\leq p_{im}\) and \(c_{in}\leq c_{im}\), with at least one strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each activity chooses exactly one finite duration-cost alternative; a mode is dominated when another is no slower and no more costly.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_i\) is finite and nonempty.
Durations satisfy \(p_{im}>0\), and costs \(c_{im}\) are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected pair is \((p_i(x),c_i(x))\), and dominated modes can be removed without losing a Pareto-efficient solution.

notation.meaning: Available crashing modes for activity i
Duration and direct cost of mode m

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite mode definition fits the terminal container, but the cited locator does not inspectably support discrete duration-cost alternatives or the dominance claim. The phrase 'without losing a Pareto-efficient solution' is also ambiguous between preserving every efficient solution and preserving existence of an efficient representative.

children.title: Project Cash-Flow Timing
children.top_down_role: Placement of project receipts and expenditures across the schedule.

knowledge_statements.title: Project Cash-Flow Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-time representation of schedule-dependent project cash flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) index project cash flows. Cash flow \(q\) has signed amount \(a_q\), is attached to activity \(i(q)\), has offset \(\delta_q\), and is triggered at either its start or completion. For schedule \(s\), its payment time is \[\tau_q(s)=s_{i(q)}+\delta_q\quad\text{or}\quad \tau_q(s)=s_{i(q)}+p_{i(q)}+\delta_q,\] according to the trigger convention. Thus a feasible schedule induces the dated cash-flow stream \(\{(\tau_q(s),a_q):q\in Q\}\); changing activity times changes economic value even when all amounts remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A schedule dates each signed cash flow at an activity start, completion, or specified offset, thereby determining the project's discounted cash-flow stream.
assumptions_latex: Activity durations and cash-flow trigger conventions are fixed.
Positive \(a_q\) denotes a receipt and negative \(a_q\) an expenditure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible schedule \(s\) induces dated payments \((\tau_q(s),a_q)\) for all \(q\in Q\).

notation.meaning: Signed amount of cash flow q
Offset from the selected activity event

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The event-time representation fits the cash-flow-timing leaf and is internally coherent, but start, completion, and offset trigger conventions are model choices requiring an authoritative project cash-flow scheduling source.

children.title: Net-Present-Value Objectives
children.top_down_role: Discounted-value criteria for project schedule selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Net-Present-Value Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-compounding objective for schedule-dependent signed project cash flows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For discount rate \(\rho\geq0\), dated cash flows \((\tau_q(s),a_q)\) induced by feasible schedule \(s\) have net present value \[\operatorname{NPV}_{\rho}(s)=\sum_{q\in Q}a_q e^{-\rho\tau_q(s)}.\] The net-present-value project-scheduling problem is \(\max_{s\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{NPV}_{\rho}(s)\), where \(\mathcal F\) contains exactly the schedules satisfying the project constraints. Because amounts are signed, delaying a receipt generally decreases its contribution, whereas delaying an expenditure makes its negative contribution less severe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Net present value discounts each signed cash flow by its scheduled payment time and selects a feasible schedule maximizing their discounted sum.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is finite and all payment times \(\tau_q(s)\) are finite.
The continuously compounded discount rate satisfies \(\rho\geq0\).
The feasible schedule set \(\mathcal F\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An NPV-optimal schedule belongs to \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{s\in\mathcal F}\sum_{q\in Q}a_qe^{-\rho\tau_q(s)}\).

notation.meaning: Net present value of schedule s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the NPV-objectives leaf and consistently states a continuous-compounding convention. No citation supports that convention or its use as the project-scheduling objective, so the exact formulation cannot yet be accepted.

children.title: Discount-Rate Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Schedule changes across alternative discounting regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Discount-Rate Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric behavior of finite-schedule net-present-value optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed feasible schedule \(s\), \(N_s(\rho)=\sum_{q\in Q}a_qe^{-\rho\tau_q(s)}\) is continuous and differentiable for \(\rho\geq0\), with \[N_s'(\rho)=-\sum_{q\in Q}a_q\tau_q(s)e^{-\rho\tau_q(s)}.\] If the feasible set \(\mathcal F\) is finite, the optimal value \(V(\rho)=\max_{s\in\mathcal F}N_s(\rho)\) is continuous and piecewise differentiable. At a rate where the maximizing schedule is unique locally, \(V'(\rho)=N_s'(\rho)\); nondifferentiability may occur when optimal schedules exchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed schedule's NPV has an explicit discount-rate derivative; the optimized value is continuous but can kink when the optimal schedule changes.
assumptions_latex: The cash-flow set \(Q\) and feasible schedule set \(\mathcal F\) are finite.
Amounts and payment times do not themselves depend on \(\rho\).
All payment times are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V\) is continuous and piecewise differentiable, with derivative \(-\sum_q a_q\tau_q(s)e^{-\rho\tau_q(s)}\) wherever one schedule remains locally optimal.

notation.meaning: NPV of fixed schedule s at discount rate rho
Optimal NPV as a function of the discount rate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the sensitivity leaf, and the fixed-schedule derivative is coherent. The stronger global assertion that a finite maximum of these exponential NPV functions is piecewise differentiable, including the intended meaning and extent of the pieces on the unbounded rate domain, requires an inspectable source.

children.title: Resource Leveling
children.top_down_role: Resource-profile adjustment under fixed or tightly controlled project timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource Leveling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic leveling of renewable-resource usage over a fixed discrete horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible schedule \(s\), let \(R_{kt}(s)=\sum_{i:s_i\leq t<s_i+p_i}a_{ik}\) be usage of renewable resource \(k\) in period \(t\in\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\). Given target levels \(\bar R_k\), resource leveling selects \(s\) to solve \[\min_{s\in\mathcal F_H}\sum_k w_k\sum_{t=0}^{H-1}\bigl(R_{kt}(s)-\bar R_k\bigr)^2,\] where \(\mathcal F_H\) enforces precedence, admissible start times, and completion by \(H\). The objective penalizes uneven utilization about the prescribed targets rather than merely total resource consumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource leveling schedules activities within a fixed horizon to minimize weighted squared deviations of period-by-period resource use from target levels.
assumptions_latex: Time is discretized into periods \(0,\ldots,H-1\).
Activities are nonpreemptive with integer start times and durations.
Weights satisfy \(w_k\\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A leveled schedule minimizes \(\sum_k w_k\sum_t(R_{kt}(s)-\bar R_k)^2\) over \(\mathcal F_H\).

notation.meaning: Usage of resource k in period t under schedule s
Target usage level for resource k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A quadratic target-deviation objective is a plausible resource-leveling variant and the definition role fits the leaf, but terminology and objectives vary and no source selects this version. The assumption string contains malformed TeX, written with a doubled command slash in w_k\\geq0, which must be repaired once the sourced formulation is established.

children.title: Resource Smoothing
children.top_down_role: Reduction of resource-usage variation within available schedule flexibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roughness minimization using schedule flexibility without extending a prescribed makespan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a prescribed project makespan and \(R_{kt}(s)\) the period usage of renewable resource \(k\). Resource smoothing chooses a precedence-feasible schedule completing by \(H\), commonly by moving activities within their admissible time intervals, to solve \[\min_{s\in\mathcal F_H}\sum_k w_k\sum_{t=1}^{H-1}\bigl(R_{kt}(s)-R_{k,t-1}(s)\bigr)^2.\] The fixed horizon prevents smoothness from being purchased by extending the project; optional capacity bounds may also be included in \(\mathcal F_H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource smoothing uses scheduling flexibility to reduce period-to-period changes in resource use without extending the prescribed project makespan.
assumptions_latex: Time and activity start times are discrete.
The admissible set \(\mathcal F_H\) is nonempty and fixes the completion horizon \(H\).
Weights satisfy \(w_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A smoothed schedule minimizes squared consecutive changes in \(R_{kt}(s)\) while remaining in \(\mathcal F_H\).

notation.meaning: Usage of resource k during period t
Feasible schedules that do not exceed H

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the smoothing leaf, but squared consecutive-load changes are only one possible smoothing criterion. Because the distinction between resource smoothing and leveling varies across sources, an authoritative locator is needed to support both this objective and the fixed-makespan convention.

children.title: Peak-Load Control
children.top_down_role: Schedule choices aimed at limiting maximum resource demand.

knowledge_statements.title: Peak-Load Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax or threshold control of renewable-resource usage over time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For schedule \(s\), define aggregate usage \(R_{kt}(s)\) for each renewable resource \(k\) and period \(t\). Peak-load minimization introduces \(P_k\) and solves \[\min_{s,P}\sum_k w_kP_k\quad\text{subject to}\quad R_{kt}(s)\leq P_k\ \text{for all }k,t,\quad s\in\mathcal F.\] Equivalently, threshold control fixes bounds \(B_k\) and requires \(R_{kt}(s)\leq B_k\) for every \(k,t\). The peak variables therefore equal \(P_k=\max_tR_{kt}(s)\) at any optimum with \(w_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peak-load control either minimizes the maximum period usage of each resource or requires every period's usage to remain below a prescribed threshold.
assumptions_latex: Resource usage \(R_{kt}(s)\) is defined on a finite discrete horizon.
The underlying feasible schedule set \(\mathcal F\) is nonempty.
Weights satisfy \(w_k>0\) for optimized peaks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At optimum, \(P_k=\max_tR_{kt}(s)\), while threshold feasibility is equivalent to \(\max_tR_{kt}(s)\leq B_k\).

notation.meaning: Peak usage of renewable resource k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimax and threshold formulations fit the peak-load-control leaf and are internally consistent under positive weights. No source supports grouping these two variants in this exact terminal statement, so source confirmation is required.

children.title: Resource Investment Decisions
children.top_down_role: Capacity-acquisition choices linked to project schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource Investment Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint choice of renewable capacities and a deadline-feasible project schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each renewable resource \(k\), let \(y_k\in Y_k\subseteq\mathbb Z_+\) be installed capacity and let \(C_k(y_k)\) be its investment cost. A resource-investment decision jointly chooses \(y\) and a schedule \(s\) satisfying precedence, completion by deadline \(D\), and \[R_{kt}(s)\leq y_k\qquad\text{for every resource }k\text{ and period }t.\] The basic resource-investment problem minimizes \(\sum_k C_k(y_k)\) over these decisions. Thus capacity is endogenous rather than supplied as fixed scheduling data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The model jointly selects resource capacities and a deadline-feasible schedule, minimizing the cost of capacities sufficient for every period's demand.
assumptions_latex: Each allowable capacity set \(Y_k\) is nonempty.
Investment costs \(C_k\) are specified on \(Y_k\).
At least one capacity-schedule pair meets deadline \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal pair minimizes \(\sum_kC_k(y_k)\) subject to \(R_{kt}(s)\leq y_k\) and completion by \(D\).

notation.meaning: Installed capacity of renewable resource k
Resource demand induced by schedule s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint capacity-schedule definition fits the resource-investment leaf, but integer installed capacities are a model-specific choice without support. The periods quantified by t are also not explicitly introduced. An authoritative resource-investment project-scheduling source is required before choosing the capacity domain and precise formulation.

children.title: Resource Availability Costs
children.top_down_role: Costs associated with providing resource capacity over time.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource Availability Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable cost representation for endogenous renewable-resource capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_k\) denote the available capacity of renewable resource \(k\). Its availability cost is a function \(C_k:Y_k\to\mathbb R_+\), usually nondecreasing, and total capacity cost is \[C(y)=\sum_k C_k(y_k).\] Common specifications include linear cost \(C_k(y_k)=c_ky_k\), fixed-charge cost \(C_k(y_k)=f_k\mathbf 1_{\{y_k>0\}}+c_ky_k\), and discrete incremental costs on finite \(Y_k\). Feasibility links this economic representation to scheduling through \(R_{kt}(s)\leq y_k\) for all \(k,t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource availability cost assigns a usually nondecreasing acquisition cost to each capacity level, summed across resources and linked to schedules by period demand bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each capacity domain \(Y_k\subseteq\mathbb R_+\) is specified.
Costs are separable across resources unless interaction terms are explicitly added.
Availability purchased as \(y_k\) applies throughout the modeled horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Total separable availability cost is \(C(y)=\sum_kC_k(y_k)\), with schedule feasibility requiring \(R_{kt}(s)\leq y_k\).

notation.meaning: Allowable capacity levels for resource k
Cost of making capacity y_k available
Capacity required by schedule s in period t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separable-cost representation fits the availability-cost leaf, but separability, monotonicity, fixed-charge structure, and horizon-wide availability are model-dependent conventions with no citation. Parameter conditions ensuring that the displayed examples map into nonnegative costs are also unstated.

children.title: Capacity–Schedule Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Interactions between purchased capacity and project completion performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity–Schedule Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto representation for renewable-resource capacity investment versus project makespan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^R\) be the admissible capacity vectors and let \(T(k)\) be the minimum makespan among schedules feasible under \(k\in K\). For a nondecreasing investment cost \(C:K\to\mathbb R_+\), the capacity–schedule tradeoff set is \[\mathcal P=\{(C(k),T(k)):k\in K,\ \nexists k'\in K\text{ with }C(k')\le C(k),\ T(k')\le T(k)\text{ and at least one strict inequality}\}.\] Equivalently, a budget \(B\) induces the value \(T^*(B)=\min\{T(k):k\in K,\ C(k)\le B\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tradeoff frontier contains capacity choices for which neither investment cost nor optimal makespan can be improved without worsening the other.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^R\) is nonempty and finite.
\(T(k)\) is defined by the underlying feasible project-scheduling model.
\(C\) is nondecreasing componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is the nondominated cost–makespan frontier, and \(T^*(B)\) is its budget-constrained value function.

notation.meaning: Minimum feasible makespan under capacity vector k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard bicriteria Pareto formulation of capacity-investment project scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto representation and content kind fit the capacity–schedule tradeoff leaf, but no inspectable source supports this specialized formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Resource Multiproject Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic multiproject scheduling with renewable capacities shared across projects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A shared-resource multiproject instance consists of projects \(p\in P\), disjoint activity sets \(V_p\), durations \(d_i\ge0\), precedence arcs \(E_p\), renewable-resource demands \(a_{ir}\ge0\), and common capacities \(K_r\). A schedule assigns starts \(s_i\ge0\) such that \(s_j\ge s_i+d_i\) for every \((i,j)\in E_p\), and \[\sum_{p\in P}\sum_{i\in V_p:\,s_i\le t<s_i+d_i}a_{ir}\le K_r\] for every resource \(r\) and time \(t\). An objective may minimize portfolio makespan, weighted completion, or another specified portfolio criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several projects are scheduled together, with each precedence network respected and every renewable-resource capacity enforced across all projects simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: Activities are nonpreemptive.
Durations and renewable-resource demands are deterministic.
Each precedence graph \((V_p,E_p)\) is acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible multiproject schedule satisfies every project precedence constraint and each portfolio-wide shared-capacity constraint.

notation.meaning: Activities and precedence arcs of project p.
Start time and duration of activity i.
Demand of activity i and shared capacity for resource r.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard deterministic shared-renewable-resource multiproject model

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits shared-resource multiproject scheduling, but it introduces neither the resource index set nor the time domain and supplies no supporting citation.

children.title: Project Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of projects for inclusion in a constrained portfolio.

knowledge_statements.title: Project Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary portfolio selection subject to budget, logical restrictions, and joint schedule feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a finite project set, let \(x_p\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection of project \(p\), and let \(\mathcal L\subseteq\{0,1\}^{P}\) encode the stated logical restrictions. Given values \(v_p\), nonnegative costs \(c_p\), and budget \(B\), define \(S(x)=\{p\in P:x_p=1\}\) and \[\mathcal X=\{x\in\mathcal L:c^\top x\le B,\ S(x)\text{ admits a feasible joint schedule}\}.\] Project selection solves \[\max\{v^\top x:x\in\mathcal X\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project selection chooses a maximum-value subset satisfying the budget and logical restrictions and admitting a feasible joint schedule.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is finite.
Each project \(p\in P\) has value \(v_p\) and selection cost \(c_p\ge0\).
\(B\ge0\), and schedulability is defined by the associated portfolio-scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal selection belongs to \(\arg\max\{v^\top x:x\in\mathcal X\}\).

notation.meaning: Indicator that project p is selected.
Value and selection cost of project p.
Family of selections satisfying the stated logical restrictions.
Feasible selections satisfying logical, budget, and schedulability requirements.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard binary project-portfolio selection formulation augmented by schedulability

children.title: Portfolio Timing
children.top_down_role: Temporal placement of selected projects across planning periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio Timing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Timing decisions for projects already admitted to a portfolio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a selected project set \(S\), portfolio timing assigns each project a release or launch time \(\tau_p\in T_p\), together with activity starts \(s_i\). If activity \(i\) belongs to project \(p\) and has project-relative release \(r_i\), then \(s_i\ge\tau_p+r_i\). The activity starts must also satisfy project precedences and portfolio-wide resource capacities. A timing vector \(\tau\) is feasible exactly when such activity starts exist; an optimal timing vector minimizes the specified portfolio objective over this feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Portfolio timing chooses project launch dates and compatible activity starts while respecting precedences, timing domains, and resources shared by the selected projects.
assumptions_latex: The selected project set \(S\) is fixed.
Each launch-time domain \(T_p\) is specified.
The underlying activity-scheduling constraints are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible portfolio timing is the projection of jointly feasible launch and activity-start decisions onto the launch-time vector \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: Admissible launch-time domain for project p.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard launch-time formulation for a fixed project portfolio

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and projection interpretation fit portfolio timing for a fixed selected set, but no inspectable source supports the particular launch-time formulation.

children.title: Selection–Timing Coupling
children.top_down_role: Portfolio structures in which composition choices affect feasible timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection–Timing Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear consistency conditions linking project admission and launch-period assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_p\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection and let \(y_{pt}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate launch of project \(p\) in period \(t\in T_p\). Exact selection–timing consistency is imposed by \[\sum_{t\in T_p}y_{pt}=x_p\qquad(p\in P).\] Hence an unselected project has no launch period and a selected project has exactly one. If \(s_i\) is the start of an activity \(i\) in project \(p\) with relative release \(r_i\), the additional link \(s_i\ge\sum_{t\in T_p}(t+r_i)y_{pt}\) activates its timing requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A project receives exactly one launch period precisely when selected, and its activity dates are linked to that chosen launch.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and every \(T_p\) are finite.
Selection and launch-assignment variables are binary.
Activity start variables use the same time scale as launch periods.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{t\in T_p}y_{pt}=x_p\) enforces exact logical coupling between selection and timing.

notation.meaning: Indicator that project p launches in period t.
Start time of an activity belonging to project p.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard binary activation and assignment coupling constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assignment equality correctly couples selection and launch timing. The activity-start inequality is only a partial activation formulation and requires a source specifying the surrounding model and treatment of unselected activities.

knowledge_statements.title: Serial Schedule Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activity-by-activity serial schedule-generation scheme for deterministic RCPSP instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an acyclic precedence network, durations, renewable demands and capacities, and a priority list \(\pi\). Initialize time-zero resource profiles and the scheduled set \(S=\varnothing\). Repeatedly choose the first activity \(i\) in \(\pi\) whose predecessors lie in \(S\); assign \(s_i\) to the earliest time not preceding their completion at which inserting \([s_i,s_i+d_i)\) preserves every capacity constraint; then set \(S\leftarrow S\cup\{i\}\). Stop when all activities are scheduled and output \((s_i)_i\), or report failure if no finite feasible insertion exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activities are selected one at a time by priority and placed at their earliest precedence- and resource-feasible start times.
assumptions_latex: The precedence graph is acyclic.
Activities are nonpreemptive with deterministic durations.
The priority list contains every activity exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever every insertion succeeds, the output schedule is precedence- and renewable-resource-feasible.

notation.meaning: Start time and duration of activity i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical serial schedule-generation scheme for the deterministic RCPSP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the canonical serial schedule-generation scheme and its terminal container, but no authoritative, inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Schedule Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-incremental parallel schedule-generation scheme for deterministic RCPSP instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an acyclic precedence network, deterministic durations and demands, renewable capacities, and a priority rule. Set \(t=0\), with no activity started. At each decision time, form the eligible set of unstarted activities whose predecessors have completed. In priority order, start at \(t\) every eligible activity whose demand fits the residual capacities, updating those capacities after each start. If activities remain and none can start, advance \(t\) to the next completion time. Stop after all activities complete and output their start times; report failure if unfinished activities remain but no completion or feasible start can occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each event time, the scheme starts as many eligible activities as residual resources permit, then advances to the next completion.
assumptions_latex: The precedence graph is acyclic.
Activities are nonpreemptive with deterministic durations.
Each individual activity demand does not exceed capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the procedure terminates normally, its output is a precedence- and renewable-resource-feasible schedule.

notation.meaning: Generated start time of activity i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical parallel schedule-generation scheme for the deterministic RCPSP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The event-time algorithm matches parallel schedule generation, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Project-Scheduling Branching Schemes
children.top_down_role: Decision partitions used to organize project-scheduling search trees.

knowledge_statements.title: Project-Scheduling Branching Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact branching by mutually exhaustive extensions of a partial project schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a partial schedule represented by a node \(N\), construct a finite branch set \(B(N)\) of admissible decisions, such as choosing the next eligible activity, fixing an ordering conflict, or assigning an activity start interval. Create one child \(N_b\) for each \(b\in B(N)\), adding the corresponding constraint and propagating precedence and resource implications. The branching rule is exact when the child completion sets satisfy \[\mathcal F(N)=\bigcup_{b\in B(N)}\mathcal F(N_b),\] where \(\mathcal F(N)\) denotes all complete feasible schedules extending \(N\). Terminal complete nodes yield candidate schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact branching rule partitions or covers all feasible completions of a partial schedule by finitely many constrained child nodes.
assumptions_latex: Each search node denotes a well-defined set of feasible schedule completions.
Every branch adds a valid scheduling decision or disjunction.
The branch set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coverage identity ensures that branching cannot discard a feasible completion before pruning is applied.

notation.meaning: Set of branch decisions at node N.
Complete feasible schedules extending node N.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic completeness condition for exact project-scheduling branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coverage identity is a sound generic exact-branching condition and the algorithm kind fits, but the record blends several branching variants without specialized source support.

children.title: Project-Scheduling Bounds
children.top_down_role: Bounds used to assess partial project schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Project-Scheduling Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node bounds for makespan-minimizing exact project-scheduling search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a makespan-minimization search node \(N\) with feasible-completion set \(\mathcal F(N)\) and node optimum \(z^*(N)=\min_{s\in\mathcal F(N)}C_{\max}(s)\). A valid lower bound \(L(N)\) and incumbent-derived upper bound \(U\) satisfy \[L(N)\le z^*(N)\le U\] whenever \(\mathcal F(N)\ne\varnothing\) and the incumbent is feasible. The length of every precedence path whose activities remain forced at \(N\), combined with fixed elapsed time where applicable, gives a lower bound; any complete feasible extension supplies an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node lower bound never exceeds its best feasible makespan, while any complete incumbent schedule supplies a valid upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The objective is makespan minimization.
\(N\) defines a set of feasible schedule completions.
The upper bound comes from a complete feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(N)\le z^*(N)\le U\), enabling safe comparison of unexplored nodes with the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Best makespan achievable below node N.
Makespan of the current feasible incumbent.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard minimization bounds and critical-path relaxation for project scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimization-bound inequalities and property kind fit the leaf. The critical-path lower-bound claim is only qualitative and lacks an inspectable supporting source.

children.title: Search-Tree Control
children.top_down_role: Node-selection and tree-management regimes for exact search.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Tree Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node selection, incumbent management, and termination in exact scheduling search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an open-node set \(Q\), incumbent value \(U\), and incumbent schedule \(\bar s\). Initialize \(Q\) with the root, \(U=+\infty\), and no incumbent. Repeatedly select a node \(N\in Q\) by a fixed policy; remove it, propagate constraints, and prune it if infeasible or if \(L(N)\ge U\). If \(N\) yields a feasible complete schedule of value below \(U\), update \((U,\bar s)\); otherwise branch and insert its children. Stop when \(Q=\varnothing\); output \(\bar s\), or declare infeasibility if none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search-tree control selects open nodes, applies bounds, updates the incumbent, inserts children, and terminates when no unexplored node remains.
assumptions_latex: Branching covers every feasible completion of its parent.
Every applied lower bound is valid.
The search tree is finite or the node policy eventually processes every retained node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(\bar s\) is globally optimal if it exists; otherwise the root problem is infeasible.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound at node N.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite branch-and-bound control logic specialized to project scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branch-and-bound control logic fits the leaf, but the alternative fairness assumption does not itself ensure finite termination; a source is needed to fix the precise convergence or termination conditions.

children.title: Project-Scheduling Pruning Certificates
children.top_down_role: Structural grounds for discarding search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Project-Scheduling Pruning Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally verifiable certificates for safely eliminating scheduling search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a makespan-minimization node \(N\), either of the following is a pruning certificate: an infeasibility witness proving \(\mathcal F(N)=\varnothing\), such as a propagated domain contradiction; or a valid lower-bound value \(L(N)\) together with a feasible incumbent schedule \(\bar s\) satisfying \[L(N)\ge C_{\max}(\bar s).\] The verifier checks the contradiction or the validity of the bound, verifies feasibility of \(\bar s\), and compares the two values. In the second case every completion of \(N\) is no better than the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node may be pruned after verifying either infeasibility or a lower bound no better than the feasible incumbent’s makespan.
assumptions_latex: The objective is makespan minimization.
The claimed lower bound is valid for every completion of \(N\).
The incumbent schedule is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certificate verifies that deleting node \(N\) cannot remove a schedule improving the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Feasible completions of search node N.
Certified lower bound for node N.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard infeasibility and bound-dominance certificates for branch-and-bound

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate and the dominance inequality is mathematically standard, but validity checking for the bound or infeasibility witness is not concretely specified or sourced.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Programming for Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Bellman recursion on a finite event-state representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct a finite directed state graph whose state \(q\) records sufficient scheduling information—completed activities, active activities with residual durations, current renewable-resource usage, and current event time—to determine feasible next events and future cost. Let \(q_0\) be the initial state and \(Q_F\) the terminal states. For every feasible transition \(q\to q'\), let \(c(q,q')\ge0\) be the elapsed time. Compute \[V(q)=\min_{q'\in\Gamma(q)}\{c(q,q')+V(q')\},\qquad V(q)=0\text{ for }q\in Q_F.\] Store minimizing successors and reconstruct a schedule from \(q_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic programming minimizes remaining elapsed time over a finite event-state graph and reconstructs an optimal feasible project schedule.
assumptions_latex: The state representation is finite and Markov-sufficient.
Transitions preserve precedence and renewable-resource feasibility.
Every complete feasible schedule corresponds to a path from \(q_0\) to \(Q_F\), and conversely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(q_0)\) equals the minimum makespan, and stored minimizing transitions reconstruct an optimal schedule.

notation.meaning: Initial state and set of terminal states.
Minimum remaining elapsed time from state q.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Bellman recursion on a finite exact event-state graph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits dynamic programming for project scheduling, but the generic state description does not establish an acyclic or otherwise well-founded recursion, and no specialized source fixes the exact state-transition model.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Programming for Project Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-programming formulation and complete search for a renewable-resource project-scheduling instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given activities \(V\), precedence arcs \(E\), durations \(p_i\), resource demands \(r_{ik}\), and capacities \(R_k\), introduce start variables \(S_i\) and interval variables \(I_i=[S_i,S_i+p_i)\). Post \(S_j\ge S_i+p_i\) for every \((i,j)\in E\), and post \(\operatorname{Cumulative}((I_i,r_{ik})_{i\in V},R_k)\) for each resource \(k\). Initialize domains using release dates and a valid horizon. Repeatedly propagate all constraints; if no contradiction and some domain is non-singleton, branch on a start, interval, or precedence decision. Maintain the best makespan \(U\), impose \(C_{\max}<U\), and stop when the search tree is exhausted. Return the incumbent schedule, which is optimal if one exists, or infeasibility otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model activities as intervals, propagate precedence and cumulative-resource constraints, and exhaustively branch while tightening the incumbent makespan bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite acyclic precedence graph.
\(p_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(r_{ik}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and \(R_k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
The branching scheme is exhaustive over every feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The returned incumbent minimizes }C_{\max}=\max_{i\in V}(S_i+p_i)\text{, or the instance is certified infeasible.}\)

notation.meaning: Start time and execution interval of activity i.
Capacity of resource k and activity i's demand for it.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the exact-method leaf, but the optimality and infeasibility guarantees require an authoritative constraint-programming source and a precise condition that the finite search horizon preserves every relevant feasible or optimal schedule.

children.title: Priority-Rule Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Priority-driven construction of project schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Priority-Rule Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serial schedule-generation heuristic for precedence-constrained renewable-resource project scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the set of unscheduled activities and let \(Q(A)\) contain activities whose predecessors have already been scheduled. Initialize an empty schedule. While \(A\ne\varnothing\), select \(i\in\arg\max_{j\in Q(A)}\pi_j\), using a fixed tie rule, and assign \(i\) the earliest start \(S_i\) satisfying all predecessor completion times and, throughout \([S_i,S_i+p_i)\), every renewable-resource capacity. Remove \(i\) from \(A\) and update \(Q(A)\). Stop after all activities are inserted and return the resulting schedule. For an acyclic precedence graph and finite capacities admitting the activities individually, the construction terminates with a precedence- and resource-feasible schedule, but it need not minimize makespan.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly choose the highest-priority eligible activity and place it at its earliest resource-feasible start; the resulting schedule is feasible but not necessarily optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is finite and acyclic.
\(0\le r_{ik}\le R_k\) for every activity \(i\) and resource \(k\).
\(\pi_i\in\mathbb R\) and the tie rule determine a selected eligible activity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_j\ge S_i+p_i\text{ for }(i,j)\in E\text{, and }\sum_{i:S_i\le t<S_i+p_i}r_{ik}\le R_k\text{ for every }k,t.\)

notation.meaning: Assigned start time of activity i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The serial priority-rule procedure and feasibility claim are mathematically plausible and fit the heuristic leaf, but no inspectable source supports the formulation or guarantee.

children.title: Sampling-Based Schedule Search
children.top_down_role: Randomized exploration of schedule-generation choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Based Schedule Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized schedule generation by sequential sampling from eligible activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a positive sampling weight \(w_i(q)\) for each activity \(i\) eligible in construction state \(q\). For replication \(m=1,\ldots,M\), start with an empty schedule. At state \(q\), draw an eligible activity with probability \(w_i(q)/\sum_{j\in Q(q)}w_j(q)\), place it at its earliest precedence- and resource-feasible start, and update \(q\); continue until every activity is scheduled. Evaluate the resulting makespan \(C^{(m)}_{\max}\). Return a sampled schedule attaining \(\min_{1\le m\le M}C^{(m)}_{\max}\). Every returned schedule is feasible under a serial schedule-generation scheme, while increasing \(M\) changes search coverage but supplies no finite-sample optimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample eligible activities according to positive weights, construct feasible schedules, and return the best of a prescribed number of samples.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
\(w_i(q)>0\) for every activity eligible in state \(q\).
Earliest insertion enforces every precedence and renewable-resource constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\max}^{\mathrm{out}}=\min_{1\le m\le M}C^{(m)}_{\max}\text{ and the output schedule is feasible.}\)

notation.meaning: Eligible activities in construction state q.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The randomized serial schedule-generation algorithm fits the leaf, but its formulation and finite-sample claims have no cited source.

children.title: Multistart Project Search
children.top_down_role: Repeated search from varied initial schedules or construction states.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistart Project Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent randomized restarts with incumbent selection for project scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a restart count \(M\), a randomized constructor \(H(\xi)\), and a feasibility-preserving improvement map \(L\). Initialize \(U=+\infty\) and no incumbent. For \(m=1,\ldots,M\), draw an independent seed \(\xi_m\), construct a feasible project schedule \(S^{(m)}=H(\xi_m)\), and compute \(\widehat S^{(m)}=L(S^{(m)})\). If \(C_{\max}(\widehat S^{(m)})<U\), replace the incumbent and set \(U=C_{\max}(\widehat S^{(m)})\). Stop after \(M\) restarts and return the incumbent. The output is feasible and no worse than any completed restart, but finite \(M\) alone does not certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run randomized construction and feasible improvement from multiple independent starts, retaining the schedule with the smallest observed makespan.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
\(H(\xi)\) returns a feasible schedule for every sampled seed.
\(L\) preserves feasibility and does not increase makespan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\max}(S^{\mathrm{out}})=\min_{1\le m\le M}C_{\max}(\widehat S^{(m)})\text{, with }S^{\mathrm{out}}\text{ feasible.}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and best-of-restarts conclusion fit multistart search, but the record supplies no source for the stated framework and guarantees.

children.title: Lagrangian Project Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Project-scheduling decompositions based on relaxed coupling constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Project Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian relaxation of coupling constraints in a minimization project-scheduling model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^*=\inf\{\sum_{h=1}^H f_h(x_h):x_h\in X_h,\ \sum_{h=1}^H A_hx_h\le b\}\). For multipliers \(\lambda\ge0\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=\sum_h f_h(x_h)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(\sum_hA_hx_h-b)\). Its dual function decomposes as \[g(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{h=1}^H\inf_{x_h\in X_h}\bigl(f_h(x_h)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_hx_h\bigr).\] The Lagrangian dual value is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}g(\lambda)\), and weak duality gives \(d^*\le z^*\). Thus any multiplier together with certified component infima yields a project lower bound; equality requires additional strong-duality conditions and is not automatic for discrete schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing shared constraints separates a project model into component subproblems; maximizing the sum of their Lagrangian infima gives a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(H<\infty\) and every \(X_h\) is nonempty.
The original problem is a minimization problem with coupling inequalities \(\sum_hA_hx_h\le b\).
Every component infimum defining \(g(\lambda)\) is finite for the multiplier under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda)\le d^*\le z^*\text{ for every admissible }\lambda\ge0.\)

notation.meaning: Decision vector and local feasible set of component h.
Nonnegative multiplier vector for coupling constraints.
