children.title: Constraint-Programming Timetabling
children.top_down_role: Covers domain-based search over linked timetable constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Programming Timetabling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-domain constraint model using event-period variables and global resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each event \(v\in V\), introduce a finite-domain variable \(t_v\in D_v\subseteq C\). For every conflict \(\{u,v\}\in E\), impose \(t_u\ne t_v\). Resource capacities may be expressed by requiring, for every period \(c\) and resource \(r\), \[\sum_{v:r\in R_v}[t_v=c]\le b_{rc}.\] A solution is a complete domain assignment satisfying all constraints; soft costs may be minimized over this solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-domain variables select periods, while disequalities and resource-capacity constraints enforce timetable feasibility.
assumptions_latex: All event domains \(D_v\) are finite.
\(b_{rc}\) is the available capacity of resource r in period c.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t_v)_{v\in V}\text{ is a solution}\iff\text{every stated finite-domain constraint holds}\).

notation.meaning: indicator of event v occupying period c

review_flags: No supplied locator covers finite-domain constraint-programming timetabling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the finite-domain timetabling model. The capacity expression also implicitly assumes that every listed event consumes one unit of resource capacity, which must be stated or replaced by explicit demands.

children.title: Integer–Constraint Hybridization
children.top_down_role: Covers coordinated use of integer optimization with constraint programming.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer–Constraint Hybridization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A logic-based decomposition coupling an integer master with a constraint-programming feasibility subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition decisions into integer master variables \(y\in Y\cap\mathbb{Z}^p\) and detailed timetable variables \(t\). Initialize a master relaxation. At iteration \(k\), solve it for \(y^k\), then invoke a constraint-programming subproblem deciding whether some \(t\) satisfies \(C(t;y^k)\). If feasible, return \((y^k,t^k)\) when its objective meets the stopping criterion. Otherwise obtain a valid exclusion \(B_k(y)\le0\), add it to the master, and repeat; report infeasibility if the master becomes infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer master proposes aggregate decisions; a constraint solver completes or rejects them, adding valid exclusions after rejection.
assumptions_latex: Every subproblem rejection yields a valid cut excluding \(y^k\).
The master integer domain is finite or another valid termination rule is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any returned pair \((y^k,t^k)\) satisfies both the master constraints and \(C(t^k;y^k)\).

notation.meaning: valid rejection cut from iteration k

review_flags: No supplied locator supports this logic-based integer–constraint hybrid scheme.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits a hybridization leaf, but the logic-based decomposition, validity and form of rejection cuts, stopping condition, and infeasibility conclusion require a specific methodological source.

children.title: Method Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers structural conditions favoring either exact method family or their hybrid.

knowledge_statements.title: Method Selection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural conditions distinguishing compact integer, propagation-oriented constraint, and decomposed hybrid regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a timetabling instance \(I\), define features \(m(I)\), \(g(I)\), and \(d(I)\) indicating respectively a compact linear encoding, strong finite-domain propagation, and a separable aggregate/detail structure. The selection rule is \[M(I)=\begin{cases}\mathrm{IP},&m(I)=1\text{ and }d(I)=0,\\\mathrm{CP},&g(I)=1\text{ and }m(I)=0,\\\mathrm{Hybrid},&d(I)=1,\\\mathrm{Undetermined},&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\] This is a regime classifier, not a claim that the selected method has uniformly smaller runtime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose IP for compact linear structure, CP for propagation-dominant structure, and a hybrid for separable aggregate and detailed decisions.
assumptions_latex: The feature predicates are fixed before solver selection.
The cases are evaluated in the displayed order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(I)\in\{\mathrm{IP},\mathrm{CP},\mathrm{Hybrid},\mathrm{Undetermined}\}\) is determined by the structural predicates.
review_flags: The regime predicates are an explicit formalization requiring empirical or methodological sourcing.
No universal dominance claim is intended.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate for a method-selection leaf, but the displayed classifier is an unsupported bespoke rule. Its feature predicates are described only informally, and no methodological or empirical source validates the case priorities or recommendations.

children.title: Neighborhood-Based Timetabling
children.top_down_role: Covers solution improvement through localized timetable changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighborhood-Based Timetabling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract single-solution neighborhood search for a finite timetabling space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite schedule space \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), neighborhood map \(N:X\rightrightarrows X\), initial schedule \(x_0\), acceptance predicate \(A_t(x,y)\), and stopping time \(T\), set \(x^{\star}=x_0\). For \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\), select \(y_t\in N(x_t)\); set \(x_{t+1}=y_t\) when \(A_t(x_t,y_t)\) holds and otherwise set \(x_{t+1}=x_t\). Whenever \(f(x_{t+1})<f(x^{\star})\), replace \(x^{\star}\) by \(x_{t+1}\). Return \(x^{\star}\), with feasibility enforced either by restricting \(X\) or by an explicitly specified penalty in \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iteratively propose neighboring timetables, apply an acceptance rule, retain the best encountered schedule, and stop under a specified budget or criterion.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
\(N(x)\neq\varnothing\) for every nonterminal \(x\in X\).
\(T\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^{\star}\in\{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_T\},\qquad f(x^{\star})=\min_{0\le t\le T}f(x_t).\]

notation.meaning: Schedules reachable by one neighborhood move from the current schedule.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no timetabling or neighborhood-search source supports this template. The loop also requires a neighbor at every iteration, while “nonterminal” schedules are not defined and no early-termination rule is given.

children.title: Population-Based Timetabling
children.top_down_role: Covers search over multiple candidate timetables.

knowledge_statements.title: Population-Based Timetabling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generational population search with variation, survivor selection, and incumbent retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite schedule space \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), population size \(\mu\), initial multiset \(P_0\in X^{\mu}\), variation kernel \(V_t\), survivor rule \(S_t\), and horizon \(T\), generate offspring \(Q_t\sim V_t(P_t)\) and set \(P_{t+1}=S_t(P_t\uplus Q_t)\in X^{\mu}\) for \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\). Maintain an incumbent \(x^{\star}\) minimizing \(f\) over every schedule evaluated through time \(T\). Variation may include parent selection, recombination, and mutation; feasibility must be preserved, repaired, or represented by an explicit penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evolve a population of timetables through selection and variation, form successive populations, and return the best schedule evaluated within the prescribed horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
\(\mu,T\in\mathbb N\) with \(\mu\ge1\).
\(S_t\) always returns exactly \(\mu\) schedules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(x^{\star})=\min\{f(x):x\in P_t\cup Q_t,\ 0\le t<T\text{, or }x\in P_T\}.\]
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits, but the population template has no supporting source. The incumbent conclusion uses an informal “or” inside set-builder notation and does not precisely define the complete set of evaluated schedules.

children.title: Memetic Timetabling
children.top_down_role: Covers population search enriched by local improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Memetic Timetabling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population search in which offspring undergo schedule-level local improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite schedule space with objective \(f\), population size \(\mu\), variation kernel \(V_t\), local-improvement map \(L_t:X\to X\), and survivor rule \(S_t\). Starting from \(P_0\in X^{\mu}\), generate \(Q_t\sim V_t(P_t)\), form \(\widehat Q_t=\{L_t(q):q\in Q_t\}\), and set \(P_{t+1}=S_t(P_t\uplus\widehat Q_t)\) for \(t<T\). Each \(L_t(q)\) is obtained by a finite neighborhood search initialized at \(q\). Return the best schedule evaluated by either the population process or its local searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate offspring with a population method, improve each selected offspring by local search, perform survivor selection, and return the best evaluated timetable.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
Each invocation of \(L_t\) terminates.
\(S_t\) returns a population of size \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f(x^{\star})=\min\{f(x):x\text{ is evaluated before termination}\}.\]

notation.meaning: Local-improvement procedure applied at generation t.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role and population-plus-local-search structure are plausible, but no source establishes that this is the intended memetic-timetabling formulation or supports applying local improvement to every offspring.

children.title: Population–Neighborhood Composition
children.top_down_role: Covers division of search roles between population exploration and neighborhood refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Population–Neighborhood Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator representation of population exploration composed with neighborhood refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_{\mu}(X)\) denote populations of \(\mu\) schedules. A population–neighborhood composition is an iteration operator \(C_t:\mathcal P_{\mu}(X)\to\mathcal P_{\mu}(X)\) admitting the factorization \(C_t=S_t\circ R_t\circ G_t\). Here \(G_t\) performs population-level selection and variation, \(R_t\) applies zero or more neighborhood transitions to designated generated schedules, and \(S_t\) selects \(\mu\) survivors. Thus \(P_{t+1}=C_t(P_t)\). The composition is sequential when every selected output of \(G_t\) is refined before \(S_t\), and partial when \(R_t\) acts only on a specified subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each hybrid generation as population exploration followed by optional neighborhood refinement and survivor selection, with the refined subset explicitly identified.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty schedule space.
\(G_t\), \(R_t\), and \(S_t\) have compatible domains and codomains.
\(S_t\) returns exactly \(\mu\) schedules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_{t+1}=(S_t\circ R_t\circ G_t)(P_t)\in\mathcal P_{\mu}(X).\]

children.title: Selection Hyper-Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Covers supervisory selection among lower-level timetable heuristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Hyper-Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online selection among predefined low-level timetable heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a schedule space \(X\), objective \(f\), finite heuristic portfolio \(H=\{h_1,\ldots,h_k\}\) with \(h_i:X\to X\), state features \(\phi_t\), selection policy \(\pi_t\), acceptance predicate \(A_t\), and horizon \(T\), initialize \(x_0\). At iteration \(t\), choose \(i_t=\pi_t(\phi_t)\), compute \(y_t=h_{i_t}(x_t)\), and accept \(x_{t+1}=y_t\) exactly when \(A_t(x_t,y_t)\) holds. Update \(\pi_t\) from the observed transition and reward, retain the best evaluated schedule, and return it at \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, use observed search features to select a predefined low-level heuristic, apply an acceptance rule, update selection information, and retain the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite and nonempty.
Every selected \(h_i\) terminates on \(X\).
\(T\in\mathbb N\) is finite.

notation.meaning: Features observable by the high-level controller.

children.title: Generation Hyper-Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Covers supervisory construction of lower-level timetable heuristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Generation Hyper-Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search over a parameterized or grammar-defined space of timetable heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be a heuristic-description space and \(D:\Theta\to X^X\) a decoder mapping each description to an executable timetable heuristic. Given training instances \(\mathcal I\), performance functional \(J:\Theta\to\mathbb R\), generator state \(z_0\), and horizon \(T\), produce \(\theta_t=G_t(z_t)\), evaluate \(J(\theta_t)\) by executing \(D(\theta_t)\) on the prescribed instances and budgets, and update \(z_{t+1}=U_t(z_t,\theta_t,J(\theta_t))\). Return a best evaluated description \(\theta^{\star}\) and its decoded heuristic \(D(\theta^{\star})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a formal space of heuristic descriptions, decode and evaluate generated heuristics on fixed timetable instances, update the generator, and return the best evaluated heuristic.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\neq\varnothing\) and \(D\) is defined on every evaluated description.
All evaluations use fixed instance and resource conventions.
\(T\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[J(\theta^{\star})=\min_{0\le t<T}J(\theta_t),\qquad D(\theta^{\star}):X\to X.\]

notation.meaning: Decoder from descriptions to executable heuristics.

children.title: Hybrid Timetabling Methods
children.top_down_role: Covers coordinated combinations of distinct timetable-solving approaches.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Timetabling Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal composition of distinct timetable-solving components with an explicit interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\\) be a timetable state space. A hybrid timetabling method is a solver whose transition operator \(H_t:X\to X\) combines at least two distinct component operators \(M_{1,t},M_{2,t}\) through a specified composition or controller. In a sequential hybrid, \(H_t=M_{2,t}\circ M_{1,t}\); in a controlled hybrid, \(H_t(x)=M_{c_t,t}(x)\), where \(c_t\) is selected from observable state or search history. A valid specification states the exchanged representation, invocation order, resource allocation, feasibility convention, and final incumbent rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid timetabling solver combines distinct optimization components through specified interfaces, invocation rules, budgets, feasibility handling, and a common incumbent convention.
assumptions_latex: All composed component domains and codomains are compatible.
Every invoked component has a finite assigned resource budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[H_t\in\{M_{2,t}\circ M_{1,t},\ x\mapsto M_{c_t,t}(x)\}\quad\text{under the declared integration rule}.\]

children.title: Adaptive Hybrid Control
children.top_down_role: Covers dynamic allocation of roles among components of a hybrid solver.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Hybrid Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online controller that reallocates effort among hybrid timetable components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given component operators \(M_1,\ldots,M_k\), controller state \(z_t\), observable features \(\phi(x_t,z_t)\), policy \(\pi_t\), reward \(r_t\), and total budget \(B\), initialize \((x_0,z_0)\). While budget remains, select \((i_t,b_t)=\pi_t(\phi(x_t,z_t))\), where \(b_t>0\) is the allocated component budget; compute \(y_t=M_{i_t}(x_t;b_t)\), apply the declared acceptance rule to obtain \(x_{t+1}\), observe \(r_t\), and update \(z_{t+1}=U(z_t,i_t,b_t,r_t)\). Stop before cumulative allocation exceeds \(B\) and return the best evaluated schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly select a hybrid component and its budget from current search features, execute it, observe performance, update controller state, and return the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(k\ge2\) and each component terminates within its allocated budget.
\(B<\infty\) and every allocation satisfies \(b_t>0\).
Features and rewards are observable after each invocation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sum_t b_t\le B,\qquad f(x^{\star})=\min\{f(x):x\text{ is evaluated by termination}\}.\]

children.title: Hybrid Integration Failures
children.top_down_role: Covers incompatibilities or duplicated search effort among combined components.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Integration Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigid composition can destroy progress even when each component succeeds alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b,c\}\) minimize \(f(a)=2\), \(f(b)=1\), and \(f(c)=0\). Define component maps by \(A(a)=b\), \(A(b)=c\), \(A(c)=c\), and \(B(a)=c\), \(B(b)=a\), \(B(c)=c\). Starting at \(a\), repeated use of \(A\) reaches \(c\) in two calls, while \(B\) reaches \(c\) in one call. Nevertheless, the rigid hybrid macro-step \(H=B\circ A\) satisfies \(H(a)=a\); hence \(H^t(a)=a\) for every \(t\ge1\). Component-wise success therefore does not imply success of their fixed composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two components can each reach the optimum alone while their rigid sequential composition returns to the initial state forever.
assumptions_latex: The state space and component maps are exactly as displayed.
The hybrid invokes \(A\) and then \(B\) without intermediate acceptance or adaptation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A^2(a)=c,\qquad B(a)=c,\qquad (B\circ A)^t(a)=a\ne c\quad(t\ge1).\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: self-contained finite counterexample; external attribution unnecessary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Competition Problem Formulations
children.top_down_role: Covers formal problem variants adopted by timetabling competitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Competition Problem Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical mathematical representation of a timetabling competition problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A competition problem formulation is a tuple \(\mathfrak F=(E,P,R,D,\mathcal X,\mathcal H,\mathcal S,f,\prec)\). The data sets describe events \(E\), periods \(P\), resources \(R\), and instance data \(D\); \(\mathcal X(D)\) is the candidate schedule space; \(\mathcal H(D)\) and \(\mathcal S(D)\) are hard- and soft-constraint index sets. Feasible schedules satisfy \(g_j(x;D)\le0\) for every \(j\in\mathcal H(D)\). The score \(f(x;D)\), together with comparison order \(\prec\), ranks feasible submissions. The formulation also fixes parsing, validation, and score-aggregation conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A competition formulation fixes the schedule variables, instance data, hard and soft constraints, feasibility test, scoring function, comparison order, and validation conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(E,P,R\) and every competition instance are finite.
Every hard-constraint predicate and score component is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F(D)=\{x\in\mathcal X(D):g_j(x;D)\le0\ \forall j\in\mathcal H(D)\},\qquad \min_{x\in F(D)} f(x;D).\]

notation.meaning: Set of feasible schedules for the instance.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite constraint-optimization representation of benchmark rules
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the leaf, but the proposed tuple is not tied to any identified competition specification. The soft-constraint index set is introduced without defining its score contribution, and the generic scalar minimization may not match official comparison rules.

children.title: Competition Instance Families
children.top_down_role: Covers grouped benchmark instances sharing origin or structural characteristics.

knowledge_statements.title: Competition Instance Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schema-consistent indexed collections of competition timetable instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a competition formulation \(\mathfrak F\) with admissible data schema \(\mathcal D_{\mathfrak F}\). A competition instance family is an indexed collection \(\mathcal I=\{D_{\alpha}:\alpha\in A\}\subseteq\mathcal D_{\mathfrak F}\) whose members share the same parsing rules, constraint semantics, and scoring convention. Family indices may encode dimensions such as numbers of events, periods, rooms, curricula, or availability restrictions. For every \(\alpha\in A\), the formulation determines a schedule space \(\mathcal X(D_{\alpha})\), feasible set \(F(D_{\alpha})\), and objective \(f(\cdot;D_{\alpha})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An instance family is an indexed set of benchmark data files sharing one formulation, schema, constraint semantics, and scoring rule while varying declared structural parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is a nonempty finite or countable index set.
Every \(D_{\alpha}\) satisfies the formulation's data schema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal D_{\mathfrak F},\qquad F(D_{\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal X(D_{\alpha})\quad\text{for every }\alpha\in A.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: schema-based definition of benchmark families
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the leaf, but no competition rules or benchmark documentation support the asserted family criterion, schema, indexing dimensions, or shared scoring semantics.

children.title: Formulation–Instance Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Covers which instance families support particular competition formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Formulation–Instance Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact compatibility between encoded instances and a competition formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be an instance file, \(\mathfrak F\) a formulation, \(Y_F(D)\) the formulation-feasible encoded solutions, \(F(D)\) the intended feasible timetables, \(q_D\) the encoded score, and \(\delta_D:Y_F(D)\to F(D)\) the official decoder. The pair \((\mathfrak F,D)\) is compatible exactly when \(D\) satisfies the declared schema, every referenced entity and parameter is well typed, \(\delta_D\) is total and surjective, and scoring is preserved: \(q_D(y)=f(\delta_D(y);D)\) for every \(y\in Y_F(D)\). Thus encoding introduces neither missing feasible timetables nor score distortion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility requires schema validity, well-typed data, complete decoding of feasible encodings, coverage of every intended feasible timetable, and exact preservation of official scores.
assumptions_latex: The formulation supplies decidable schema and feasibility predicates.
The decoder and both scoring functions are defined on their stated domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[D\in\mathcal D_{\mathfrak F},\qquad \delta_D(Y_F(D))=F(D),\qquad q_D=f(\cdot;D)\circ\delta_D\text{ on }Y_F(D).\]

notation.meaning: Feasible solutions in the formulation's encoding.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role, but the proposed exact criterion requires a source. Total surjective decoding and exact score equality are strong encoding-equivalence requirements that need not define ordinary formulation–instance compatibility.

children.title: Cross-Competition Comparability
children.top_down_role: Covers limits on comparisons across differing competition specifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Competition Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational comparability condition for results originating from distinct timetabling competitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let competitions \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) specify formulations \(F_1,F_2\), instance sets \(I_1,I_2\), scoring maps \(s_1,s_2\), and run protocols \(R_1,R_2\). Their results are cross-competition comparable on \(J\subseteq I_1\) when there are an instance correspondence \(\phi:J\to I_2\), feasibility-preserving solution maps \(\psi_i:X_{F_1}(i)\to X_{F_2}(\phi(i))\), and a common score \(q\) such that \(q(i,x)=s_1(i,x)=s_2(\phi(i),\psi_i(x))\) after explicitly declared normalization. Moreover, \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) must impose equivalent resource limits, termination rules, information access, and aggregation statistics on the compared runs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two competitions are comparable only when instances, feasible solutions, scores, resource limits, termination rules, and result aggregation admit an explicit semantics-preserving correspondence.
assumptions_latex: \(J\subseteq I_1\) is the declared comparison domain.
All score normalization and protocol transformations are fixed before examining algorithm rankings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compared scores and rankings have a common mathematical interpretation on \(J\).

notation.meaning: feasible solutions of formulation F on instance i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: operational benchmark comparability is defined by preserving instance semantics, feasibility, scoring, and experimental protocol
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the container, but the proposed correspondence and protocol-equivalence criteria are domain-specific and uncited; support is needed to determine whether one-way instance and solution maps suffice for cross-competition comparability.

children.title: Benchmark Bounds
children.top_down_role: Covers published lower or upper reference values for benchmark instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal–dual or relaxation-based bounds for a minimization benchmark instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization instance with feasible set \(X\), objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), and optimum \(z^*=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\), a benchmark-bound certificate is a pair \((L,U)\) satisfying \(L\le z^*\le U\). The upper bound is certified by a supplied feasible solution \(\bar x\in X\) with \(U=f(\bar x)\). The lower bound is certified by a verifiable relaxation, dual solution, or valid inequality argument whose value is \(L\). If \(L=U\), then \(\bar x\) is optimal; otherwise \(U-L\) and, when defined, \((U-L)/\max\{1,|U|\}\) are certified absolute and relative gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid lower bound and feasible-solution upper bound enclose the optimum; equality certifies optimality, while their difference certifies the remaining gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\) and \(z^*\) is finite.
Bounds use the same formulation, objective convention, and numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\le z^*\le U\), with optimality certified when \(L=U\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: primal feasible solutions and valid relaxations provide standard upper and lower bounds for minimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and primal–dual enclosure are mathematically sound, but no cited source supports the benchmark-certificate convention or the particular relative-gap normalization.

children.title: Best-Known Solution Records
children.top_down_role: Covers incumbent objective values reported for benchmark instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Known Solution Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Versioned incumbent records for fixed benchmark formulations and objective conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For benchmark instance \(i\) under formulation version \(v\), a best-known solution record is a tuple \(B=(i,v,x,z,h,t,\sigma)\), where \(x\in X_v(i)\), \(z=f_v(i,x)\), \(h\) identifies the submitted solution artifact, \(t\) is the validation timestamp, and \(\sigma\) records validation status. For a minimization benchmark, the current record must satisfy \(z=\min\{f_v(i,y):y\in\mathcal V_{i,v}\}\), where \(\mathcal V_{i,v}\) is the set of solutions validated by the registry by time \(t\). The designation is empirical and version-relative; it does not assert \(z=z^*\) unless an independent optimality certificate is attached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A best-known record is the lowest validated incumbent for a fixed instance and formulation version; it is not an optimality claim without a certificate.
assumptions_latex: Each accepted artifact is checked for feasibility and objective recomputation.
Records from different formulation versions are not pooled without an explicit equivalence map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) identifies the registry incumbent for \((i,v)\) at time \(t\), but alone does not certify optimality.

notation.meaning: validated solutions for instance i and version v
persistent identifier or digest of the solution artifact

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: benchmark incumbent registries distinguish validated best-known values from proven optima
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Computational Reporting Standards
children.top_down_role: Covers runtime, hardware, stopping, reproducibility, or result-summary disclosures.

knowledge_statements.title: Computational Reporting Standards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum reproducibility condition for computational timetabling benchmark reports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A computational benchmark report is reproducible only if each reported statistic is indexed by the formulation and instance versions, algorithm and parameter configuration, implementation version, hardware and software environment, random-seed policy, stopping rule, resource limits, feasibility and objective tolerances, and number of independent runs. For stochastic runs with observations \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\), the report must state the aggregation functional and uncertainty summary, such as \(\bar Y=n^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^nY_r\) together with a declared interval estimator. Time measurements must identify whether they are wall-clock time, CPU time, or another resource measure, and excluded or failed runs must remain accounted for.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reproducible reports identify models, instances, code, parameters, machines, seeds, limits, tolerances, repetitions, statistics, timing conventions, and failed runs.
assumptions_latex: All compared observations use a declared benchmark protocol.
Any preprocessing and external solver time are either included or separately reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every performance statistic has enough metadata to reconstruct its experimental meaning and sampling unit.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reproducible computational experiments require complete model, implementation, resource, randomness, and statistical metadata
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the reporting-standards leaf, but the claim that all listed items are required for reproducibility is a normative domain-specific standard needing an authoritative citation and locator.

children.title: Performance Claim Comparability
children.top_down_role: Covers conditions affecting fair comparison of reported computational results.

knowledge_statements.title: Performance Claim Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparability predicate for two algorithmic performance claims on timetabling benchmarks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let claims \(P_A\) and \(P_B\) concern algorithms \(A\) and \(B\). They are directly comparable only on a nonempty common instance set \(J\) when both use the same formulation version, feasibility test, objective ordering, preprocessing policy, information access, resource measure and budget, termination rule, and aggregation functional. For paired stochastic comparison, outcomes \(Y_{A,i,r}\) and \(Y_{B,i,r}\) must share declared instance and replication indices, and any inferential claim must specify its estimand, uncertainty procedure, and multiplicity policy. If a condition differs, comparability requires an explicit transformation proved to preserve the reported performance relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Performance claims are directly comparable only under aligned models, instances, metrics, budgets, stopping rules, preprocessing, randomness, and statistical summaries.
assumptions_latex: \(J\ne\varnothing\) is fixed independently of observed algorithm outcomes.
Missing, failed, and censored runs follow the same declared treatment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any asserted ordering between \(A\) and \(B\) refers to the same estimand and experimental protocol.

notation.meaning: outcome of algorithm A on instance i in replication r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fair computational comparison requires a common estimand and aligned experimental conditions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but the exhaustive comparability predicate and transformation requirement are methodological claims without cited support.

knowledge_statements.title: Institution-Specific Model Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of benchmark validity after institution-specific constraints or preferences alter the modeled problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reference formulation minimize \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let institution \(k\) minimize \(f_k(x)=f(x)+p_k(x)\) over \(X_k\subseteq X\). Institution-specific model drift occurs when \(X_k\ne X\) or the preference order induced by \(f_k\) on \(X_k\) differs from that induced by \(f\). Ranking transfer can then fail: for \(x,y\in X_k\), take \(f(x)=0\), \(f(y)=1\), \(p_k(x)=2\), and \(p_k(y)=0\). The reference model prefers \(x\), whereas institution \(k\) prefers \(y\). Consequently, benchmark superiority under \((X,f)\) need not imply deployment superiority under \((X_k,f_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Institutional constraints or penalties can change feasibility or reverse benchmark rankings, so performance on the reference model may not transfer to local deployment.
assumptions_latex: The reference and institutional objectives are minimized.
The timetables \(x\) and \(y\) in the ranking-reversal example belong to \(X_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An algorithm ranking under \((X,f)\) is not generally valid under \((X_k,f_k)\).

notation.meaning: institutional feasible set, added penalty, and resulting objective

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: changing feasibility or the objective order can invalidate optimization rankings

children.title: Demand Forecasting
children.top_down_role: Covers estimation of future service demand by time, location, or service class.

knowledge_statements.title: Demand Forecasting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic demand forecast supplying the personnel-planning pipeline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For planning periods \(T\), let \(D=(D_t)_{t\in T}\) be nonnegative random demand and let \(\mathcal H\) denote information available at the forecast origin. A demand forecast is represented by a conditional law \(P_{D\mid\mathcal H}\), or by scenarios \(\{(d^{(s)},p_s):s\in S\}\) with \(p_s\ge0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\). A point forecast is a declared functional of that law, such as \(\hat d_t=\mathbb E[D_t\mid\mathcal H]\) or a conditional quantile. The horizon, time aggregation, units, forecast origin, and conditioning information are part of the representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demand forecasting supplies a conditional distribution or weighted scenarios, with point forecasts defined as explicit functionals and with horizon, units, and information fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(D_t\ge0\) for every \(t\in T\).
Scenario weights form a probability distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The forecast specifies both anticipated demand and, when retained, its uncertainty over \(T\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: probabilistic forecasts are conditional laws commonly approximated by weighted scenarios
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probabilistic representation is coherent and fits demand forecasting, but no authoritative forecasting or personnel-planning source supports its use as the exact pipeline interface.

children.title: Workload Conversion
children.top_down_role: Covers translation of forecast demand into labor requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Workload Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of forecast demand into time- and skill-indexed labor requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\in\mathbb R_+^{T\times Q}\) contain demand by period and service class, and let \(w\in\mathbb R_+^{T\times K}\) contain required labor-hours by period and skill. A workload conversion is a declared map \(g:\mathbb R_+^{T\times Q}\to\mathbb R_+^{T\times K}\) with \(w=g(d)\). In a linear conversion, \(w_{tk}=\sum_{q\in Q}a_{tkq}d_{tq}+b_{tk}\), where coefficients encode service time, routing, productivity, and non-demand work. If staffing must be integral, headcount requirements may be derived as \(r_{tk}=\lceil w_{tk}/(\ell_t u_{tk})\rceil\), with period length \(\ell_t\) and usable productivity \(u_{tk}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workload conversion maps service demand to labor-hours by time and skill, then may translate those hours into integral staffing requirements.
assumptions_latex: Conversion coefficients and units are fixed for the planning horizon.
\(\ell_t>0\) and \(u_{tk}>0\) wherever headcount is computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The converted workload is \(w=g(d)\), with staffing requirement \(r\) when the stated headcount rule is applied.

notation.meaning: labor-hours of skill k induced by one unit of class-q demand

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: workload planning converts demand through service-time and productivity coefficients before staffing
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits workload conversion, but the linear coefficients and headcount formula require domain support; the headcount step may also overlap the separate Staffing-Level Determination container.

children.title: Forecast-Uncertainty Transfer
children.top_down_role: Covers propagation of demand uncertainty into workload estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Forecast-Uncertainty Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pushforward of forecast uncertainty through the demand-to-workload conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let uncertain demand \(D\) have conditional distribution \(P_D\), and let workload be \(W=g(D)\) for a measurable conversion map \(g\). Forecast uncertainty transfers to workload through the pushforward law \(P_W=g_{\#}P_D\), defined by \(P_W(B)=P_D(g^{-1}(B))\) for every measurable workload set \(B\). For a scenario forecast \(\{(d^{(s)},p_s)\}_{s\in S}\), the transferred representation is \(\{(g(d^{(s)}),p_s)\}_{s\in S}\), merging identical workload scenarios by summing their probabilities. Replacing this law by \(g(\mathbb E[D])\) generally discards variability and need not equal \(\mathbb E[g(D)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workload uncertainty is the pushforward of demand uncertainty through the conversion map; converting only mean demand generally loses uncertainty and may bias mean workload.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is measurable on the support of \(P_D\).
Scenario probabilities are preserved unless coincident outputs are merged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The workload distribution is \(P_W=g_{\#}P_D\), not generally a point mass at \(g(\mathbb E[D])\).

notation.meaning: pushforward of the demand distribution through g
random demand and induced random workload

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uncertainty under a measurable deterministic transformation is represented by a pushforward distribution
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pushforward representation is mathematically precise and the content kind fits, but no source with an inspectable locator supports its use for this demand-to-workload interface.

children.title: Demand–Workload Granularity Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Covers incompatible temporal or service aggregation across the two planning stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Demand–Workload Granularity Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information loss when demand is coarser than staffing-relevant workload periods or skills.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let fine-period demand be \(d=(d_1,d_2)\) and suppose only the aggregate \(D=d_1+d_2\) is forecast. The disaggregations \(d=(D,0)\) and \(d'=(D/2,D/2)\) have the same aggregate but different peak workloads under \(w_t=a d_t\): \(\max_t w_t=aD\) and \(\max_t w'_t=aD/2\). Hence any deterministic conversion \(h(D)\) using only aggregate demand returns the same staffing input for both profiles and cannot exactly represent both peak requirements. More generally, if aggregation \(A\) is noninjective and \(g(d)\ne g(d')\) for some \(Ad=Ad'\), no map \(h\) satisfies \(g=h\circ A\) on the full demand domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coarse demand totals cannot determine fine-period workload when different disaggregations share a total but create different peaks; exact conversion then requires added assumptions or data.
assumptions_latex: Staffing feasibility depends on fine-period workload rather than only total workload.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact workload recovery from aggregated demand is impossible whenever \(g\) is not constant on fibers of \(A\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a noninjective aggregation cannot support exact recovery of a quantity varying within its fibers
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure example and nonfactorization condition are mathematically correct and fit the leaf, but the record has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Staffing-Level Determination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization model selecting aggregate staffing capacity before individual rostering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let finite sets \(T\) and \(K\) index planning periods and skills. Let \(n_k\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the number of workers of skill \(k\), \(a_{tk}\ge0\) the deployable capacity per such worker in period \(t\), \(c_k\ge0\) the corresponding employment cost, and \(W_t\) the required workload. Staffing-level determination may be represented by \[\min_{n\in N}\left\{\sum_{k\in K}c_kn_k+\rho\!\left(\left(W_t-\sum_{k\in K}a_{tk}n_k\right)_+\right)_{t\in T}\right\},\] where \(N\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^K\) contains budget, skill-mix, and policy restrictions, \((z)_+=\max\{z,0\}\), and \(\rho\) is a declared shortage-risk functional. Deterministic coverage instead imposes \(\sum_{k\in K}a_{tk}n_k\ge W_t\) for every \(t\in T\); stochastic or robust variants derive \(\rho\) or their coverage constraints from the declared workload uncertainty model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Staffing-level determination chooses integer worker counts by skill to balance employment cost against deterministic, stochastic, or robust workload shortages before assigning individuals.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(K\) are finite.
\(N\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^K\) is nonempty, and all costs, capacities, and workloads use consistent units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any optimizer \(n^*\) is an aggregate staffing plan under the declared workload-risk criterion.

notation.meaning: number of workers with skill k
period-t capacity supplied per skill-k worker

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: aggregate staffing models choose integer skill counts against capacity requirements and shortage risk

children.title: Shift Design
children.top_down_role: Covers specification of shift start times, durations, or staffing profiles.

knowledge_statements.title: Shift Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-covering representation for constructing permitted shifts from fine time periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a finite set of atomic work periods and \(S\) a finite set of candidate shifts. Each shift \(s\in S\) has incidence \(a_{ts}\in\{0,1\}\) and cost \(c_s\ge0\), and satisfies the declared start-time, duration, break, rest, and skill rules. Given requirements \(r_t\ge0\) and shortage penalties \(p_t\ge0\), shift design selects multiplicities by solving \[\min_{y\in\mathbb Z_+^S,\,u\in\mathbb R_+^T}\left\{\sum_{s\in S}c_sy_s+\sum_{t\in T}p_tu_t:\sum_{s\in S}a_{ts}y_s+u_t\ge r_t\quad\text{for every }t\in T\right\}.\] Additional coupling constraints may restrict consecutive shifts or compatibility with days-off and leave patterns. The output is a shift portfolio and its induced coverage profile.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shift design selects valid shift types and integer multiplicities to cover period requirements while accounting for cost, shortages, breaks, rest, and leave-pattern compatibility.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and \(S\) are finite.
Every candidate shift in \(S\) already satisfies its internal labor-rule constraints.
\(c_s\ge0\), \(p_t\ge0\), and \(r_t\ge0\) for all applicable indices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \(y\) defines a labor-rule-feasible shift portfolio minimizing the declared shift costs and uncovered-requirement penalties.

notation.meaning: coverage of period t by one copy of shift s
penalty per unit of uncovered requirement in period t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: shift design is conventionally represented as integer covering over labor-rule-feasible shift patterns

children.title: Days-Off Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Covers placement of nonworking days across personnel schedules.

assumptions_latex: A finite cyclic planning horizon \(D=\{1,\ldots,T\}\) is given.
Each employee \(i\in E\) has admissible work/off sequences and required bounds \(L_i\leq \sum_{d\in D}x_{id}\leq U_i\).
Daily staffing requirements are \(r_d\in\mathbb Z_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible schedule satisfies \(\sum_{i\in E}x_{id}\geq r_d\) for every \(d\in D\), all employee workload bounds, and every admissibility rule encoded by \((x_{i1},\ldots,x_{iT})\in P_i\).

notation.meaning: Binary indicator that employee i works on day d
Set of employees and planning days
Admissible work/off patterns for employee i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon binary days-off model with staffing coverage and employee pattern rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A days-off scheduling instance seeks binary vectors \(x_i=(x_{id})_{d\in D}\) for employees \(i\in E\). The value \(x_{id}=1\) denotes work and \(x_{id}=0\) denotes a day off. A schedule is feasible precisely when \(x_i\in P_i\) for every \(i\in E\), \(L_i\leq\sum_{d\in D}x_{id}\leq U_i\) for every \(i\in E\), and \(\sum_{i\in E}x_{id}\geq r_d\) for every \(d\in D\). An optimization version minimizes a specified cost \(\sum_{i\in E}\sum_{d\in D}c_{id}x_{id}\) over this feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Days-off scheduling chooses each employee's work/off sequence so that individual pattern and workload rules hold while daily staffing demand is covered, optionally at minimum cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Days-Off Scheduling

children.title: Shift–Leave Pattern Coupling
children.top_down_role: Covers dependencies between shift structures and days-off patterns.

assumptions_latex: Finite sets of employees \(E\), shifts \(S\), and leave patterns \(P_i\) are given.
Parameter \(a_{ipd}\in\{0,1\}\) indicates availability of employee \(i\) on day \(d\) under leave pattern \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupling is enforced by \(x_{isd}\leq\sum_{p\in P_i}a_{ipd}y_{ip}\) for all \(i,s,d\), together with \(\sum_{p\in P_i}y_{ip}=1\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Availability induced by leave pattern p

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition linking selected leave patterns to daily shift assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Shift-leave pattern coupling requires each employee \(i\in E\) to select exactly one leave pattern, \(\sum_{p\in P_i}y_{ip}=1\), and permits a shift assignment only on a day made available by that selection. Thus, for every \(i\in E\), \(s\in S\), and day \(d\), the linking inequality is \(x_{isd}\leq\sum_{p\in P_i}a_{ipd}y_{ip}\). If at most one shift may be worked daily, the additional condition is \(\sum_{s\in S}x_{isd}\leq\sum_{p\in P_i}a_{ipd}y_{ip}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chosen leave pattern determines each employee's available days, and shift assignments are allowed only on those days.

children.title: Shift-Pattern Incompatibility
children.top_down_role: Covers conflicts between designed shifts and feasible leave sequences.

assumptions_latex: Each candidate pattern \(p\in P\) occupies a resource-time set \(R_p\).
Some pattern pairs may also violate an explicitly specified transition or contractual rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every incompatible pair \(\{p,q\}\in F\), feasible selection vectors satisfy \(z_p+z_q\leq1\).

notation.meaning: Binary selection indicator for pattern p
Resources and times occupied by pattern p

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-graph representation of mutually incompatible shift patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the incompatibility graph \(G=(P,F)\) by placing \(\{p,q\}\in F\) exactly when the two patterns cannot be jointly selected, for example because \(R_p\cap R_q\neq\varnothing\) on a capacity-one resource or because their conjunction violates a transition rule. A binary pattern selection \(z\in\{0,1\}^{P}\) respects pairwise incompatibility exactly when \(z_p+z_q\leq1\) for every \(\{p,q\}\in F\). Hence its selected support \(\{p\in P:z_p=1\}\) is a stable set of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate shift patterns form a conflict graph; feasible selections are stable sets containing no incompatible pair.

children.title: Line-of-Work Construction
children.top_down_role: Covers assembly of recurring work sequences across a planning horizon.

assumptions_latex: A finite set \(D\) of legal duties and a horizon of days \(H=\{1,\ldots,T\}\) are given.
Compatibility parameter \(c_{dq}\in\{0,1\}\) specifies whether duty \(q\) may follow duty \(d\).
A workline must obey prescribed workload and rest bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A line of work is feasible exactly when its daily duty sequence satisfies membership, connection, rest, and aggregate workload constraints.

notation.meaning: Set of legal duties and planning days
Duty assigned on day t, with 0 denoting off

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon construction of legal recurring or nonrecurring duty sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line of work is a sequence \(\ell=(\ell_t)_{t\in H}\in(D\cup\{0\})^T\), where \(0\) denotes an off day. It is feasible when every nonzero \(\ell_t\) is a legal duty, every consecutive nonzero pair satisfies \(c_{\ell_t,\ell_{t+1}}=1\), and the sequence satisfies all stated rest, consecutive-work, and workload bounds. In a cyclic workline, the wraparound pair \((\ell_T,\ell_1)\) must satisfy the same connection and rest conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Line-of-work construction assembles legal duties and off days into a sequence satisfying connection, rest, consecutive-work, and workload rules.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits line-of-work construction, but the asserted collection of connection, cyclic, rest, consecutive-work, and workload conditions lacks a cited domain source establishing the intended workline convention.

children.title: Duty Construction
children.top_down_role: Covers assembly of tasks or activities into feasible daily duties.

assumptions_latex: Atomic tasks \(J\) have fixed start and finish times \(s_j<f_j\).
Connection time \(\tau_{jk}\geq0\) and duty limits are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A duty is feasible when its ordered tasks are temporally connectable and its span, paid time, breaks, and task count obey all prescribed limits.

notation.meaning: Required connection time from task j to task k
Ordered task sequence defining a duty

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Duty as a temporally connected sequence of atomic tasks subject to labor limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A duty is an ordered sequence \(d=(j_1,\ldots,j_m)\) of distinct tasks from \(J\). It is temporally connected when \(f_{j_r}+\tau_{j_rj_{r+1}}\leq s_{j_{r+1}}\) for every \(r\in\{1,\ldots,m-1\}\). It is legal when, in addition, its elapsed span \(f_{j_m}-s_{j_1}\), paid duration, number and lengths of breaks, and number of constituent tasks satisfy their prescribed lower and upper bounds. Duty construction selects or generates such legal sequences to cover required tasks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duty construction chains fixed-time tasks into a temporally feasible sequence that also satisfies span, paid-time, break, and labor-rule limits.
knowledge_statements.title: Duty Construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duty definition is mathematically coherent and fits Duty Construction, but no source supports the domain-specific span, paid-time, break, and labor-rule characterization.

children.title: Duty-to-Workline Composition
children.top_down_role: Covers placement of constructed duties within longer work sequences.

assumptions_latex: A set \(D\) of legal duties and days \(H=\{1,\ldots,T\}\) are given.
Parameter \(c_{dq}\) records whether duty \(q\) may follow duty \(d\) with sufficient rest.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(u_{dt}+u_{q,t+1}\leq1\) for all \((d,q)\) with \(c_{dq}=0\) compose selected duties into a connection-feasible workline.

notation.meaning: Indicator that duty d occupies day t

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary linking formulation that composes daily duties into a feasible workline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_{dt}=1\) mean that duty \(d\in D\) is placed on day \(t\in H\). Daily composition requires \(\sum_{d\in D}u_{dt}\leq1\) for every \(t\). For each forbidden succession \((d,q)\) with \(c_{dq}=0\), impose \(u_{dt}+u_{q,t+1}\leq1\) for \(t<T\). Equivalently, the selected duty-day vertices form a path through a layered compatibility graph whose arcs join \((d,t)\) to \((q,t+1)\) exactly when \(c_{dq}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duty-to-workline composition chooses at most one duty per day and links consecutive choices only through permitted rest-compatible successions.
knowledge_statements.title: Duty-to-Workline Composition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary succession constraints fit the container, but they are not equivalent to selecting a path in the stated layered graph: at-most-one-duty constraints permit disconnected selections and skipped layers. A source and a corrected graph/formulation equivalence are required.

children.title: Duty Connection Failures
children.top_down_role: Covers temporal, spatial, or qualification conflicts between consecutive duty elements.

assumptions_latex: Duties \(d,q\) have end and start times \(e_d\) and \(s_q\) on consecutive days.
Required inter-duty rest is \(R_{dq}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A connection failure occurs exactly when \(s_q+24\mathrm h-e_d<R_{dq}\), or when an additional required connection resource is unavailable.

notation.meaning: End time of predecessor duty d
Start time of successor duty q

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp infeasibility condition for connecting duties on consecutive days.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For duties on consecutive calendar days, define available rest by \(\rho_{dq}=s_q+24\mathrm h-e_d\), using times measured from the start of their respective days. The succession \((d,q)\) has a rest-based connection failure exactly when \(\rho_{dq}<R_{dq}\). Even when \(\rho_{dq}\geq R_{dq}\), the connection fails if a required transfer, location, qualification, or other explicitly modeled linking resource is unavailable. Such a pair must be excluded from every feasible workline.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two consecutive duties cannot be linked when available overnight rest is below the required minimum or another mandatory connection resource is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.title: Duty Connection Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the node, but the 24-hour rest formula depends on a restrictive time convention and may not cover duties crossing day boundaries. No domain source establishes that convention or the additional connection resources.

children.title: Individual Roster Assignment
children.top_down_role: Covers allocation of roster patterns or shifts to named personnel.

assumptions_latex: Employees \(E\) and complete roster lines \(L\) are finite.
Eligibility parameter \(a_{i\ell}\in\{0,1\}\) and assignment cost \(c_{i\ell}\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible assignment satisfies \(\sum_{\ell\in L}x_{i\ell}=1\) for every \(i\), \(\sum_{i\in E}x_{i\ell}\leq1\) for every \(\ell\), and \(x_{i\ell}\leq a_{i\ell}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bipartite assignment formulation for allocating complete roster lines to employees.

source_refs.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Individual roster assignment is the binary optimization problem \(\min\sum_{i\in E}\sum_{\ell\in L}c_{i\ell}x_{i\ell}\) subject to \(\sum_{\ell\in L}x_{i\ell}=1\) for each employee \(i\), \(\sum_{i\in E}x_{i\ell}\leq1\) for each roster line \(\ell\), and \(x_{i\ell}\leq a_{i\ell}\). If every line must be filled, the line inequalities are replaced by equalities. Thus the model is a minimum-cost bipartite assignment restricted to eligible employee-line edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individual roster assignment matches employees to complete roster lines, respecting eligibility and one-to-one allocation while minimizing assignment cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Individual Roster Assignment

source_witnesses.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

children.title: Individual Task Assignment
children.top_down_role: Covers allocation of specific tasks, services, or duties to named personnel.

assumptions_latex: Employees \(E\) and tasks \(J\) are finite.
Eligibility \(a_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), task demand \(b_j\in\mathbb Z_+\), and employee capacity \(u_i\in\mathbb Z_+\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires \(\sum_i x_{ij}=b_j\), \(\sum_jx_{ij}\leq u_i\), and \(x_{ij}\leq a_{ij}\) for all applicable indices.

notation.meaning: Indicator that employee i receives task j
Required number of assignees for task j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacitated bipartite assignment of atomic tasks to eligible employees.

source_refs.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Individual task assignment chooses \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) for \(i\in E\) and \(j\in J\). Each task demand is met by \(\sum_{i\in E}x_{ij}=b_j\), each employee capacity is respected by \(\sum_{j\in J}x_{ij}\leq u_i\), and eligibility is imposed by \(x_{ij}\leq a_{ij}\). With costs \(c_{ij}\), the standard objective is \(\min\sum_{i\in E}\sum_{j\in J}c_{ij}x_{ij}\). Time-overlap constraints may further forbid simultaneous tasks assigned to one employee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individual task assignment allocates task demand among eligible employees while respecting capacity, overlap rules, and assignment costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Individual Task Assignment

source_witnesses.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited ordinary assignment section does not clearly support the stated multi-demand, capacitated variant. The plain statement also says overlap rules are respected although no overlap constraints are specified. A source for the capacitated formulation and an explicit overlap model are required.

children.title: Roster-to-Task Linking
children.top_down_role: Covers consistency between assigned work periods and task placements.

assumptions_latex: Roster availability \(r_{it}\in\{0,1\}\) and task activity \(h_{jt}\in\{0,1\}\) are given for periods \(t\in T\).
Qualification compatibility is \(q_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The link \(x_{ij}\leq q_{ij}\) and \(h_{jt}x_{ij}\leq r_{it}\) for every \(i,j,t\) ensures that task assignments respect qualifications and rostered availability.

notation.meaning: Employee i is rostered available in period t
Task j is active in period t

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linking constraints between rostered availability and employee-task assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Roster-to-task linking requires an assigned employee to be both qualified and rostered throughout the task. For every employee \(i\), task \(j\), and period \(t\), impose \(x_{ij}\leq q_{ij}\) and \(h_{jt}x_{ij}\leq r_{it}\). Because \(h_{jt}\) is fixed and binary, the latter is a linear linking inequality. If task \(j\) requires \(b_j\) employees, coverage is \(\sum_i x_{ij}=b_j\). These conditions prevent a feasible roster assignment and a feasible task assignment from being combined incompatibly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Roster-to-task linking permits an employee-task assignment only when the employee is qualified and rostered during every active task period.
knowledge_statements.title: Roster-to-Task Linking

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualification and availability linking inequalities are coherent and fit Roster-to-Task Linking, but no inspectable source supports this exact interface formulation.

children.title: Personnel–Task Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Covers assignment conflicts involving availability, qualification, or workload.

assumptions_latex: Assignment variables \(x_{ij}\) link employees \(i\in E\) to tasks \(j\in J\).
Qualification and roster availability are encoded by \(q_{ij}\) and \(r_{it}\), while task activity is \(h_{jt}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive value of \(m_{ij}=x_{ij}\bigl((1-q_{ij})+\sum_t h_{jt}(1-r_{it})\bigr)\) certifies a personnel-task mismatch.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable certificate of qualification or availability mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed assignment \(x\), define \(m_{ij}=x_{ij}\bigl((1-q_{ij})+\sum_{t\in T}h_{jt}(1-r_{it})\bigr)\). Then \(m_{ij}>0\) certifies that employee \(i\) is assigned to task \(j\) despite lacking its qualification or being unavailable during at least one active period. The certificate is verified by inspecting the fixed data \(q_{ij}\), \(h_{jt}\), and \(r_{it}\). An assignment is free of these personnel-task mismatches exactly when \(m_{ij}=0\) for every \((i,j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mismatch is certified when an assigned employee lacks the task qualification or is not rostered during an active task period.
knowledge_statements.title: Personnel–Task Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mismatch certificate fits the failure-oriented terminal container, but no source is supplied and the period set T used in the summation is not explicitly introduced in the assumptions or notation.

children.title: Rerostering Decisions
children.top_down_role: Covers revisions to published or provisional personnel rosters.

assumptions_latex: An incumbent roster \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^{E\times S\times D}\) and disrupted feasibility set \(F(\omega)\) are given.
Change penalties \(p_{isd}\geq0\) and operating costs \(c_{isd}\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A rerostering decision is an optimizer of operating cost plus weighted deviation from the incumbent roster over the disrupted feasible set.

notation.meaning: Feasible rosters under disruption scenario omega

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reactive roster optimization balancing feasibility, operating cost, and disruption to the incumbent plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given disruption scenario \(\omega\), rerostering chooses \(x\in F(\omega)\) by solving \[\min_{x\in F(\omega)}\ \sum_{i,s,d}c_{isd}x_{isd}+\lambda\sum_{i,s,d}p_{isd}|x_{isd}-\bar x_{isd}|,\] where \(\lambda\geq0\) controls roster stability. The feasible set incorporates updated employee availability, coverage, skills, rest, and labor constraints. The absolute deviations may be linearized with variables \(z_{isd}\geq x_{isd}-\bar x_{isd}\) and \(z_{isd}\geq\bar x_{isd}-x_{isd}\), replacing each absolute value by \(z_{isd}\) in the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rerostering selects a disruption-feasible replacement roster while trading operating cost against weighted changes from the incumbent roster.
knowledge_statements.title: Rerostering Decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization representation fits Rerostering Decisions, but no domain source supports the selected deviation objective and disrupted-feasibility interpretation. The employee, shift, and day index sets used in the sums should also be explicitly introduced.

children.title: Disruption Recovery Objectives
children.top_down_role: Covers restoration of coverage, feasibility, service, or operational continuity.

assumptions_latex: A baseline roster \(x^0\) and a disruption scenario \(\omega\) are fixed.
The recovered roster must belong to a nonempty feasible set \(F(\omega)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F(\omega)}\bigl(C_{\mathrm{op}}(x,\omega),D(x,x^0),C_{\mathrm{fair}}(x)\bigr)\] under the declared lexicographic or Pareto ordering.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines recovery through feasibility, operating performance, baseline disruption, and fairness objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a baseline roster \(x^0\), disruption \(\omega\), and feasible recovery set \(F(\omega)\), a disruption-recovery objective is an ordered criterion built from operational loss \(C_{\mathrm{op}}(x,\omega)\), roster deviation \(D(x,x^0)\), and optionally fairness cost \(C_{\mathrm{fair}}(x)\). A recovered roster is optimal when it minimizes this vector under a specified lexicographic order, or is nondominated when no feasible roster weakly improves every component and strictly improves one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery objectives compare feasible replacement rosters by operational loss, deviation from the original roster, and possibly fairness, using a declared lexicographic or Pareto rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Disruption Recovery Objectives

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but no cited source supports the selected objective components or the treatment of lexicographic and Pareto optimization. The displayed vector argmin is meaningful only after its ordering is formally fixed.

children.title: Disruption Severity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers recovery contexts ranging from isolated absences to widespread operational failures.

assumptions_latex: A disruption descriptor \(\omega\) and baseline roster \(x^0\) are fixed.
Recovery cost and roster distance are normalized nonnegative functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\rho(\omega)\in I_k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\omega\text{ belongs to severity regime }k.\]

notation.meaning: Disjoint severity intervals covering the index range.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an application-declared severity index; regime thresholds are not universal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(\omega)\) be the recovered-roster feasible set and define \(\rho(\omega)=\inf_{x\in F(\omega)}\{\alpha C_{\mathrm{op}}(x,\omega)+\beta D(x,x^0)\}\), with \(\alpha,\beta\geq0\); set \(\rho(\omega)=+\infty\) if \(F(\omega)=\varnothing\). For declared disjoint intervals \(I_1,\ldots,I_K\) covering \([0,+\infty]\), disruption \(\omega\) is in severity regime \(k\) exactly when \(\rho(\omega)\in I_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disruption regime is determined by where its minimum normalized recovery burden, or infeasibility, falls within application-defined severity intervals.
knowledge_statements.title: Disruption Severity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed recovery-burden index and interval classification are application-defined rather than a standard disruption-severity taxonomy. An authoritative source is required to establish that this construction represents the intended leaf and to specify normalization, weights, and the extended-real interval partition.

children.title: Roster Stability Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Covers tension between operational recovery and preservation of original assignments.

assumptions_latex: The feasible recovery set \(F(\omega)\) is nonempty.
Operational cost and baseline deviation are real-valued on \(F(\omega)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x^*\text{ is efficient}\iff\nexists y\in F(\omega): C(y)\leq C(x^*),\ D(y,x^0)\leq D(x^*,x^0),\text{ with one strict}.\]

notation.meaning: Operational cost of a recovered roster.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the bicriteria Pareto boundary between recovery performance and roster stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible recovered roster \(x^*\in F(\omega)\) is stability-efficient if no \(y\in F(\omega)\) satisfies both \(C(y)\leq C(x^*)\) and \(D(y,x^0)\leq D(x^*,x^0)\), with at least one strict inequality. Consequently, improving operational cost beyond an efficient point requires increased baseline deviation, unless another efficient roster has the same value of one criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered roster is stability-efficient when no feasible alternative improves operating cost and baseline similarity simultaneously, with at least one strict improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Roster Stability Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto-efficiency condition is mathematically recognizable and the property kind fits, but no source supports its use as the roster-stability tradeoff for this context. The additional consequence also needs careful source-backed qualification.

children.title: Interprofessional Coverage Coordination

assumptions_latex: Role-period demands and worker-role competency indicators are fixed.
A worker cannot perform simultaneous incompatible assignments.

Assignment of worker \(i\) to role \(r\) in period \(t\).

assumptions_latex: Each worker has a primary role and a declared set of substitutable roles.

Mode-independent structure lies in coverage, assignment, and sequencing; mode-specific legality is encoded through \(D_m\) and the additional constraint set \(X_m\).

children.title: Mode-Specific Duty Limits

knowledge_statements.title: Mode-Specific Duty Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate defining legal duties under transport-mode-dependent resource limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a transport mode \(m\), let \(K_m\) index regulated duty resources. A duty \(d\) is mode-legitimate if and only if \(g_{mk}(d)\le L_{mk}\) for every \(k\in K_m\), and every required categorical rule \(h_{m\ell}(d)=1\) holds. Resources may include elapsed duty time, driving time, work between breaks, night work, and consecutive work; categorical rules may govern relief locations, route knowledge, or traction and vehicle qualifications. Thus the feasible-duty set is \(D_m=\{d:g_{mk}(d)\le L_{mk}\ \forall k,\ h_{m\ell}(d)=1\ \forall \ell\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A duty is legal for a transport mode exactly when it satisfies every applicable numerical limit and categorical operating rule.
assumptions_latex: All applicable rules for mode \(m\) are represented by the indexed predicates.
Resource measurements and limits use consistent units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in D_m\) if and only if every mode-specific duty predicate is satisfied.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Sector Roster Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for transferring a feasible roster between service-workforce sectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a sectoral roster model by \((E,T,Q,P,A,d,X)\), with feasible set \(F=\{x\in X:Ax\ge d\}\). A roster transfers exactly from source sector \(1\) to target sector \(2\) under maps \(\phi_E,\phi_T,\phi_Q,\phi_P\) when the induced variable map \(\Phi\) preserves pattern admissibility and incidence, and satisfies \(x\in X_1\Rightarrow\Phi(x)\in X_2\) together with \(A_1x\ge d_1\Rightarrow A_2\Phi(x)\ge d_2\). Thus every source-feasible roster maps to a target-feasible roster.

assumptions_latex: Both sector models use finite pattern-based representations.
