review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility-preserving mappings formalize exact model transfer
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-transfer notion and its terminology require a source. The listed implications establish a sufficient feasibility-preserving map, but the statement does not justify the claimed exact or necessary characterization.

children.title: Workforce Coverage Requirements
children.top_down_role: Covers required staffing quantities by period, location, or service.

knowledge_statements.title: Workforce Coverage Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum headcount coverage condition over demand intervals or activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be employees and \(J\) coverage requirements. Let \(x_{ej}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that employee \(e\) supplies coverage to requirement \(j\), and let \(d_j\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be its minimum staffing level. The workforce coverage requirement is satisfied if and only if \(\sum_{e\in E}x_{ej}\ge d_j\) for every \(j\in J\). If overstaffing is forbidden, replace the inequality by equality; if understaffing is penalized, introduce \(u_j\ge0\) and require \(\sum_e x_{ej}+u_j\ge d_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every demand item must receive at least its required number of assigned employees, with optional shortfall variables when understaffing is allowed.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(J\) are finite.
Each assignment contributes one unit of undifferentiated coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage is feasible exactly when all indexed lower bounds are met.

notation.meaning: Binary contribution of employee e to requirement j.
Minimum workforce required for item j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indexed lower-bound constraints are the canonical workforce coverage formulation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No specific source locator is supplied. The hard coverage condition is standard, but the shortfall variant is incomplete without an objective or bound that penalizes or limits u_j; otherwise the relaxed constraint is always satisfiable by increasing u_j.

children.title: Skill-Mix Requirements
children.top_down_role: Covers required composition of qualifications within staffed periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Skill-Mix Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous lower bounds on total staffing and designated skill categories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be employees, \(J\) demand items, and \(S\) skill categories. For each \((j,s)\), let \(q_{es}=1\) when employee \(e\) possesses skill \(s\), and let \(r_{js}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be the required count. An assignment \(x\) satisfies the skill mix if and only if \(\sum_{e\in E}q_{es}x_{ej}\ge r_{js}\) for every \((j,s)\), together with \(\sum_{e\in E}x_{ej}\ge d_j\) for every \(j\). Overlapping skills may count simultaneously unless the model includes explicit allocation variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each demand item must have enough total workers and enough assigned workers in every required skill category.
assumptions_latex: Employee qualifications are fixed binary data.
Simultaneous counting of multiple skills is permitted unless separately restricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All total-staff and skill-category lower bounds hold.

notation.meaning: Indicator that employee e has skill s.
Required number of skill-s employees for item j.
Binary assignment of employee e to item j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: skill-mix constraints are qualified cardinality lower bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source with an inspectable locator is supplied. The statement does not define x_{ej} as binary or introduce and domain d_j, so all variables and parameters are not locally specified.

children.title: Skill-Qualified Coverage
children.top_down_role: Covers simultaneous satisfaction of staffing volume and qualification composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Skill-Qualified Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage condition with explicit allocation of qualified workers to demanded skills.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_{ejs}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that employee \(e\), assigned to demand item \(j\), is allocated to skill \(s\). Skill-qualified coverage holds if \(y_{ejs}\le x_{ej}\) and \(y_{ejs}\le q_{es}\) for all \((e,j,s)\), \(\sum_{e\in E}y_{ejs}\ge r_{js}\) for all \((j,s)\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}y_{ejs}\le1\) for every \((e,j)\) when one employee may fill at most one simultaneous skill requirement. The final inequality is omitted when simultaneous multi-skill credit is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage is skill-qualified when only assigned, qualified employees count and each worker obeys the chosen simultaneous-skill counting convention.
assumptions_latex: Qualifications \(q_{es}\) are fixed binary data.
Skill demands \(r_{js}\) are nonnegative integers.
The simultaneous-credit convention is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every skill demand is covered by admissible allocations of assigned qualified employees.

notation.meaning: Allocation of employee e to skill s for demand item j.
Assignment of employee e to demand item j.
Qualification indicator for employee e and skill s.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: allocation variables prevent unqualified or impermissibly duplicated skill coverage
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source with an inspectable locator is supplied. The sets E, J, and S and the domains of x_{ej}, q_{es}, and r_{js} are not introduced in the statement, so the condition is not self-contained.

children.title: Coverage Substitution Shortfalls
children.top_down_role: Covers nominally sufficient staffing that fails due to incompatible skills.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Substitution Shortfalls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear shortfall accounting when one supplied skill may substitute partially for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\), \(T\), and \(K\) be finite sets of employees, periods, and skill classes. Let \(x_{ejt}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that employee \(e\) supplies skill \(j\) in period \(t\), and let \(a_{ejk}\ge 0\) be the amount of class-\(k\) coverage credited from that assignment. For demand \(d_{kt}\ge 0\), the substitution shortfall is a variable \(u_{kt}\ge 0\) satisfying \[u_{kt}\ge d_{kt}-\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{j\in K}a_{ejk}x_{ejt}\qquad(k\in K,\ t\in T).\] If shortfall is minimized with a positive coefficient, then equality holds at optimality unless another constraint requires excess \(u_{kt}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shortfall equals the uncovered portion of each skill-period demand after crediting direct and permitted substitute coverage.
assumptions_latex: \(E,T,K\) are finite.
\(a_{ejk}\ge 0\) encodes permitted substitution credit.
Shortfall has a positive minimization penalty when equality is desired.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_{kt}\ge \max\{0,d_{kt}-\sum_{e,j}a_{ejk}x_{ejt}\}\) for every \((k,t)\).

notation.meaning: class-k credit from employee e supplying class j
uncovered class-k demand in period t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no inspectable rostering source supports the substitution-credit convention. The plain statement asserts equality whereas the formulation only imposes a lower bound unless the stated objective condition applies.

children.title: Minimum Rest Constraints
children.top_down_role: Covers required nonworking intervals between duties or shifts.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum Rest Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise elapsed-time constraint between chronologically consecutive assignments of one employee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite set of shifts with start times \(s_i\) and end times \(f_i\), and let \(x_{ei}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of employee \(e\) to shift \(i\). For every ordered pair \((i,j)\) with \(f_i\le s_j\) and no assigned shift of \(e\) strictly between them, minimum rest \(R_e\ge0\) requires \[x_{ei}=x_{ej}=1\ \Longrightarrow\ s_j-f_i\ge R_e.\] An equivalent big-\(M\) constraint for each candidate consecutive pair is \(s_j-f_i\ge R_e-M(2-x_{ei}-x_{ej})\), with \(M\) large enough to deactivate the inequality otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An employee must receive at least the prescribed elapsed rest time between consecutive assigned shifts.
assumptions_latex: Shift start and end times are fixed.
\(R_e\ge0\) is specified for each employee.
Candidate pairs are ordered chronologically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every consecutive assigned pair \((i,j)\) for employee \(e\) satisfies \(s_j-f_i\ge R_e\).

notation.meaning: start and end times of shift i
minimum required rest for employee e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but the endogenous notion of consecutive assigned shifts is not captured by a clearly defined fixed set of candidate pairs. A domain source and validated formulation are required.

children.title: Recovery-Time Requirements
children.top_down_role: Covers extended recuperation following demanding work sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery-Time Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent recovery after a designated workload or fatigue-triggering work block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For employee \(e\), let \(B_e\) be the set of designated work blocks. A block \(b\in B_e\) ends at time \(f_b\), has recovery class \(c(b)\), and requires uninterrupted recovery duration \(Q_{e,c(b)}\ge0\). If \(j\) is the first shift assigned to \(e\) after \(b\), with start time \(s_j\), feasibility requires \[s_j-f_b\ge Q_{e,c(b)}.\] Equivalently, no shift whose start lies in \([f_b,f_b+Q_{e,c(b)})\) may be assigned to \(e\). The recovery duration may depend on the preceding block's length, intensity, shift types, or accumulated fatigue class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a triggering work block, the employee cannot begin another shift until the block-specific recovery duration has elapsed.
assumptions_latex: Each triggering block has a well-defined end time and recovery class.
Recovery must be uninterrupted.
Required durations \(Q_{e,c}\) are exogenous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next assigned start satisfies \(s_j\ge f_b+Q_{e,c(b)}\).

notation.meaning: triggering work blocks for employee e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition matches the leaf, but triggering blocks, recovery classes, and uninterrupted-recovery semantics are model-dependent and have no supporting source locator.

children.title: Shift-Succession Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Covers permitted or prohibited transitions between shift types.

knowledge_statements.title: Shift-Succession Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forbidden or allowed transitions between shift types on successive roster days.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be ordered days, \(S\) a finite set of shift types including an off type, and \(x_{eds}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that employee \(e\) receives type \(s\) on day \(d\), with \(\sum_{s\in S}x_{eds}=1\). Given a forbidden transition set \(F_e\subseteq S\times S\), shift succession is feasible exactly when \[x_{eds}+x_{e,d+1,s'}\le1\qquad(e,\ d<n,\ (s,s')\in F_e).\] Equivalently, every realized adjacent pair belongs to the allowed set \((S\times S)\setminus F_e\). Longer forbidden successions require analogous inequalities over consecutive windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each adjacent pair of an employee's daily shift types must avoid the employee's forbidden transition set.
assumptions_latex: Exactly one shift type, including off, is selected per employee-day.
Days are linearly ordered.
\(F_e\) is specified for each employee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No realized adjacent shift pair lies in \(F_e\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forbidden-transition condition is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but the employee domain is not introduced and no specific rostering source supports the formulation.

children.title: Cumulative Fatigue Exposure
children.top_down_role: Covers workload patterns associated with inadequate rest or unfavorable transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Fatigue Exposure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete fatigue stock with carryover, assignment loads, and an exposure ceiling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For employees \(e\in E\) and periods \(t=1,\ldots,n\), let \(x_{est}\in\{0,1\}\) select shift type \(s\), let \(q_{est}\ge0\) be its fatigue load, and let \(0\le\rho_e\le1\) be fatigue carryover. Starting from \(F_{e1}=F_e^0\ge0\), define \[F_{e,t+1}=\rho_eF_{et}+\sum_{s\in S}q_{est}x_{est}.\] A cumulative-exposure limit \(\overline F_{et}\) requires \(F_{et}\le\overline F_{et}\) at every monitored period. More general finite-memory exposure models replace the recurrence by a weighted sum of recent assignment loads.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fatigue carries forward, increases with assigned shift loads, and must remain below a specified employee-period ceiling.
assumptions_latex: Fatigue loads are nonnegative.
\(0\le\rho_e\le1\).
Initial fatigue \(F_e^0\) is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{et}\le\overline F_{et}\) for every monitored employee-period pair.

notation.meaning: fatigue stock at the start of period t
fatigue load of shift type s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits cumulative fatigue exposure, but the recurrence, timing convention, and monitored-period set are model-specific and unsupported by a cited fatigue-rostering source.

children.title: Consecutive-Work Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers bounds on uninterrupted sequences of working periods or days.

knowledge_statements.title: Consecutive-Work Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sliding-window formulation of a maximum consecutive working-days rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and let \(w_{ed}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that employee \(e\) works on day \(d\). A maximum of \(L_e\ge0\) consecutive working days is enforced on the finite horizon by \[\sum_{r=d}^{d+L_e}w_{er}\le L_e\qquad(e\in E,\ d=1,\ldots,n-L_e).\] Indeed, each window of \(L_e+1\) days must contain at least one day off. If work runs may cross the horizon boundary, the same rule must also be imposed on windows completed using known pre-horizon or post-horizon assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every window of one more than the permitted run length must contain a day off.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{ed}\) is binary.
Days are consecutive and ordered.
Boundary history is supplied when runs may cross the horizon.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No employee has a work run longer than \(L_e\) days.

notation.meaning: work indicator for employee e on day d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sliding-window condition fits the leaf, but L_e must be specified as a nonnegative integer, and no inspectable rostering source is supplied.

children.title: Days-Off Patterns
children.top_down_role: Covers placement or grouping of nonworking days.

knowledge_statements.title: Days-Off Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Allowed-word formulation for local patterns of working and nonworking days.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{ed}\in\{0,1\}\) equal one when employee \(e\) is off on day \(d\). Fix a window length \(q_e\) and an allowed set \(P_e\subseteq\{0,1\}^{q_e}\). The roster satisfies the days-off pattern rule when \[(z_{ed},z_{e,d+1},\ldots,z_{e,d+q_e-1})\in P_e\qquad(d=1,\ldots,n-q_e+1).\] Thus \(P_e\) may encode isolated-day-off prohibitions, required off-day blocks, weekend patterns, or other local rules. If patterns may cross the planning boundary, the tested words must include fixed history or cyclic boundary values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every fixed-length window of an employee's off-day sequence must belong to a prescribed set of allowed binary patterns.
assumptions_latex: The roster has an ordered finite day horizon.
\(P_e\) is explicitly specified.
Boundary values are supplied when cross-boundary patterns matter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every tested off-day word belongs to \(P_e\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The allowed-word condition fits the leaf, but the employee and horizon domains are not fully introduced, and the contract-specific pattern semantics lack a source.

children.title: Work–Leave Cycle Structure
children.top_down_role: Covers recurring alternation between work runs and leave blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Work–Leave Cycle Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic binary-template representation of a repeating work–leave regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let employee \(e\) have cycle length \(C_e\ge1\) and binary template \(p_e=(p_{e1},\ldots,p_{eC_e})\), where one denotes work and zero denotes leave. With phase \(\phi_e\in\{0,\ldots,C_e-1\}\), the induced horizon roster is represented by \[w_{ed}=p_{e,\,1+((d-1+\phi_e)\bmod C_e)}\qquad(d=1,\ldots,n).\] If several templates are permitted, feasibility requires selection of exactly one template and phase. The modular representation makes the cycle continuous across the planning boundary; truncating it instead produces a finite pattern rather than a complete cycle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repeating work–leave roster is a periodic binary template, optionally shifted by an employee-specific phase.
assumptions_latex: \(C_e\) is a positive integer.
Template entries are binary.
The cycle is interpreted periodically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w_{e,d+C_e}=w_{ed}\) whenever both indexed days are represented.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind for this leaf, and the periodic formula is coherent, but no domain-relevant source is cited and the employee domain is unstated.

children.title: Horizon-Boundary Pattern Effects
children.top_down_role: Covers work or leave sequences extending across planning-horizon boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Boundary Pattern Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon omission of work–leave patterns that begin before or end after the modeled interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rule allowing at most \(L\ge1\) consecutive workdays on horizon \(D=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Internal constraints \(\sum_{r=d}^{d+L}w_r\le L\) test only \(d=1,\ldots,n-L\). If the employee worked on day \(0\) and \(w_1=\cdots=w_L=1\), all internal windows may be feasible, yet the actual cross-boundary run has length \(L+1\) and violates the rule. Therefore finite-horizon pattern constraints are valid for continuing rosters only after incorporating boundary history, terminal commitments, or an explicitly cyclic convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Internal windows can miss a prohibited run crossing the planning boundary; history, terminal commitments, or cyclic constraints are necessary.
assumptions_latex: The roster continues outside the modeled horizon.
At most \(L\) consecutive workdays are allowed.
Only fully internal windows are initially constrained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Internal-window feasibility does not imply cross-boundary pattern feasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct kind and the counterexample captures a genuine omission. However, the claimed remedies require precise assumptions—especially terminal commitments versus pre-horizon history—and no source is supplied.

children.title: Contractual Work Rules
children.top_down_role: Covers roster restrictions arising from employment agreements or worker categories.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractual Work Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified feasibility predicate for employee-specific contractual roster languages and quantitative limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For employee \(e\), let \(r_e\) denote the finite roster word over shift types, let \(\mathcal L_e\) be the language of contractually allowed words, and let \(A_er_e\le b_e\) collect quantitative contractual restrictions after binary encoding of \(r_e\). The contractual work rules are satisfied exactly when \[r_e\in\mathcal L_e\quad\text{and}\quad A_er_e\le b_e.\] The language component may impose successions, work–leave patterns, or weekend rules; the inequalities may impose hours, assignment counts, or overtime limits. Employee-specific contracts are represented by distinct pairs \((\mathcal L_e,A_e r_e\le b_e)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A roster is contractually feasible when its shift sequence is allowed and all encoded quantitative limits hold for that employee.
assumptions_latex: The planning horizon and shift alphabet are finite.
Each contract supplies an allowed language and quantitative bounds.
Roster words have a fixed binary encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Contractual feasibility is \(r_e\in\mathcal L_e\cap\{r:A_er\le b_e\}\).

notation.meaning: encoded roster word for employee e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition broadly fits the leaf, but r_e is used both as a symbolic word and as a vector in A_e r_e without a distinct encoding map. The language-plus-inequalities formalization also needs domain support.

children.title: Working-Hour Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers minimum, maximum, or target labor hours over defined periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Hour Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower and upper paid-hour bounds over designated contractual accounting windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ei}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of employee \(e\) to shift \(i\), and let \(h_{ei}\ge0\) be the credited hours. For each contractual accounting window \(W\) in a family \(\mathcal W_e\), define \(H_{eW}=\sum_{i\in W}h_{ei}x_{ei}\). Given lower and upper limits \(\underline H_{eW}\le\overline H_{eW}\), working-hour feasibility requires \[\underline H_{eW}\le H_{eW}\le\overline H_{eW}\qquad(W\in\mathcal W_e).\] The windows may overlap and may represent days, weeks, averaging periods, or the complete planning horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Credited assigned hours must lie between the contractual lower and upper bounds in every designated accounting window.
assumptions_latex: Credited shift hours are nonnegative and known.
Accounting windows are specified.
Hour bounds are contract-specific.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\underline H_{eW}\le\sum_{i\in W}h_{ei}x_{ei}\le\overline H_{eW}\) for every \(W\in\mathcal W_e\).

notation.meaning: credited hours in accounting window W

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits working-hour limits, but the employee and shift domains are not introduced, and i in W ambiguously treats an accounting window as a set of shifts. A sourced accounting convention is required.

children.title: Overtime Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Covers eligibility, caps, premiums, or authorization of excess hours.

knowledge_statements.title: Overtime Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear accounting and upper bounds for hours exceeding regular contractual allowances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For employee \(e\) and accounting window \(W\), let \(H_{eW}\) be credited worked hours, \(R_{eW}\ge0\) the regular-hour allowance, and \(o_{eW}\ge0\) recorded overtime. Valid overtime accounting requires \[o_{eW}\ge H_{eW}-R_{eW},\qquad 0\le o_{eW}\le O_{eW},\] where \(O_{eW}\ge0\) is the overtime cap. If overtime is minimized or positively penalized, then \(o_{eW}=\max\{0,H_{eW}-R_{eW}\}\). A prohibition on overtime is the special case \(O_{eW}=0\). Additional aggregate limits can impose \(\sum_{W\in\mathcal W'}o_{eW}\le O_e^{\mathcal W'}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overtime records hours above the regular allowance and cannot exceed the applicable window or aggregate cap.
assumptions_latex: Credited hours and regular allowances use the same accounting convention.
Overtime variables are nonnegative.
Equality accounting uses positive overtime minimization or penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le\max\{0,H_{eW}-R_{eW}\}\le O_{eW}\) in every accounting window.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and the inequalities are coherent under positive minimization of overtime, but equality accounting and aggregate-window semantics are convention-dependent and unsupported by a source locator.

children.title: Cross-Period Hour Accounting
children.top_down_role: Covers accumulation or balancing of hours across roster periods.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Period Hour Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balance equations carrying contractual work-hour credit or debt between consecutive accounting periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be ordered accounting periods, let \(h_{ip}\) be employee \(i\)'s assigned hours in period \(p\), and let \(q_{ip}\) be the contractual target. With initial balance \(b_{i0}\), cross-period accounting requires
\[b_{ip}=b_{i,p-1}+h_{ip}-q_{ip}\qquad(i\in I,\ p\in P).\]
If carryover bounds are contractual, impose \(L_{ip}\le b_{ip}\le U_{ip}\). A terminal settlement rule is expressed by \(b_{im}=\bar b_i\), or by penalizing positive and negative parts satisfying \(b_{im}=b_{im}^{+}-b_{im}^{-}\) with \(b_{im}^{+},b_{im}^{-}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each period’s hour balance equals the previous balance plus worked hours minus target hours, subject to carryover bounds and any terminal settlement rule.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(P=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) are finite.
\(h_{ip},q_{ip},b_{ip},L_{ip},U_{ip}\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{ip}=b_{i,p-1}+h_{ip}-q_{ip}\), with prescribed carryover and terminal conditions.

notation.meaning: hours assigned to employee i in period p
hour credit or debt carried after period p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition formulation matches cross-period hour accounting and is internally coherent, but no inspectable domain source supports the balance, carryover, or terminal-settlement variants. Standard-field rationale alone does not resolve which contractual variants belong in this leaf.

children.title: Personnel Qualification Requirements
children.top_down_role: Covers credentials, competencies, or authorization required for assigned work.

knowledge_statements.title: Personnel Qualification Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage constraints requiring assigned personnel to possess each demanded qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be personnel, \(T\) duty slots, and \(Q\) qualifications. Let \(x_{it}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment, \(a_{iq}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that person \(i\) holds qualification \(q\), and let \(r_{tq}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be demand. Qualification feasibility requires
\[\sum_{i\in I}a_{iq}x_{it}\ge r_{tq}\qquad(t\in T,\ q\in Q).\]
When an assignment itself requires a designated qualification \(q(t)\), individual eligibility is additionally enforced by \(x_{it}\le a_{i,q(t)}\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(t\in T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every duty slot must receive enough assigned personnel holding each required qualification, and individually restricted duties may use only eligible personnel.
assumptions_latex: \(I,T,Q\) are finite.
Qualification indicators \(a_{iq}\) and demands \(r_{tq}\) are fixed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i\in I}a_{iq}x_{it}\ge r_{tq}\) for all \(t\in T\) and \(q\in Q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected condition kind fits the leaf, and the qualified-coverage and individual-eligibility constraints are mathematically precise. No specific authoritative rostering source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Team Composition Requirements
children.top_down_role: Covers role, skill, seniority, or size requirements within working teams.

knowledge_statements.title: Team Composition Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear lower, upper, and relational constraints on personnel categories within each staffed team.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be personnel, \(T\) team-duty slots, and \(G\) personnel categories, with membership data \(c_{ig}\in\{0,1\}\) and assignment variables \(x_{it}\in\{0,1\}\). A team-composition specification consists of bounds
\[\ell_{tg}\le \sum_{i\in I}c_{ig}x_{it}\le u_{tg}\qquad(t\in T,\ g\in G).\]
Required category ratios or implications may be represented by linear relations; for example, the requirement that every team containing a trainee also contain a supervisor is
\[\sum_{i\in I}c_{i,\mathrm{trainee}}x_{it}\le M_t\sum_{i\in I}c_{i,\mathrm{supervisor}}x_{it},\]
where \(M_t\) bounds the team size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each team must satisfy category headcount bounds and any specified composition relations, such as requiring a supervisor whenever a trainee is assigned.
assumptions_latex: \(I,T,G\) are finite.
\(M_t\) is a valid upper bound on team size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every staffed team satisfies its prescribed category bounds and relational composition constraints.

notation.meaning: assignment of person i to team-duty slot t
membership of person i in category g

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits team-composition requirements, but the trainee-supervisor inequality does not explicitly quantify the duty slot, and the category and team semantics require domain support. No source is supplied, so the intended formulation cannot be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Personnel Substitution Rules
children.top_down_role: Covers conditions under which one worker may replace another.

knowledge_statements.title: Personnel Substitution Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility and capacity conditions for replacing an unavailable or unassigned worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be personnel and \(T\) duty slots. Let \(s_{ijt}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that person \(j\) substitutes for person \(i\) in slot \(t\), and let \(A_{ijt}\in\{0,1\}\) encode qualification, contractual, and temporal admissibility. Valid substitutions satisfy
\[s_{ijt}\le A_{ijt},\qquad \sum_{j\in I}s_{ijt}\le1,\qquad \sum_{i\in I}s_{ijt}\le1.\]
If \(z_{it}=1\) records that \(i\)'s originally assigned duty in \(t\) requires replacement, exact replacement additionally requires \(\sum_{j\in I}s_{ijt}=z_{it}\). The substitute's resulting roster must also satisfy all ordinary workload and overlap constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A replacement must be admissible, cover the displaced duty as required, avoid simultaneous multiple substitutions, and preserve the substitute’s ordinary roster feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(T\) are finite.
Admissibility data \(A_{ijt}\) incorporate all substitution-specific rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected substitutions satisfy admissibility, replacement, and per-slot capacity conditions.

notation.meaning: indicator that j replaces i in slot t
indicator that i's duty requires replacement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, but the model does not state whether self-substitution is excluded, whether a substitute can also hold an ordinary assignment in the slot, or precisely how ordinary overlap constraints couple to substitution variables. These application-dependent semantics need an inspectable source.

children.title: Qualification–Team Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Covers consistency between individual credentials and team-level composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Qualification–Team Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate coupling a worker’s qualifications with the requirements of a team role.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be personnel, \(T\) team roles, and \(Q\) qualifications. For each role \(t\), let \(R_t\subseteq Q\) be its mandatory qualifications, and for each person \(i\), let \(Q_i\subseteq Q\) be held qualifications. Define
\[C_{it}=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_t\subseteq Q_i\ \text{ and all role-specific incompatibility rules are satisfied}.\]
With assignment variable \(x_{it}\in\{0,1\}\), qualification–team compatibility is the condition \(x_{it}\le C_{it}\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(t\in T\). Thus no assignment may connect an incompatible person-role pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A person may occupy a team role only when all mandatory qualifications and role-specific compatibility rules are satisfied.
assumptions_latex: \(I,T,Q\) are finite.
Held and required qualification sets are fixed before assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{it}\le C_{it}\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(t\in T\).

notation.meaning: qualifications required by team role t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and compatibility-matrix formulation fit the leaf. However, the phrase 'all role-specific incompatibility rules' leaves part of the predicate externally unspecified, and no domain source identifies the intended rules or supports this formulation.

children.title: Roster Preferences
children.top_down_role: Covers general worker preferences concerning shifts, duties, timing, or colleagues.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Preferences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive penalty representation of soft employee preferences over assignments and roster features.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be the set of hard-feasible rosters and let \(K_i\) index preference features declared for employee \(i\). For roster \(x\in X\), let \(v_{ik}(x)\ge0\) measure violation of feature \(k\), and let \(w_{ik}\ge0\) be its priority weight. The aggregate preference cost is represented by
\[P(x)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K_i}w_{ik}v_{ik}(x).\]
A preference-optimal roster minimizes \(P(x)\) over \(X\), unless preference cost is one component of a stated multiobjective rule. Zero violation denotes satisfaction; positive values permit graded rather than merely binary dissatisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft roster preferences are represented by weighted violation measures and optimized over rosters satisfying all hard constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty finite set of hard-feasible rosters.
All weights and violation measures are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(x)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K_i}w_{ik}v_{ik}(x)\) quantifies aggregate preference dissatisfaction.

notation.meaning: violation magnitude of a preference feature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for the additive soft-preference model, and the notation and optimization scope are coherent. No authoritative rostering source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Specific Roster Requests
children.top_down_role: Covers dated or otherwise explicit requests for work or leave.

knowledge_statements.title: Specific Roster Requests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard or soft encoding of an employee’s request to work or avoid a specified duty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{it}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether employee \(i\) works duty slot \(t\). A request-on pair \((i,t)\) is satisfied when \(x_{it}=1\), while a request-off pair is satisfied when \(x_{it}=0\). If requests are soft, introduce violations \(u_{it}^{+},u_{it}^{-}\in\{0,1\}\) and impose
\[x_{it}+u_{it}^{+}\ge1\quad\text{for request-on pairs},\qquad x_{it}\le u_{it}^{-}\quad\text{for request-off pairs}.\]
Their weighted sum may be minimized. If a request is designated hard, set its corresponding violation variable to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Work and leave requests impose requested assignment values; soft requests allow penalized violations, while hard requests fix the corresponding assignment.
assumptions_latex: Assignment variables are binary.
Each request is classified as request-on or request-off and as hard or soft.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each request is either satisfied or recorded by its designated violation variable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits specific work and leave requests, and the binary violation encodings are correct under the stated assumptions. No inspectable rostering source supports the hard-versus-soft request formulation.

children.title: Roster Fairness Criteria
children.top_down_role: Covers equitable distribution of desirable or undesirable assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Fairness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equity criteria applied to employee burdens or preference dissatisfaction within a feasible roster.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be the feasible roster set and let \(b_i(x)\in\mathbb R\) be the normalized undesirable burden assigned to employee \(i\) by roster \(x\). Common checkable fairness criteria include range fairness,
\[\max_{i\in I}b_i(x)-\min_{i\in I}b_i(x)\le\Delta,\]
and minimax fairness, under which \(x\) minimizes \(\max_{i\in I}b_i(x)\) over \(X\). Lexicographic minimax fairness instead lexicographically minimizes the vector of burdens sorted in nonincreasing order. Burdens must be normalized when employee contracts or availabilities make raw counts incomparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fairness can bound burden disparity, minimize the worst burden, or lexicographically improve ordered burdens, using normalized measures when employees have unequal opportunities.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and the feasible roster set \(X\) are finite.
Burden values are comparable across employees after any required normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fairness is enforced or optimized through a specified disparity, minimax, or lexicographic burden criterion.

notation.meaning: normalized undesirable burden of employee i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record combines a disparity condition, a minimax optimization criterion, and a lexicographic minimax criterion, so generic condition is not an exact mathematical role for the whole statement. A domain source is also needed to justify the selected fairness notions and normalization requirement before a reliable replacement can be specified.

children.title: Preference–Fairness Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Covers conflicts between individual satisfaction and equitable treatment.

knowledge_statements.title: Preference–Fairness Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto and scalarized formulations relating total preference dissatisfaction to interemployee fairness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be the hard-feasible roster set, \(P(x)\ge0\) total preference dissatisfaction, and \(F(x)\ge0\) a fairness loss. The attainable tradeoff set is
\[Y=\{(P(x),F(x)):x\in X\}.\]
A roster \(x^*\in X\) is Pareto efficient if no \(x\in X\) satisfies \(P(x)\le P(x^*)\) and \(F(x)\le F(x^*)\) with at least one strict inequality. A supported tradeoff roster is obtained by minimizing \(\lambda P(x)+(1-\lambda)F(x)\) for \(0\le\lambda\le1\); unsupported efficient points may require an epsilon-constraint formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preference and fairness losses define a Pareto frontier; weighted sums find supported compromises, while epsilon constraints can recover unsupported efficient rosters.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a nonempty finite feasible roster set.
\(P\) and \(F\) are nonnegative losses to be minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Efficient preference–fairness compromises are the nondominated points of \(Y\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Pareto and scalarization definitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the attainable-set and scalarization treatment, and the Pareto and supported-point statements are precise for a finite feasible set. No authoritative multiobjective or rostering source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Day–Shift Assignment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary tensor representation assigning each employee at most one shift on each day.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be employees, \(D\) days, and \(S_d\) shifts available on day \(d\). Define \(x_{ids}\in\{0,1\}\) to equal one exactly when employee \(i\) works shift \(s\) on day \(d\). A basic day–shift model contains
\[\sum_{s\in S_d}x_{ids}\le1\qquad(i\in I,\ d\in D),\]
\[\sum_{i\in I}a_{iq}x_{ids}\ge r_{dsq}\qquad(d\in D,\ s\in S_d,\ q\in Q),\]
where \(a_{iq}\) records qualifications and \(r_{dsq}\) is required coverage. Work-pattern, rest, and contractual constraints are additional relations among variables on multiple days.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary employee–day–shift variables enforce at most one daily shift and qualified coverage, with multi-day rules added as linking constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(I,D,Q\), and every \(S_d\) are finite.
Coverage requirements and qualification indicators are fixed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary tensor \(x_{ids}\) represents a roster satisfying daily exclusivity and qualified coverage.

source_refs.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

source_witnesses.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct kind for a day-shift assignment model, and the displayed constraints are coherent. The cited assignment-problem section is indirect and does not support the employee-day-shift tensor, qualified coverage rows, or multiday rostering interpretation; a roster-specific source is required.

children.title: Set-Covering Roster Models
children.top_down_role: Covers roster-column selections permitting demand or assignment requirements to be covered at least once.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Covering Roster Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roster-column formulation permitting selected legal rosters to cover demand at least once.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_i\) be the finite set of legal complete rosters for employee \(i\), and let \(y_{ir}\in\{0,1\}\) select roster \(r\in R_i\). If \(a_{ir,tq}\in\{0,1\}\) indicates whether that roster supplies qualification \(q\) in duty slot \(t\), a set-covering roster formulation includes
\[\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{r\in R_i}a_{ir,tq}y_{ir}\ge d_{tq}\qquad(t\in T,\ q\in Q),\]
\[\sum_{r\in R_i}y_{ir}=1\qquad(i\in I).\]
With roster costs \(c_{ir}\), the objective is typically to minimize \(\sum_{i,r}c_{ir}y_{ir}\). Excess coverage is allowed unless separately bounded or penalized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each employee selects one legal roster column, and the selected columns cover every qualified demand requirement, possibly with excess coverage.
assumptions_latex: Personnel, duty slots, qualifications, and legal roster sets are finite.
Each roster column already satisfies all employee-local rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected roster columns satisfy \(\sum_{i,r}a_{ir,tq}y_{ir}\ge d_{tq}\) for every demand row.

notation.meaning: selection indicator for employee roster column
coverage supplied by a roster column

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the set-covering roster leaf, and the formulation consistently permits excess coverage while selecting one legal roster per employee. No inspectable rostering or column-generation source is supplied.

children.title: Set-Partitioning Roster Models
children.top_down_role: Covers roster-column selections requiring exact assignment coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Partitioning Roster Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roster-column formulation requiring exact coverage of each modeled demand unit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_i\) be the legal complete rosters for employee \(i\), let \(y_{ir}\in\{0,1\}\) select roster \(r\in R_i\), and let \(a_{irj}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether column \((i,r)\) covers demand unit \(j\in J\). A set-partitioning roster formulation imposes
\[\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{r\in R_i}a_{irj}y_{ir}=1\qquad(j\in J),\]
\[\sum_{r\in R_i}y_{ir}=1\qquad(i\in I).\]
The first equations assign every demand unit to exactly one selected roster column; hence demand units must be defined at a granularity for which exact single coverage is meaningful. Costs are minimized over these equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each employee selects one legal roster column, and every atomic demand unit is covered by exactly one selected column.
assumptions_latex: Personnel, demand units, and legal roster sets are finite.
Every demand unit is defined so that exact single coverage is meaningful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected columns partition the demand units through \(\sum_{i,r}a_{irj}y_{ir}=1\) for all \(j\in J\).

notation.meaning: selection indicator for employee roster column
incidence of roster column with demand unit j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation fits the set-partitioning roster leaf, and the exact-cover equations are mathematically coherent for atomic demand units. No inspectable rostering or set-partitioning source is supplied to support this particular column interpretation.

children.title: Covering-to-Partitioning Transitions
children.top_down_role: Covers structural changes between excess-coverage and exact-coverage regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Covering-to-Partitioning Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition from employee-pattern covering constraints to exact-assignment constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite employee set, let \(P_e\) be the finite set of feasible roster columns for employee \(e\in E\), and let \(x_{ep}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate selection of column \(p\in P_e\). A set-covering model imposes \(\sum_{p\in P_e}x_{ep}\ge 1\) for every \(e\in E\). Its set-partitioning counterpart is obtained by replacing these inequalities with \(\sum_{p\in P_e}x_{ep}=1\) for every \(e\in E\), while retaining all other common constraints. Equivalently, after writing \(\sum_{p\in P_e}x_{ep}-s_e=1\) with \(s_e\ge 0\), the transition imposes \(s_e=0\) for every \(e\in E\). For the corresponding linear relaxation, the exact-assignment restriction is an exposed face whenever it is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set partitioning is obtained from set covering by requiring each employee to select exactly one roster column. In the linear relaxation, the nonempty exact-assignment restriction is a face of the covering polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and every \(P_e\) are finite.
\(x_{ep}\in\{0,1\}\) for all \(e\in E\) and \(p\in P_e\).
All constraints other than the employee covering or partitioning constraints are held fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_{\mathrm{part}}=\{x\in F_{\mathrm{cover}}:\sum_{p\in P_e}x_{ep}=1\text{ for every }e\in E\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible complete roster columns for employee e.
Integer feasible set of the set-covering formulation.
Integer feasible set after imposing exact employee assignment.

children.title: Roster Column Granularity
children.top_down_role: Covers differences between complete-roster, partial-roster, or duty-level columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Column Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the decision scope represented by one roster column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a planning horizon \(T\), employees \(E\), and assignment alphabet \(S\). A roster column of granularity \((U,H)\), where \(U\subseteq E\) and \(H\subseteq T\), is one feasible joint assignment \(p:U\times H\to S\). Employee-level columns have \(|U|=1\); day-level columns have \(|H|=1\); complete-horizon employee columns have \(|U|=1\) and \(H=T\); complete-roster columns have \(U=E\) and \(H=T\). Increasing either indexed scope yields coarser decision granularity because one variable encodes more elementary assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column granularity is the employee and time scope encoded by one variable, ranging from local assignments to complete rosters.
assumptions_latex: \(E\), \(T\), and \(S\) are finite.
Feasibility is defined by the roster rules restricted to \(U\times H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(p)=(U,H)\), with elementary scope size \(|U|\,|H|\).

notation.meaning: Employee and time scope of a column.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the proposed employee-time granularity pair and the direction labeled coarser are not established as standard rostering terminology. A domain source is required.

children.title: Network-Flow Roster Models
children.top_down_role: Covers roster decisions represented through flows over state or time networks.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Flow Roster Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-expanded flow representation of individual employee rosters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each employee \(e\), let \(G_e=(V_e,A_e)\) be a directed time-expanded network with source \(s_e\), sink \(t_e\), and arc costs \(c_{ea}\). A binary arc flow \(y_{ea}\) represents use of roster transition \(a\). Flow conservation requires one unit from \(s_e\) to \(t_e\): \(B_e y_e=b_e\), where \(b_e(s_e)=1\), \(b_e(t_e)=-1\), and all other entries are zero. If \(q_{ead}\) records coverage of demand item \(d\), workforce requirements are imposed by \(\sum_e\sum_{a\in A_e}q_{ead}y_{ea}\ge r_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each employee’s roster is a unit source-to-sink flow in a time-expanded network, coupled to other employees through coverage constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible source-to-sink route encodes an admissible employee roster.
\(y_{ea}\in\{0,1\}\) for each employee-arc pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\sum_e c_e^{\mathsf T}y_e:B_e y_e=b_e,\ \sum_e Q_e y_e\ge r,\ y_e\in\{0,1\}^{A_e}\}\) is a network-flow roster formulation.

The local extract is only a table of contents.

children.title: Path-Based Roster Models
children.top_down_role: Covers feasible work sequences represented as paths or path columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Based Roster Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete employee rosters represented as source-to-sink path columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For employee \(e\), let \(P_e\) be the source-to-sink paths in a roster network, and let \(x_{ep}\in\{0,1\}\) select path \(p\). With path cost \(c_{ep}\) and coverage coefficient \(a_{epd}\) for demand item \(d\), the path formulation minimizes \(\sum_e\sum_{p\in P_e}c_{ep}x_{ep}\), subject to \(\sum_{p\in P_e}x_{ep}=1\) for each employee and \(\sum_e\sum_{p\in P_e}a_{epd}x_{ep}\ge r_d\) for every demand item. Each selected column therefore represents one complete feasible employee roster.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-based model chooses one complete network path per employee and couples these choices through workforce coverage constraints.
assumptions_latex: Each path in \(P_e\) encodes a feasible complete roster for employee \(e\).
The planning horizon and employee set are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{\sum_{e,p}c_{ep}x_{ep}:\sum_{p\in P_e}x_{ep}=1,\ \sum_{e,p}a_{epd}x_{ep}\ge r_d,\ x_{ep}\in\{0,1\}\}\) is the path-based representation.

notation.meaning: Source-to-sink roster paths for employee e.
Coverage supplied by path p to demand item d.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The path formulation is coherent and appropriately classified as a representation, but the general path-flow citation does not support the rostering master formulation, one-roster-per-employee constraints, or workforce coverage coupling. The local extract is only a table of contents.

children.title: Flow-to-Path Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Covers correspondence between aggregate flows and individual roster paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-to-Path Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite acyclic source-to-sink flow decomposition used for roster columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed acyclic graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and a nonnegative flow \(y\) satisfying conservation at every vertex other than \(s\) and \(t\). If the flow value is \(v\), then there exist source-to-sink paths \(p\) and coefficients \(\lambda_p>0\) such that \(y=\sum_p\lambda_p\chi^p\) and \(\sum_p\lambda_p=v\). At most \(|A|\) coefficients need be positive. If \(y\) is integral, the coefficients may be chosen integral; a unit integral flow is the incidence vector of one source-to-sink path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative flow in an acyclic roster network decomposes into finitely many path flows; an integral unit flow is one roster path.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and directed acyclic.
\(y\ge 0\) satisfies flow conservation outside \(s\) and \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=\sum_p\lambda_p\chi^p\), \(\sum_p\lambda_p=v\), and \(|\{p:\lambda_p>0\}|\le |A|\).

children.title: Network State-Space Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers representation growth caused by detailed work-history states.

knowledge_statements.title: Network State-Space Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential state growth under history-distinguishing roster rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(k\ge 1\) and alphabet \(\Sigma=\{0,1,\#\}\). Consider roster strings whose prefix before \(\#\) has length \(k\) and whose length-\(k\) suffix after \(\#\) must reproduce that prefix. Before reading \(\#\), any deterministic state network recognizing this rule must distinguish all \(2^k\) binary prefixes: two different prefixes require different accepted continuations. Consequently, an exact deterministic time-expanded network whose state contains all information needed to enforce this rule has at least \(2^k\) reachable states at the delimiter layer. Polynomial horizon length therefore does not guarantee polynomial network size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rules that require recalling an arbitrary k-day history force at least 2^k distinguishable network states, making exact state expansion exponential.
assumptions_latex: The network state must determine feasibility of every possible continuation.
The encoding is deterministic and exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V_k|\ge 2^k\) at the history-completion layer.

notation.meaning: Length of the history that must be remembered.
Reachable network states after k history symbols.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinguishable-prefix lower bound is mathematically plausible and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but no source supports the automata lower-bound argument or its transfer to exact time-expanded roster networks.

children.title: Roster Automata
children.top_down_role: Covers state-transition representations of admissible work histories.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Automata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state acceptance model for shift sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A roster automaton is a finite automaton \(M=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\), where \(\Sigma\) is a finite alphabet of shift or rest labels, \(Q\) is a finite state set, \(q_0\in Q\) is initial, \(F\subseteq Q\) is accepting, and \(\delta:Q\times\Sigma\to Q\) is the transition function. For a horizon of length \(T\), a roster \(w=w_1\cdots w_T\in\Sigma^T\) is feasible for the encoded rules exactly when the extended transition satisfies \(\delta^*(q_0,w)\in F\). States summarize all past information relevant to future admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A roster automaton accepts exactly those finite shift sequences whose successive labels end in an accepting state.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and \(\Sigma\) are finite.
The automaton is deterministic; partial transitions may be completed with a rejecting sink.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_T(M)=\{w\in\Sigma^T:\delta^*(q_0,w)\in F\}\).

notation.meaning: Transition function extended to finite words.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic finite-automaton definition is precise and fits the leaf, but neither the formal automata definition nor its rostering interpretation has a cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Regular-Language Work Patterns
children.top_down_role: Covers admissible work sequences expressed through regular-language structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular-Language Work Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-pattern feasibility expressed as a regular language.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma\) be a finite alphabet of daily shift and rest labels. A work-pattern family \(L\subseteq\Sigma^*\) is regular if there exists a finite roster automaton \(M=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) such that \(L=\{w\in\Sigma^*: \delta^*(q_0,w)\in F\}\). For a fixed horizon \(T\), its feasible rosters are \(L\cap\Sigma^T\). Thus regular-language rules include precisely those pattern restrictions whose required history can be summarized by one of finitely many continuation-equivalence states.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A work-pattern family is regular when a finite automaton recognizes exactly its admissible shift strings; fixed-horizon rosters are its words of length T.
assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is finite.
Work patterns are represented as finite words.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\text{ is regular}\iff \exists M\text{ finite with }L=L(M)\).

notation.meaning: Set of all finite work-label strings.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regular-language definition is standard and locally appropriate, but the continuation-equivalence characterization is a substantive theorem-level claim and no formal-language source is cited.

children.title: Pattern-to-Automaton Encoding
children.top_down_role: Covers translation of work-pattern restrictions into automaton states or transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pattern-to-Automaton Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state compilation of a regular work-pattern specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a regular expression \(R\) over a finite roster alphabet \(\Sigma\). Construct an \(\varepsilon\)-NFA recursively. Use standard base automata for each symbol, the empty word, and the empty language. For a union, introduce fresh start and accepting states, add \(\varepsilon\)-transitions from the fresh start to both component starts, and add \(\varepsilon\)-transitions from both component accepting states to the fresh accepting state. For concatenation, add \(\varepsilon\)-transitions from every accepting state of the first component to the start of the second component. For Kleene star, introduce fresh start and accepting states, allow an \(\varepsilon\)-transition directly from the new start to the new accepting state and another to the component start, and add transitions from every component accepting state to both the component start and the new accepting state. The resulting \(\varepsilon\)-NFA \(N\) satisfies \(L(N)=L(R)\). If a deterministic automaton is required, apply subset construction using \(\varepsilon\)-closures; a subset is accepting exactly when it contains an accepting state of \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compile a regular work-pattern expression into an equivalent epsilon-NFA using the standard recursive constructions, then apply subset construction if a deterministic roster automaton is required.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a finite regular expression over a finite alphabet \(\Sigma\).
Only union, concatenation, Kleene star, atomic symbols, the empty word, and the empty language are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(N)=L(R)\), and determinization returns \(D\) with \(L(D)=L(R)\).

children.title: Automaton Expressiveness Limits
children.top_down_role: Covers work-pattern dependencies that require impractically large or richer representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Automaton Expressiveness Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite automata cannot encode unbounded counting dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Over \(\Sigma=\{W,R\}\), consider the work-pattern language \(L=\{W^nR^n:n\ge 0\}\), requiring an initial work block followed by an equally long rest block. No finite roster automaton recognizes \(L\). Indeed, after the prefixes \(W^0,W^1,\ldots\), exact recognition requires pairwise distinct continuation states because appending \(R^i\) must accept after \(W^i\) but reject after \(W^j\) for \(j\ne i\). Hence finite-state roster models cannot exactly express rules requiring an unbounded counter unless the horizon or counter is bounded and incorporated into the state space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite automata cannot enforce equality of two unbounded block lengths; such rules require bounds, counters, or a richer representation.
assumptions_latex: The planning horizon is unbounded.
The automaton has finitely many states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{W^nR^n:n\ge 0\}\) is not regular and is not recognizable by any finite roster automaton.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unbounded-horizon counterexample is mathematically standard and correctly classified as a failure boundary, but the nonregularity claim and distinguishability argument lack a cited source.

children.title: Multistage Roster Models
children.top_down_role: Covers roster decisions distributed across successive planning stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Roster Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential roster decisions under progressively revealed information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the finite decision stages be \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(\Omega\) be a finite scenario set, and let \(h_t^\omega=(\xi_1^\omega,\ldots,\xi_t^\omega)\) be the information history observed under scenario \(\omega\in\Omega\) through stage \(t\). A multistage roster policy selects \(x_t(h_t^\omega)\in X_t(h_t^\omega,x_{1:t-1})\). It is nonanticipative when \(x_t(h_t^\omega)=x_t(h_t^{\omega'})\) whenever \(h_t^\omega=h_t^{\omega'}\). For scenario \(\omega\), define total cost \(C^\omega(x)=\sum_{t=1}^T c_t(x_t(h_t^\omega),\xi_t^\omega)\). Given a specified functional \(\rho:\mathbb{R}^{|\Omega|}\to\mathbb{R}\), the model minimizes \(\rho((C^\omega(x))_{\omega\in\Omega})\) over feasible nonanticipative policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-scenario multistage roster model selects sequential decisions from revealed histories, forces scenarios with the same history to share their current decision, and optimizes a specified functional of scenario costs.
assumptions_latex: The stage set and scenario set \(\Omega\) are finite.
At stage \(t\), only the history \(h_t^\omega\) is observable.
The objective functional \(\rho:\mathbb{R}^{|\Omega|}\to\mathbb{R}\) is specified as part of the model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\ \mathrm{nonanticipative}}\rho((C^\omega(x))_{\omega\in\Omega})\) defines the finite-scenario multistage roster problem.

notation.meaning: Information history available at stage t under scenario omega.
Stage-t roster decision prescribed for the observed history.
Total policy cost in scenario omega.
Specified functional of the vector of scenario costs.

children.title: Hierarchical Roster Models
children.top_down_role: Covers roster decisions organized across strategic, tactical, or operational levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Roster Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leader-follower representation of roster decisions at distinct authority levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A two-level hierarchical roster model consists of an upper-level decision \(x\in X\), a lower-level feasible set \(Y(x)\), upper objective \(F(x,y)\), and lower objective \(f(x,y)\). The lower-level response set is \(S(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Y(x)}f(x,z)\). Under the optimistic convention, the hierarchy solves \(\min\{F(x,y):x\in X,\ y\in S(x)\}\), selecting the upper-preferred response when \(S(x)\) is not a singleton. In rostering, \(x\) may prescribe staffing or shift templates while \(y\) assigns employees subject to those prescriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical roster model optimizes a leader decision while requiring the employee-level roster to be an optimal follower response.
assumptions_latex: \(S(x)\ne\varnothing\) for every upper-level decision considered.
The optimistic response convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X,\,y\in S(x)}F(x,y)\), where \(S(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Y(x)}f(x,z)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimistic bilevel model is mathematically coherent, but the broader title Hierarchical Roster Models does not by itself imply follower optimality or an optimistic response convention. A source is needed to establish that this is the intended local sense and to support the rostering specialization.

children.title: Cross-Stage Decision Linkage
children.top_down_role: Covers dependencies among decisions made at different planning stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Stage Decision Linkage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for successive stages of a finite personnel-roster hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb N\), let \(Y_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_k}\) be the feasible decision set at stage \(k\), and let \(y^k\in Y_k\) for \(k=1,\ldots,K\). For each \(k=1,\ldots,K-1\), let \(L_k:Y_k\times Y_{k+1}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\) be a linkage predicate. The sequence \((y^1,\ldots,y^K)\) is hierarchy-compatible exactly when \[L_k(y^k,y^{k+1})=\mathrm{true}\qquad(k=1,\ldots,K-1).\] In a linear specialization, choose \(p_k\in\mathbb N\), \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times n_k}\), \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k\times n_{k+1}}\), and \(b_k\in\mathbb R^{p_k}\), and impose \[A_k y^k+B_k y^{k+1}\le b_k\qquad(k=1,\ldots,K-1).\] Such constraints can transfer staffing totals, skill capacities, fixed assignments, or accumulated workload between adjacent stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage roster is hierarchy-compatible when every stage decision belongs to its stage-feasible set and each adjacent pair satisfies its prescribed linkage predicate; compatible linear linkage constraints may transfer roster quantities between stages.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
For every \(k\), \(Y_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_k}\) is the stage-\(k\) feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y^1,\ldots,y^K)\) is hierarchy-compatible if and only if \(y^k\in Y_k\) for every stage and \(L_k(y^k,y^{k+1})\) holds for every adjacent pair.

notation.meaning: decision vector at hierarchy stage k
dimensionally compatible data for a linear linkage constraint

children.title: Hierarchy Coordination Failures
children.top_down_role: Covers infeasibility or performance loss caused by inconsistent decisions across levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy Coordination Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal counterexample to independent optimization of linked roster stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an upper-stage capacity decision \(y\in\{0,1\}\) and a lower-stage assignment decision \(x\in\{0,1\}\), linked by \(x\le y\). The upper stage, solved independently, minimizes \(y\) and therefore selects \(y=0\). The lower stage must cover one unit of demand, so it requires \(x=1\), which violates \(x\le y\). By contrast, the integrated problem
\[\min\{y:y\in\{0,1\},\ x\in\{0,1\},\ x=1,\ x\le y\}\]
has the feasible optimum \((y,x)=(1,1)\). Thus stagewise optimal decisions need not be jointly feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent upper-stage optimization can reserve no capacity, making mandatory lower-stage coverage infeasible even though the integrated hierarchy is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The upper-stage objective omits the lower-stage coverage requirement.
The lower stage requires \(x=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The independently selected pair is infeasible, whereas the integrated model has optimum \((y,x)=(1,1)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally correct, uses the proper content kind, and directly illustrates the stated failure, but it has no cited evidence or explicit standard-field rationale as required by the evidence contract.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Programming for Rostering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary assignment formulation for a finite-horizon personnel-roster problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\), \(D\), and \(S\) be finite employee, day, and shift sets. For every \((e,d,s)\in E\times D\times S\), define \(x_{eds}\in\{0,1\}\), equal to one exactly when employee \(e\) works shift \(s\) on day \(d\). Given costs \(c_{eds}\in\mathbb R\) and staffing requirements \(r_{ds}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), a basic roster model is \[\min \sum_{e\in E}\sum_{d\in D}\sum_{s\in S}c_{eds}x_{eds}\] subject to \[\sum_{e\in E}x_{eds}\ge r_{ds}\quad((d,s)\in D\times S),\qquad \sum_{s\in S}x_{eds}\le1\quad((e,d)\in E\times D),\] together with specified linear constraints encoding qualifications, rest, workload, and fixed assignments. Feasible binary vectors correspond exactly to rosters satisfying all rules encoded by these constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary employee-day-shift variables, explicitly indexed coverage and daily-assignment constraints, and additional linear work-rule constraints represent the encoded feasible rosters.
assumptions_latex: \(E\), \(D\), and \(S\) are finite.
Every roster rule included in the model has a specified linear encoding in the chosen variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible integer vectors are exactly the rosters satisfying the encoded coverage and work rules.

notation.meaning: required staffing for day d and shift s

children.title: Rostering Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Roster-pattern generation, restricted masters, pricing structure, plus stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Rostering Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column generation for a set-covering master problem whose columns are complete employee rosters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_e\) be the set of feasible rosters for employee \(e\), with cost \(c_{er}\) and coverage coefficients \(a_{er,ds}\). Initialize finite nonempty subsets \(R'_e\subseteq R_e\). Repeatedly solve the restricted linear master over variables \(\lambda_{er}\ge0\), obtain dual multipliers \(\pi_{ds}\) and \(\sigma_e\), and for every employee minimize
\[\bar c_{er}=c_{er}-\sum_{d,s}\pi_{ds}a_{er,ds}-\sigma_e\quad\text{over }r\in R_e.\]
Add any column having negative reduced cost. Stop when no employee has such a column; then the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full linear master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted roster master, price new employee rosters using dual values, add negative-reduced-cost columns, and stop when none remain.
assumptions_latex: Each restricted master is feasible and solved exactly.
Each employee pricing problem is solved exactly.
The full roster sets \(R_e\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every minimum reduced cost is nonnegative, the current solution is optimal for the full linear master problem.

notation.meaning: feasible complete rosters for employee e
master weight of roster r for employee e
reduced cost of a roster column

children.title: Rostering Branch-Price Integration
children.top_down_role: Exact search architectures coupling roster pricing with branching.

knowledge_statements.title: Rostering Branch-Price Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-price integration for integer selection of complete roster columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each branch-and-bound node \(v\), augment the roster master with branching restrictions \(B_v\), solve its linear relaxation by column generation, and obtain bound \(z_v^{LP}\). Fathom \(v\) if its relaxation is infeasible, its bound cannot improve the incumbent, or its solution is integral. Otherwise choose a fractional roster-relevant decision, create child restrictions partitioning the integer solutions allowed at \(v\), and modify each pricing problem so that every generated roster satisfies the child restriction. Continue until no open node remains; return the best integral roster master solution found.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch-and-price embeds roster column generation at every search node while enforcing branching decisions inside subsequent pricing problems.
assumptions_latex: Every node relaxation and pricing problem is solved exactly.
Branching partitions the node's integer solutions without excluding any of them.
The integer roster solution set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon exhaustion of open nodes, the incumbent is optimal for the integer roster master problem.

notation.meaning: branching restrictions active at node v

children.title: Roster Pricing Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Resource-constrained pricing structures used to generate feasible roster columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Pricing Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost characterization of employee-roster pricing in a set-covering master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For employee \(e\), let a feasible roster \(r\in R_e\) have cost \(c_{er}\) and cover day-shift pair \((d,s)\) by \(a_{er,ds}\). Given master dual multipliers \(\pi_{ds}\) for coverage and \(\sigma_e\) for roster convexity, pricing solves
\[\rho_e=\min_{r\in R_e}\left(c_{er}-\sum_{d,s}\pi_{ds}a_{er,ds}-\sigma_e\right).\]
A roster attaining \(\rho_e<0\) is an improving master column. If \(\rho_e\ge0\) for every employee, no omitted column violates the corresponding dual constraint, so the restricted-master optimum equals the full-master linear optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An employee pricing problem minimizes roster reduced cost; a negative optimum yields a new column, while nonnegative optima certify full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an optimal primal-dual pair.
Pricing ranges over every feasible roster in \(R_e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negative \(\rho_e\) identifies an improving column; nonnegative \(\rho_e\) for all employees certifies full-master linear optimality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual pricing characterization fits the leaf and is internally consistent for an appropriate master convention, but no master formulation or source is supplied to establish the multiplier signs and rostering specialization.

children.title: Branch-Compatible Roster Representations
children.top_down_role: Representations whose pricing structure remains tractable under branching decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Compatible Roster Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring that master branching decisions remain enforceable by roster pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(v\), let \(\mathcal X_v\) be its set of feasible integer master solutions, and let \(\mathcal X_{v1},\ldots,\mathcal X_{vm}\) be the child solution sets induced by a branching disjunction. Let \(R_e\) be the feasible roster set for employee \(e\), with pricing-visible encoding \(\phi_e(r)\) for \(r\in R_e\). The representation is branch-compatible with this disjunction when \[\mathcal X_v=\mathop{\dot\bigcup}_{j=1}^m\mathcal X_{vj},\] and, for each child \(j\), the restrictions defining \(\mathcal X_{vj}\) induce enforceable admissibility conditions on every affected \(\phi_e(r)\), so pricing can generate only child-admissible columns without enumerating \(R_e\). For an additive path encoding, such a condition may be imposed through arc, shift, or assignment attributes already tracked by pricing, possibly after finite state augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A roster representation is branch-compatible when the child nodes partition the parent's integer solutions and every child restriction can be enforced directly in affected roster-pricing problems.
assumptions_latex: Each column encodes a complete feasible employee roster.
Pricing exposes, or can finitely augment its state to expose, every attribute used by the branching restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every column generated for child \(j\) satisfies that child's restrictions, while the child integer-solution sets collectively preserve every integer solution of the parent.

notation.meaning: integer master solutions feasible at node v
integer master solutions assigned to child j
feasible roster set for employee e

children.title: Roster Network Models
children.top_down_role: Network representations of shifts, duties, rest periods, plus roster transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Network Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclic state-transition network representation of a single employee's finite-horizon rosters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed acyclic graph layered by planning periods \(0,
1,\ldots,T\). A vertex \((t,q)\) records period \(t\) and sufficient roster state \(q\); an arc from layer \(t-1\) to \(t\) selects one shift or rest decision and updates the state. Designate source \(o\) and sink \(z\). If arcs are admitted exactly when the associated transition respects all local work rules, then every \(o\)-to-\(z\) path decodes to a feasible roster, and every feasible roster induces exactly one such path. Additive roster cost equals the sum of its path's arc costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A layered acyclic network represents roster decisions as arcs and feasible complete rosters as source-to-sink paths with additive costs.
assumptions_latex: The horizon \(T\) and state set are finite.
The state retains all history needed to test future work-rule transitions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible rosters and \(o\)-to-\(z\) paths are in cost-preserving bijection.
