children.title: Rostering Dynamic Programming
children.top_down_role: State-based optimization across roster construction horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Rostering Dynamic Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward dynamic programming on a finite roster-state transition system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_t\) be the reachable roster states after period \(t\), let \(U_t(q)\) be the admissible shift or rest decisions from state \(q\), and let \(F_t(q,u)\) and \(g_t(q,u)\) be the successor state and transition cost. Initialize \(V_0(q_0)=0\) and \(V_0(q)=+\infty\) otherwise. For \(t=1,\ldots,T\), compute
\[V_t(q')=\min\{V_{t-1}(q)+g_t(q,u):u\in U_t(q),\ F_t(q,u)=q'\}.\]
Store an attaining predecessor. Output a minimum-cost admissible terminal state and recover its roster by backtracking; report infeasibility if every terminal label is infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic programming propagates minimum costs across roster states period by period, then backtracks from the best admissible terminal state.
assumptions_latex: The horizon and reachable state sets are finite.
The state is sufficient for feasibility and additive future cost.
Transition costs are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backtracking an optimal terminal label returns a minimum-cost feasible roster, or infinite labels certify infeasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite deterministic recurrence and optimality conclusion are appropriately stated and the algorithm content kind fits, but no source supports the dynamic-programming principle or its rostering specialization.

children.title: Resource-Constrained Roster Paths
children.top_down_role: Path families encoding workload, legality, coverage, plus temporal resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Roster Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-feasible source-to-sink paths in a roster transition network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed roster network with source \(o\) and sink \(z\). Each arc \(a\in A\) has cost \(c_a\in\mathbb R\) and resource increment \(w_a\in\mathbb Z^m\). Given bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb Z^m\) with \(\ell\le u\), an \(o\)-to-\(z\) path \(P\) is resource-feasible when \[\ell\le \sum_{a\in P}w_a\le u\] holds componentwise and every state-dependent transition restriction encoded by \(G\) is satisfied. The resource-constrained roster-path problem is \[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in P}c_a:P\text{ is a resource-feasible }o\text{-to-}z\text{ path}\right\}.\] Resource components may represent total workload, weekends, duties, or other additive roster attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource-constrained roster path is a source-to-sink path whose total additive resource vector lies within its prescribed componentwise bounds and whose transitions satisfy the restrictions encoded by the network.
assumptions_latex: The roster network and resource dimension \(m\) are finite.
Resource accumulation is additive along arcs.
\(\ell,u\in\mathbb Z^m\) satisfy \(\ell\le u\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible solutions are precisely the \(o\)-to-\(z\) paths satisfying the componentwise total-resource bounds and all encoded transition restrictions.

notation.meaning: componentwise lower and upper bounds on total path resources

children.title: Roster State-Space Limits
children.top_down_role: State growth, resource dimensionality, plus dominance limitations.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster State-Space Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case state growth for exact dynamic programming with independently relevant roster resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an exact roster dynamic program whose state distinguishes the accumulated values of \(m\) integer resources, with resource \(j\) ranging over \(\{0,1,\ldots,U_j\}\). The direct product representation has at most
\[\prod_{j=1}^{m}(U_j+1)\]
resource states per time layer. This dependence is unavoidable for the representation in general: if every resource vector in the product set is reachable and two distinct vectors admit different feasible continuations, no exact state merging may identify them. In particular, \(m\) independently relevant binary resources yield \(2^m\) pairwise distinguishable states at one layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tracking independently relevant roster counters can require a product-sized state space, including exponentially many states in the number of binary resources.
assumptions_latex: The dynamic program explicitly records all \(m\) resource values.
Distinct resource vectors may have distinct feasible continuations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit resource-state count is bounded above by \(\prod_{j=1}^{m}(U_j+1)\), and instances can require all these states.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product upper bound is immediate for the stated explicit representation, but the worst-case necessity and pairwise-distinguishability claims are nontrivial complexity assertions without a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Programming for Rostering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain constraint-programming method for employee-shift roster feasibility and optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) and \(D\) be finite employee and day sets, and let the finite set \(S\) contain all shifts and an off-duty symbol. Introduce variables \(X_{ed}\in S\) for every \((e,d)\in E\times D\). Post constraints for daily coverage, employee qualifications, forbidden shift successions, run lengths, workload bounds, and fixed assignments. Let \(C(X)\) be their conjunction and let \(f:S^{E\times D}\to\mathbb R\) be a penalty function. Solve \[\min\{f(X):X\in S^{E\times D},\ C(X)=\mathrm{true}\}\] by repeatedly applying solution-preserving finite-domain propagation and performing complete search over the remaining domains. If search exhausts all nodes without a feasible assignment, report infeasibility; otherwise return the feasible assignment of minimum penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-programming rostering applies solution-preserving propagation and complete finite-domain search to employee-day shift variables, returning a minimum-penalty feasible roster or certifying infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(E\), \(D\), and \(S\) are finite.
Every posted propagator preserves every solution of its constraint.
The search explores the remaining finite domains completely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete optimization returns a minimum-penalty encoded roster when one exists and otherwise certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: shift assigned to employee e on day d

children.title: Rostering Local Search
children.top_down_role: Neighborhood-based improvement for personnel rosters.

assumptions_latex: The roster set \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
The objective \(F:X\to\mathbb{R}\) and neighborhood map \(N:X\rightrightarrows X\) are evaluable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned roster \(x^*\) satisfies \(F(x^*)\le F(y)\) for every \(y\in N(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of admissible or penalized rosters

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite deterministic descent with strict improvement and arbitrary tie-breaking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^0\in X\), set \(k=0\). At iteration \(k\), form the improving set \(I_k=\{y\in N(x^k):F(y)<F(x^k)\}\). If \(I_k=\varnothing\), stop and output \(x^*=x^k\). Otherwise choose any \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in I_k}F(y)\), increment \(k\), and repeat. Because \(X\) is finite and every accepted move strictly decreases \(F\), the procedure terminates after finitely many moves at a roster locally optimal with respect to \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly replace the roster by a strictly better neighbor. Finiteness guarantees termination at a roster having no improving neighbor.
knowledge_statements.title: Rostering Local Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite strict-descent algorithm and local-optimality conclusion are mathematically coherent and fit the leaf, but no inspectable domain-specific citation is supplied.

children.title: Rostering Metaheuristics
children.top_down_role: Higher-level search frameworks for diversified roster exploration.

assumptions_latex: The roster search space \(X\) is finite.
Each state records a current roster and any finite auxiliary memory required by the search rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The framework defines a roster metaheuristic whenever its acceptance, memory, diversification, and stopping rules are completely specified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract finite-state definition covering common trajectory-based roster metaheuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A roster metaheuristic is a finite-state search process with state \(s_k=(x_k,m_k)\), where \(x_k\in X\) is a roster and \(m_k\) is auxiliary memory. A generation rule produces candidates \(C(s_k)\subseteq X\); an acceptance rule selects \(x_{k+1}\in C(s_k)\cup\{x_k\}\), possibly using randomness; and a memory update sets \(m_{k+1}=U(s_k,x_{k+1})\). Unlike pure descent, acceptance may permit \(F(x_{k+1})\ge F(x_k)\). A specified stopping rule returns the best visited roster \(x^{\mathrm{best}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le j\le k}F(x_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A roster metaheuristic combines candidate generation, acceptance, memory, and stopping rules, possibly accepting nonimproving moves and returning the best visited roster.
knowledge_statements.title: Rostering Metaheuristics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is an unusually restrictive finite-state characterization of roster metaheuristics. An authoritative source is needed to support this boundary and distinguish it from ordinary local search.

children.title: Roster Neighborhood Families
children.top_down_role: Shift, assignment, sequence, block, plus ejection neighborhoods.

assumptions_latex: A roster is represented by an assignment matrix \(x\in X\subseteq\{0,1\}^{E\times T\times S}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each move family induces a neighborhood map \(N_M(x)=\{m(x):m\in M,\ m\text{ is applicable at }x\}\).

notation.meaning: Neighborhood induced by a move family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Move-induced neighborhoods for finite assignment-matrix rosters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A roster neighborhood family is a set \(M\) of partial maps \(m:X\rightharpoonup X\). Typical subfamilies are reassignment moves, which alter one employee-period assignment; swaps, which exchange two assignments; block moves, which replace assignments on a contiguous period set; and cyclic exchanges, which permute assignments among employees. For \(x\in X\), the induced neighborhood is \(N_M(x)=\{m(x):m\in M,\ x\in\operatorname{dom}(m)\}\). A move family is feasibility-preserving relative to \(X_F\subseteq X\) precisely when \(N_M(x)\subseteq X_F\) for every \(x\in X_F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A neighborhood family consists of applicable roster transformations, such as reassignments, swaps, blocks, or cycles, and maps each roster to its reachable neighbors.
knowledge_statements.title: Roster Neighborhood Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The move-induced neighborhood definition is coherent and appropriate for the leaf, but the roster-specific move taxonomy has no supporting citation.

children.title: Feasibility-Preserving Roster Search
children.top_down_role: Search restricted to moves that retain roster legality.

assumptions_latex: Hard roster constraints define \(X_F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\le 0\text{ for all }j\in H\}\).
The initial roster satisfies \(x^0\in X_F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every generated roster remains in \(X_F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant characterization for searches that never leave hard feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A roster search is feasibility-preserving if its initialization and transition rules satisfy \(x^0\in X_F\) and \(N(x)\subseteq X_F\) for every \(x\in X_F\). Equivalently, every accepted transition \(x^{k+1}\in N(x^k)\) preserves all inequalities \(g_j(x^{k+1})\le 0\) for \(j\in H\). By induction over the iteration index, these conditions imply \(x^k\in X_F\) for every generated iterate \(k\). The condition restricts hard constraints only; soft-constraint violations may still be represented in the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a hard-feasible roster and permit only moves whose endpoints are hard feasible; then every search iterate remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Roster Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Moreover, requiring the entire neighborhood to lie in the feasible set is stronger than requiring only accepted transitions to preserve feasibility, so the asserted equivalence depends on how N is defined.

children.title: Penalty-Guided Roster Search
children.top_down_role: Search across controlled infeasibility using violation penalties.

assumptions_latex: The finite roster space is \(X\), with base cost \(c:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
Each constraint violation measure satisfies \(v_j:X\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), and each penalty weight satisfies \(\lambda_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, the output is locally optimal for the current penalized objective \(F_\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-penalty neighborhood descent over feasible and infeasible rosters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F_\lambda(x)=c(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{q}\lambda_jv_j(x)\). Initialize \(x^0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in N(x^k)}F_\lambda(y)\). If \(F_\lambda(y_k)<F_\lambda(x^k)\), set \(x^{k+1}=y_k\) and continue; otherwise stop and return \(x^*=x^k\). The violation terms allow comparison of infeasible rosters, while the weights determine the tradeoff between base cost and violations. On termination, \(F_\lambda(x^*)\le F_\lambda(y)\) for every \(y\in N(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize base cost plus weighted violation measures over roster neighborhoods, stopping when no neighbor improves the current penalized objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Guided Roster Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-penalty descent scheme fits the algorithm leaf, but argmin over N(x^k) is undefined when the neighborhood is empty. A source and an explicit empty-neighborhood rule or nonemptiness assumption are required.

children.title: Hybrid Rostering Solvers
children.top_down_role: Rostering architectures combining complementary optimization paradigms.

assumptions_latex: A roster model has decision set \(X\), constraints \(C\), and objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
At least two distinct solver components exchange mathematically defined information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The composite procedure is a hybrid rostering solver when the exchanged information can alter a component's subsequent search or model.

notation.meaning: Information passed from component i to component j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition based on coupled, heterogeneous optimization components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid rostering solver is a composite algorithm \(A=(A_1,\ldots,A_p)\), with \(p\ge2\), in which distinct components solve or search representations of the roster problem and exchange information \(I_{i\to j}\). Such information may be variable assignments, bounds, cuts, columns, penalties, conflicts, or incumbent rosters. The coupling is substantive when some received \(I_{i\to j}\) changes the feasible region, objective, branching, propagation, neighborhood, or stopping test of \(A_j\). Merely running independent solvers and selecting the best output is not hybridization under this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid rostering solver couples distinct optimization components through information that changes at least one component's subsequent model or search.
knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Rostering Solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The operational definition fits the leaf, but its substantive-coupling criterion and exclusion of independent portfolios are taxonomy choices requiring an authoritative hybrid-rostering source.

children.title: Roster Decomposition Methods
children.top_down_role: Partitioning by employees, periods, skills, units, or decision layers.

assumptions_latex: Roster variables are partitioned as \(x=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(p)},z)\).
Block \(i\) has local feasible set \(X_i(z)\) and local cost \(f_i(x^{(i)},z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The roster problem is represented as a coupling problem in \(z\) with conditionally independent block subproblems.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of block i at fixed coupling variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable decomposition with shared coupling decisions and separable conditional subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), define \(\phi_i(z)=\min\{f_i(x^{(i)},z):x^{(i)}\in X_i(z)\}\), with value \(+\infty\) when \(X_i(z)=\varnothing\). If all cross-block constraints are expressed through \(z\), then the original roster optimization admits the representation \[\min_{z\in Z}\left\{f_0(z)+\sum_{i=1}^{p}\phi_i(z)\right\}.\] Fixing \(z\) separates the block calculations, while optimization over \(z\) coordinates shared staffing, coverage, or employee decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition roster decisions into blocks linked by shared variables; fixing the shared variables yields independent subproblems whose values define a coordinating problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Roster Decomposition Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separable value-function representation is mathematically plausible and the representation kind fits, but no source supports its application as a roster decomposition method.

children.title: Constraint–Programming Rostering Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Integration of constraint propagation with mathematical or heuristic search.

assumptions_latex: The roster model has finite-domain variables \(x\), CP constraints \(C\), and objective \(f(x)\).
A companion optimizer or neighborhood generator can impose additional restrictions \(R_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The best returned feasible roster has objective no worse than any accepted incumbent encountered by the hybrid.

notation.meaning: Iteration-specific restrictions supplied by another component

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative hybrid using CP propagation and externally generated restricted searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an incumbent \(\bar x_0\) as absent or CP-feasible. At iteration \(k\), a companion component constructs restrictions \(R_k\), such as fixed assignments, objective bounds, or a neighborhood around \(\bar x_k\). Invoke CP propagation and search on \(C\cup R_k\). If this call returns a feasible roster \(x_k\) and either no incumbent exists or \(f(x_k)<f(\bar x_k)\), set \(\bar x_{k+1}=x_k\); otherwise retain \(\bar x_{k+1}=\bar x_k\). Update the companion component with CP conflicts, bounds, or the incumbent, and stop under a specified iteration, time, or optimality criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate externally restricted roster searches with CP propagation, feeding incumbents, conflicts, or bounds between components and retaining the best feasible roster.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint–Programming Rostering Hybrids

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The iterative CP-hybrid template fits the algorithm leaf, but it does not guarantee that any feasible incumbent exists at termination despite referring to the best returned feasible roster. A supporting source and explicit output condition are needed.

children.title: Master–Subproblem Rostering
children.top_down_role: Rostering structures divided between coordinating masters plus specialized subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The master variables satisfy \(z\in Z\), and the recourse variables satisfy \(y\in Y(z)\).
The objective is \(c(z)+q(y,z)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon finite termination with matching valid lower and upper bounds, the incumbent is globally optimal for the decomposed model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact master-subproblem scheme requiring valid cuts and bound convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Q(z)=\min\{q(y,z):y\in Y(z)\}\), with \(Q(z)=+\infty\) when the subproblem is infeasible. Initialize a master relaxation of \(\min_{z\in Z}c(z)+Q(z)\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master for \(z_k\), then solve the subproblem defining \(Q(z_k)\). If infeasible, add a valid feasibility cut excluding \(z_k\) or a certified infeasible region. If feasible, update the incumbent and add a valid optimality cut underestimating \(Q\). Repeat until the master lower bound equals the incumbent upper bound, then return the incumbent roster.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master chooses coordinating decisions; a roster subproblem tests and prices them, adding valid feasibility or optimality cuts until bounds meet.
knowledge_statements.title: Master–Subproblem Rostering

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The master–subproblem scheme is plausible, but the conditions under which globally valid feasibility and optimality cuts exist and yield valid bounds are not specified or cited.

children.title: Decomposition Coupling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cross-partition dependencies that weaken or obstruct rostering decomposition.

assumptions_latex: A decomposition retains only boundary variables \(z\) between blocks.
Two distinct global roster states induce the same boundary value \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No exact coordination rule depending only on \(z\) can distinguish those states when their feasible completions or costs differ.

notation.meaning: Information retained at the decomposition boundary
Feasible completions associated with a global state
Optimal completion value for a global state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-loss boundary for exact decomposition coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_1
e s_2\) be global partial-roster states with identical retained boundary information \(z(s_1)=z(s_2)\). If either \(Y(s_1)
e Y(s_2)\) or \(Q(s_1)
e Q(s_2)\), then \(z\) is not a sufficient coupling description. Indeed, any master cut, price, or decision rule expressed solely as a function of \(z\) assigns the same coordination information to both states, although their feasible completions or optimal completion values differ. Exact decomposition therefore requires enriching the boundary information or retaining the omitted cross-block constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling boundary is insufficient when different global states look identical at the boundary but have different feasible completions or completion costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Coupling Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-loss observation fits a failure-boundary leaf, but the conclusion about exact coordination requires a precise definition of exactness and evidence that the differing completions or values must be distinguished.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: A Classification Scheme for Integrated Staff Rostering and Scheduling Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Staff rostering, job scheduling, assignment, integration, and complexity
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: A Classification Scheme for Integrated Staff Rostering and Scheduling Problems

children.title: Staffing Requirement Design
children.top_down_role: Workforce quantities, skill mixes, plus temporal staffing profiles.

assumptions_latex: Demand is indexed by periods \(t\in T\) and skills \(s\in S\).
Each admissible shift type \(q\in Q\) contributes coverage coefficient \(a_{tsq}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A staffing design is adequate exactly when its induced coverage meets every requirement \(r_{ts}\).

notation.meaning: Required staffing for period t and skill s
Number of planned duties of shift type q
Coverage supplied by one duty of type q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic integer staffing design from period-skill requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A staffing requirement design consists of nonnegative requirements \(r=(r_{ts})_{t\in T,s\in S}\) and nonnegative integer duty counts \(n=(n_q)_{q\in Q}\). Its induced coverage is \(c_{ts}(n)=\sum_{q\in Q}a_{tsq}n_q\). The design is adequate when \(c_{ts}(n)\ge r_{ts}\) for every \((t,s)\in T\times S\). Given duty costs \(d_q\), a minimum-cost staffing design solves \[\min_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^{Q}}\left\{\sum_{q\in Q}d_qn_q:c_{ts}(n)\ge r_{ts}\ \text{for all }(t,s)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose integer counts of shift types so their period-skill coverage meets prescribed staffing requirements, optionally at minimum duty cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Staffing Requirement Design

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coverage formulation is standard, but the record conflates staffing requirements r with the duty-count design n and then adds a minimum-cost optimization model. A rostering or staffing source is needed to establish the intended leaf boundary.

children.title: Roster Construction Under Staffing Targets
children.top_down_role: Individual roster formation subject to aggregate staffing targets.

assumptions_latex: Binary variable \(x_{etq}\) indicates assignment of employee \(e\) to shift type \(q\) in period \(t\).
The hard-feasible roster set is \(X_F\), and staffing targets are \(r_{ts}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either meets all staffing targets or minimizes the specified weighted shortfall among hard-feasible rosters.

notation.meaning: Coverage delivered for period t and skill s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard-feasible roster construction with explicit target shortfalls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \((t,s)\), define delivered coverage \(c_{ts}(x)\) from qualified assignments and introduce \(u_{ts}\ge0\) satisfying \(c_{ts}(x)+u_{ts}\ge r_{ts}\). Given roster cost \(f(x)\) and positive shortfall weights \(w_{ts}\), solve lexicographically: first minimize \(\sum_{t,s}w_{ts}u_{ts}\) over \(x\in X_F\), then minimize \(f(x)\) over solutions attaining the minimum shortfall. Return the resulting \(x^*\). If a hard-feasible roster meeting every target exists, the first-stage optimum is zero and \(c_{ts}(x^*)\ge r_{ts}\) for all \((t,s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct a hard-feasible roster by first minimizing weighted staffing shortfalls and then minimizing roster cost among the best-covered solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Roster Construction Under Staffing Targets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lexicographic shortfall formulation is coherent and fits the algorithm leaf, but delivered coverage is only described informally rather than defined from x, qualifications, and shift coverage, and no source is supplied.

children.title: Staffing–Roster Coupling
children.top_down_role: Cross-layer dependencies linking workforce levels to roster feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Staffing–Roster Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint finite-horizon model linking aggregate staffing requirements to individual roster decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite employee set, \(T\) a finite set of periods, and \(x_{et}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether employee \(e\) works in period \(t\). Let \(r_t\in\mathbb Z_+\) be the staffing requirement and \(c_t(x)=\sum_{e\in E}x_{et}\) the realized coverage. Staffing and rostering are coupled by \[r_t\le c_t(x)\quad(t\in T),\qquad x_e=(x_{et})_{t\in T}\in X_e\quad(e\in E),\] where \(X_e\) contains the legal individual work patterns. In an integrated formulation, both \(r\) and \(x\) are decision variables and the objective may penalize staffing cost, roster cost, and deviations \(c_t(x)-r_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate staffing levels and individual rosters are coupled when roster coverage must meet jointly chosen staffing requirements while every employee follows a legal work pattern.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(T\) are finite.
\(X_e\subseteq\{0,1\}^{T}\) is the legal-pattern set for employee \(e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_t\le\sum_{e\in E}x_{et}\) for every \(t\in T\), with \(x_e\in X_e\) for every \(e\in E\).

notation.meaning: Binary work indicator for employee e in period t.
Legal roster-pattern set for employee e.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical finite-horizon coverage formulation for integrated staffing and personnel rostering
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the coupling leaf, but no domain source supports it, and jointly optimized staffing requirements need an admissible requirement set or demand constraints to avoid a degenerate zero-requirement interpretation.

children.title: Coverage Feedback Across Planning Layers
children.top_down_role: Information exchange between staffing design plus roster realization.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Feedback Across Planning Layers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative feedback of roster coverage deficits to an aggregate staffing layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given initial requirements \(r^0\in\mathbb Z_+^T\), set \(k=0\). At iteration \(k\), solve the rostering problem over legal rosters \(x_e\in X_e\), obtaining coverage \(c_t^k=\sum_{e\in E}x_{et}^k\). Compute deficits \(d_t^k=(r_t^k-c_t^k)_+\). If \(d^k=0\), return \((r^k,x^k)\). Otherwise the staffing layer revises its targets by a prescribed map \[r^{k+1}=F(r^k,d^k),\] and the roster is reconstructed. Stop with failure if no revision is admissible or a stated iteration limit is reached. The map \(F\), rather than this template alone, determines convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly construct a roster, measure coverage deficits, and return them to the staffing layer until all targets are covered or revision becomes impossible.
assumptions_latex: Each rostering subproblem is solved or declared infeasible.
The revision map \(F\) preserves the admissible staffing set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On successful termination, \(\sum_{e\in E}x_{et}^k\ge r_t^k\) for all \(t\in T\).

notation.meaning: Roster coverage in period t at iteration k.
Positive coverage deficit in period t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic decomposition template with explicit deficit feedback
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the feedback leaf, and successful termination implies the stated coverage condition. A source is required for this particular cross-layer template; without a specified revision map, it carries no convergence claim.

children.title: Duty Construction
children.top_down_role: Formation of legal work duties from tasks, trips, shifts, or activities.

knowledge_statements.title: Duty Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction of legal single-worker duties from elementary work pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite set of work pieces, each with a time interval, location, and required qualification. A duty is a sequence \(d=(j_1,\ldots,j_q)\) of distinct elements of \(J\) assigned to one worker such that consecutive pieces are temporally compatible, required travel or transition times are respected, the worker qualification covers every piece, and all prescribed limits on duty span, work duration, breaks, and piece count hold. A duty-construction model selects or generates members of the resulting feasible set \(D\), optionally minimizing a duty cost \(c_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A duty is a one-worker sequence of work pieces satisfying temporal, transition, qualification, break, duration, and span rules.
assumptions_latex: Every work piece has specified temporal and resource attributes.
All duty rules are represented by decidable predicates on finite sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D=\{d:\ d\text{ satisfies every prescribed duty-feasibility predicate}\}\).

notation.meaning: Finite set of elementary work pieces.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard set-partitioning interpretation of duty generation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches duty construction and is internally coherent, but the domain-specific collection of feasibility rules has no cited source.

children.title: Roster Assembly from Duties
children.top_down_role: Allocation plus sequencing of constructed duties across personnel rosters.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster Assembly from Duties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-partitioning representation of multi-period rosters assembled from feasible duties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a finite pool of feasible duties and \(a_{jd}=1\) when duty \(d\) covers work piece \(j\). Let \(y_{ed}\in\{0,1\}\) assign duty \(d\) to employee \(e\), and let \(R_e\subseteq\{0,1\}^{D}\) encode rest, succession, qualification, and workload rules. A roster assembled from duties satisfies \[y_e\in R_e\quad(e\in E),\qquad \sum_{e\in E}\sum_{d\in D}a_{jd}y_{ed}=1\quad(j\in J),\] with equality replaceable by a required coverage bound when work pieces may receive multiple workers. Thus each employee receives a compatible duty pattern and all work is covered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign feasible duties to employees so each employee’s duty pattern is legal and every work piece receives its required coverage.
assumptions_latex: The duty pool \(D\) is finite.
Each incidence coefficient \(a_{jd}\) is known.
Every employee-specific legal pattern is represented by \(R_e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_e\in R_e\) for all \(e\in E\) and \(\sum_{e,d}a_{jd}y_{ed}=1\) for all \(j\in J\).

notation.meaning: Incidence of work piece j in duty d.
Binary assignment of duty d to employee e.
Legal duty-pattern set for employee e.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits roster assembly from duties. A personnel-scheduling source is needed to support the employee-indexed pattern formulation and the stated exact-versus-multiple coverage convention.

children.title: Duty–Roster Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependencies between duty composition choices plus downstream roster feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Duty–Roster Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated formulation in which duty generation and roster assembly share coverage decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_d\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that candidate duty \(d\) is admitted and \(y_{ed}\in\{0,1\}\) assign it to employee \(e\). Duty construction and roster assembly are coupled by \[y_{ed}\le z_d\quad(e\in E,d\in D),\qquad \sum_{e\in E}y_{ed}\le z_d\quad(d\in D),\] together with duty-feasibility constraints defining admissible \(z\), employee pattern constraints \(y_e\in R_e\), and work-coverage constraints \(\sum_{e,d}a_{jd}y_{ed}=1\). If reusable duty templates are allowed, the second inequality is replaced by an appropriate multiplicity bound. The integrated objective may contain both construction and roster-assignment costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duty-selection variables and employee assignments are linked so only constructed duties can enter legal employee rosters that cover all work.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a finite candidate-duty universe.
Each selected duty is usable by at most one employee unless an explicit multiplicity is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_{ed}\le z_d\), \(y_e\in R_e\), and \(\sum_{e,d}a_{jd}y_{ed}=1\) hold on every feasible integrated solution.

notation.meaning: Binary admission indicator for duty d.
Binary assignment of duty d to employee e.
Coverage incidence of work piece j by duty d.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linking-variable formulation for integrated duty construction and roster assembly
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linking representation fits the coupling leaf, but its at-most-one-use constraint depends on a duty-instance interpretation. A source must establish that convention or specify reusable-template multiplicities.

children.title: Duty Pool Adequacy
children.top_down_role: Coverage, compatibility, plus diversity limits of candidate duty pools.

knowledge_statements.title: Duty Pool Adequacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility condition requiring the generated duty pool to support a legal complete roster.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a work-piece set \(J\), employees \(E\), duty pool \(D\), coverage incidences \(a_{jd}\), and employee pattern sets \(R_e\), the pool \(D\) is roster-adequate if and only if there exist binary assignments \(y_{ed}\) satisfying \[y_e\in R_e\quad(e\in E),\qquad \sum_{e\in E}\sum_{d\in D}a_{jd}y_{ed}\ge b_j\quad(j\in J),\] where \(b_j\in\mathbb Z_+\) is required coverage, together with any prescribed upper bounds preventing impermissible duplicate coverage. Adequacy is therefore stronger than requiring each work piece to occur in at least one duty: the covering duties must be jointly roster-compatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A duty pool is adequate exactly when its duties can be assigned jointly into legal employee patterns while meeting every work-piece coverage requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(D\), \(E\), and \(J\) are finite.
\(b_j\) and \(a_{jd}\) are nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is adequate exactly when the displayed binary feasibility system has a solution.

notation.meaning: Required coverage multiplicity of work piece j.
Coverage multiplicity supplied by duty d to work piece j.
Legal duty-pattern set for employee e.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasibility-based adequacy predicate for a restricted duty pool
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate and the feasibility-based adequacy definition is precise, including joint roster compatibility. It lacks a domain-specific source.

children.title: Job Scheduling Layer
children.top_down_role: Timing plus sequencing of jobs requiring personnel participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Job Scheduling Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational layer assigning start times and resource-compatible execution modes to jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite job set. Each job \(j\) has processing time \(p_j>0\), an admissible start-time set \(W_j\), and a required skill or resource class. The job-scheduling layer chooses start times \(s_j\in W_j\) and, where applicable, execution modes so that precedence constraints satisfy \(s_i+p_i\le s_j\), incompatible jobs do not overlap on a shared-capacity resource, and all release-date and deadline restrictions hold. Its output is a temporally feasible job plan and the induced time-dependent demand for qualified personnel, which becomes input to or is jointly constrained by the rostering layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The job layer times jobs subject to precedence, time-window, and capacity rules and thereby determines when qualified personnel are needed.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and every \(p_j\) is positive.
Precedence, time-window, and resource-capacity data are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected \((s_j)_{j\in J}\) satisfies every job-level temporal and capacity constraint.

notation.meaning: Admissible start-time set of job j.

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Lawler's cited project-scheduling section may support precedence scheduling, but the record additionally asserts shared-capacity, qualification, execution-mode, and personnel-demand interfaces not supported by the supplied locator. A domain source is required.

children.title: Personnel Rostering Layer
children.top_down_role: Assignment of work periods to personnel across the planning horizon.

knowledge_statements.title: Personnel Rostering Layer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layer assigning qualified employees to work periods induced by a job schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite employee set and \(T\) a finite time discretization. For fixed personnel demand \(q_{kt}\) of skill class \(k\) in period \(t\), the personnel-rostering layer chooses \(x_{et}\in\{0,1\}\) and, if needed, job-assignment variables. It enforces \[\sum_{e\in E_k}x_{et}\ge q_{kt}\quad(k,t),\qquad x_e\in X_e\quad(e\in E),\] where \(E_k\) contains employees qualified for class \(k\) and \(X_e\) represents availability, rest, workload, and sequence rules. The output is a legal roster capable of supplying the personnel demanded by the job schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rostering layer assigns qualified employees over time so job-induced skill demands are covered and every employee follows a legal pattern.
assumptions_latex: \(E\), \(T\), and the skill-class set are finite.
Demand \(q_{kt}\) and qualification sets \(E_k\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{e\in E_k}x_{et}\ge q_{kt}\) for every \((k,t)\), with \(x_e\in X_e\) for every \(e\).

notation.meaning: Required personnel of skill class k in period t.
Employees qualified for skill class k.
Legal roster-pattern set for employee e.

children.title: Job–Roster Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependencies linking job timing, skill demand, plus personnel availability.

knowledge_statements.title: Job–Roster Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated constraints linking scheduled job execution to qualified employee availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_{jt}(s)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that job \(j\), under schedule \(s\), executes during period \(t\). Let \(z_{ej}\in\{0,1\}\) assign employee \(e\) to job \(j\), and let \(x_{et}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate rostered availability. Job scheduling and rostering are coupled by \[z_{ej}u_{jt}(s)\le x_{et}\quad(e,j,t),\qquad \sum_{e\in Q_j}z_{ej}=m_j\quad(j\in J),\] where \(Q_j\) is the qualified employee set and \(m_j\) the required crew size. Job-level feasibility constraints on \(s\) and employee-level legality constraints on \(x\) complete the integrated model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A job may use an employee only while that employee is rostered, and each scheduled job must receive its required qualified crew.
assumptions_latex: Time is represented by a finite period set.
Each job has a specified qualified set \(Q_j\) and crew size \(m_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every executing job is staffed by \(m_j\) qualified employees who are rostered throughout its execution.

notation.meaning: Indicator that scheduled job j executes in period t.
Assignment of employee e to job j.
Rostered availability of employee e in period t.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard time-indexed linking formulation for scheduling and workforce assignment

children.title: Shared Temporal Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of job schedules with work limits, shifts, plus rest requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Temporal Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for job execution periods and employee roster availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a finite set of periods, let \(I_j(s)\subseteq T\) be the set of periods during which job \(j\in J\) executes under schedule \(s\), let \(A_e(x)\subseteq T\) be the availability set of employee \(e\in E\) under roster \(x\), and let \(z_{ej}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate assignment of employee \(e\) to job \(j\). Shared temporal feasibility holds if and only if \[z_{ej}=1\implies I_j(s)\subseteq A_e(x)\qquad(e\in E,\ j\in J),\] every job receives its required number of qualified assigned employees, and no employee is assigned to distinct jobs whose execution-period sets overlap. This condition assumes nonpreemptive jobs with fixed assigned employees and excludes partial roster overlap unless preemption or employee substitution is explicitly permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assigned employees must be rostered throughout every execution period of each job, satisfy its qualifications, and never serve jobs with overlapping execution periods.
assumptions_latex: \(E\), \(J\), and \(T\) are finite.
Jobs are nonpreemptive and require fixed assigned employees throughout execution.
Employee substitution is not permitted during a job.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{ej}=1\) implies \(I_j(s)\subseteq A_e(x)\), with qualification, crew-size, and nonoverlap conditions satisfied.

notation.meaning: Periods during which job j executes under schedule s.
Periods when employee e is rostered as available.

children.title: Integrated Roster Design
children.top_down_role: Construction of personnel work patterns within the integrated problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Roster Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roster design anticipating downstream task assignments and routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite employee set, \(T\) a finite period set, and \(K\) a finite task set. Integrated roster design chooses \(x_{et}\in\{0,1\}\) jointly with task assignments \(z_{ek}\in\{0,1\}\) and route variables \(w\). Feasibility requires \(x_e\in X_e\), every assigned task to occur while its qualified employee is rostered, and \(w\) to form temporally feasible routes containing the assigned tasks. Thus a roster is integrated-feasible only if it admits at least one compatible downstream pair \((z,w)\): \[x\in X^{\mathrm{int}}\iff x_e\in X_e\ (e\in E)\ \text{and}\ \exists(z,w)\in Y(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integrated roster is legal at the employee level and admits compatible task assignments and temporally feasible routes.
assumptions_latex: \(E\), \(T\), and \(K\) are finite.
The downstream feasibility set \(Y(x)\) explicitly represents assignment and routing constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in X^{\mathrm{int}}\) exactly when \(x_e\in X_e\) for all \(e\) and \(Y(x)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Rostered work indicator for employee e in period t.
Assignment indicator for employee e and task k.
Assignments and routes feasible under roster x.

children.title: Integrated Task Assignment
children.top_down_role: Matching personnel or crews to tasks under roster restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Task Assignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assignment model constrained simultaneously by roster availability and route realizability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a finite employee set and \(K\) a finite task set. For a roster \(x\), let \(z_{ek}\in\{0,1\}\) assign task \(k\) to employee \(e\). Integrated task assignment satisfies \[\sum_{e\in Q_k}z_{ek}=1\quad(k\in K),\qquad z_{ek}\le a_{ek}(x)\quad(e,k),\] where \(Q_k\) is the qualified set and \(a_{ek}(x)=1\) only if employee \(e\) is rostered throughout task \(k\)'s admissible service time. In addition, for each employee, the assigned task set must admit a route satisfying travel-time, task-window, and shift-boundary constraints. Assignment is therefore feasible only through both roster and routing layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each task is assigned to one qualified, roster-available employee whose assigned tasks can be joined into a feasible route.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(K\) are finite.
Each task has specified qualification, service-time, location, and time-window data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every task has one qualified roster-compatible assignee, and each employee's assigned tasks admit a feasible route.

notation.meaning: Binary assignment of task k to employee e.
Roster compatibility of employee e with task k.

children.title: Integrated Route Construction
children.top_down_role: Spatial sequencing of assigned service or transportation tasks.

knowledge_statements.title: Integrated Route Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint routing representation conditional on roster and task-assignment decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let workers be indexed by \(i\in I\), tasks by \(j\in J\), and feasible travel arcs by \((u,v)\in A_i\). Variables \(r_{it}\in\{0,1\}\), \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), and \(y_{iuv}\in\{0,1\}\) denote availability, assignment, and route-arc use. Integrated route construction imposes flow conservation at every task, \[\sum_{u:(u,j)\in A_i}y_{iuj}=x_{ij}=\sum_{v:(j,v)\in A_i}y_{ijv},\] together with depot flow, subtour elimination, and time-feasibility constraints. Moreover, \(x_{ij}\le r_{i,t(j)}\) requires every visited task to be assigned to an available worker. A feasible solution therefore constructs routes consistent with both roster and assignment layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routes must visit exactly the tasks assigned to each worker, respect depot and connectivity rules, and schedule every visit during that worker’s rostered availability.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite.
Each task has a specified service time and time requirement.
Travel arcs and travel times are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected route arcs form worker routes compatible with roster availability and task assignments.

notation.meaning: worker i is rostered in period t
task j is assigned to worker i

children.title: Roster–Assignment Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependencies between personnel availability plus task allocation.

knowledge_statements.title: Roster–Assignment Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition linking roster availability to task assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_{it}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether worker \(i\) is rostered in period \(t\), and let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether task \(j\), requiring period set \(T_j\), is assigned to worker \(i\). Roster–assignment coupling is enforced by \[x_{ij}\le r_{it}\qquad\text{for every }i\in I,\ j\in J,\ t\in T_j.\] If partial coverage is permitted, the binary inequality is replaced by \(x_{ij}a_{jt}\le r_{it}\), where \(a_{jt}\) indicates that task \(j\) occupies period \(t\). Thus an assignment is feasible only when its worker is rostered throughout every required period.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A task may be assigned to a worker only if that worker is rostered during every period occupied by the task.
assumptions_latex: Roster and assignment decisions use a common finite time index.
Each task’s required periods are known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{ij}=1\) implies \(r_{it}=1\) for every \(t\in T_j\).
review_flags: Standard coupling predicate, but the supplied source inventory does not directly support integrated personnel scheduling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the Roster–Assignment Coupling leaf, but no source is cited. The partial-coverage sentence does not actually replace the preceding constraint: when a_{jt}=1 it is the same inequality, and when a_{jt}=0 it is vacuous. The sets I and J and the indicator a_{jt} are also not fully introduced in the statement.

children.title: Assignment–Route Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependencies between task ownership plus route feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Assignment–Route Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linking condition between worker-task assignments and route visits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) assign task \(j\) to worker \(i\), and let \(y_{iuv}\in\{0,1\}\) select directed route arc \((u,v)\) for that worker. Exact assignment–route coupling requires \[\sum_{u:(u,j)\in A_i}y_{iuj}=x_{ij}=\sum_{v:(j,v)\in A_i}y_{ijv}\qquad(i\in I,\ j\in J).\] Consequently, every assigned task has exactly one incoming and one outgoing selected arc on its assignee’s route, while an unassigned task has neither. Depot-balance and subtour-elimination constraints remain necessary to turn these local degree conditions into complete connected routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker’s route enters and leaves a task exactly once if and only if that task is assigned to the worker.
assumptions_latex: Each task is represented by one routing vertex.
Selected routes are directed.
Separate constraints enforce depot balance and connectivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A task is visited by worker \(i\) exactly when \(x_{ij}=1\).
review_flags: The exact coupling is standard, but no supplied locator directly covers assignment-routing integration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the Assignment–Route Coupling leaf, and the local degree equations are coherent under the stated vertex model. However, no inspectable source is supplied for this exact assignment-routing linkage, so its intended scope and assumptions cannot be certified.

children.title: Three-Layer Coordination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sequential, iterative, plus jointly optimized integration structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Layer Coordination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified feasible-set representation for roster, assignment, and routing layers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\), \(X\), and \(Y\) be the roster, assignment, and routing feasible sets, and let \(C_{RX}\) and \(C_{XY}\) denote their coupling predicates. The fully coordinated three-layer regime has feasible set \[\mathcal F=\{(r,x,y):r\in R,\ x\in X,\ y\in Y,\ C_{RX}(r,x),\ C_{XY}(x,y)\}.\] A sequential regime instead selects \(r\), then optimizes \(x\) conditional on \(r\), and finally optimizes \(y\) conditional on \(x\); a partially integrated regime jointly optimizes two adjacent layers and passes their decisions to the third. These regimes are equivalent only when the sequential choices retain an extension attaining a global optimum of \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three-layer coordination may optimize roster, assignment, and routing jointly, sequentially, or in adjacent pairs; sequential optimization is globally exact only under an extension condition.
assumptions_latex: Each layer has a well-defined feasible set.
Cross-layer feasibility is expressed by adjacent coupling predicates.
All regimes use the same global objective when compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint coordination optimizes over \(\mathcal F\); sequential coordination is exact only if its fixed decisions extend to a global optimum in \(\mathcal F\).
review_flags: Coordination-regime terminology and decomposition assumptions require a dedicated integrated scheduling source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is appropriate for the Three-Layer Coordination Regimes leaf, but no source supports the regime taxonomy. The displayed set defines feasibility only, while the claimed equivalence and global optimality condition require an explicitly defined common objective and precise optimization rules for each sequential or partially integrated regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Time-Indexed Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon scheduling representation on a uniform discrete time grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\), and let \(x_{jt}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that nonpreemptive job \(j\) starts at grid time \(t\). With integer processing duration \(p_j\), the constraints \[\sum_{t=0}^{H-p_j}x_{jt}=1\qquad(j\in J)\] enforce one start per job. For a unit-capacity resource, nonoverlap is represented by \[\sum_{j\in J}\sum_{t:\,t\le \tau<t+p_j}x_{jt}\le1\qquad(\tau\in T).\] Release dates, deadlines, precedence relations, and resource demands are imposed by restricting admissible start indices or adding corresponding linear inequalities. The representation is exact only relative to the chosen grid and horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary variables select each job’s grid-aligned start time, while period-wise capacity inequalities prevent overlapping resource use within the finite horizon.
assumptions_latex: Processing times and admissible start times are integral grid multiples.
Jobs are nonpreemptive.
The horizon contains every permitted completion time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible binary solutions encode exactly the grid-aligned schedules satisfying the stated temporal and capacity constraints.

notation.meaning: job j starts at time index t

source_refs.locator: Section 9.7. Flows Over Time p. 236

children.title: Event-Based Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Scheduling representations indexed by ordered events or event positions.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Based Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling representation indexed by ordered events rather than fixed time periods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) be ordered event positions with event times \(\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_K\). Binary variables \(z_{je}\) assign each job \(j\) to one event, so \(\sum_{e\in E}z_{je}=1\). If job \(j\) starts at its assigned event and has duration \(p_j\), its start time satisfies \[s_j=\sum_{e\in E}\theta_e z_{je},\qquad C_j=s_j+p_j.\] Resource and precedence constraints link assignments and event times, commonly through valid linearizations. A model is complete when \(K\) is large enough that every feasible schedule admits an order-preserving assignment of its relevant start or completion occurrences to events.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jobs are assigned to ordered event positions whose times are decision variables, replacing a fixed time grid with a finite sequence of schedule events.
assumptions_latex: The event set is finite and linearly ordered.
Each represented job occurrence is assigned to one event.
Required products of binary and continuous variables are validly linearized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible model solution determines event times and a schedule consistent with the event assignments.
review_flags: Event-based formulations differ substantially across scheduling domains; no direct locator was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Event-Based Scheduling Models, but no source is supplied and event semantics vary materially across formulations. The equality s_j=sum_e theta_e z_{je} is bilinear rather than a linear scheduling constraint, and merely referring to unspecified valid linearizations is insufficient to certify the represented feasible set or the completeness claim.

children.title: Start-Time Scheduling Models
children.top_down_role: Scheduling representations centered on activity start-time variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Start-Time Scheduling Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous or discrete formulation centered on explicit job start-time variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each nonpreemptive job \(j\in J\), introduce a start variable \(s_j\) and define completion by \(C_j=s_j+p_j\). Release dates and deadlines impose \(s_j\ge r_j\) and \(C_j\le d_j\). A precedence arc \((i,j)\) imposes \(s_j\ge C_i\). For two jobs sharing a unary resource, a binary order variable \(q_{ij}\) and a valid upper bound \(M\) may enforce \[s_j\ge C_i-M(1-q_{ij}),\qquad s_i\ge C_j-Mq_{ij}.\] Together with assignment and resource constraints, these inequalities represent feasible start-time schedules without enumerating every time point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each job receives an explicit start time; temporal bounds, precedences, and disjunctive ordering constraints define feasible nonoverlapping schedules.
assumptions_latex: Jobs are nonpreemptive with known positive durations.
A valid finite big-M bound is available when disjunctions use big-M.
Resource membership is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible variables specify start and completion times satisfying the modeled temporal and resource restrictions.

notation.meaning: start and completion times of job j
binary order indicator for jobs i and j

children.title: Continuous-Time Event Models
children.top_down_role: Event representations retaining continuous temporal coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Time Event Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-event scheduling representation with real-valued event times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{1,ldots,K\}\) be ordered events with continuous times \(\theta_e\in[0,H]\) satisfying \(\theta_e\le\theta_{e+1}\). For each activity \(j\), binary variables \(u_{je}\) and \(v_{je}\) select one start event and one finish event: \[\sum_{e\in E}u_{je}=1,\qquad\sum_{e\in E}v_{je}=1.\] Valid linking constraints impose \(s_j=\theta_e\) when \(u_{je}=1\), \(C_j=\theta_e\) when \(v_{je}=1\), and \(C_j-s_j=p_j\). Capacity constraints restrict which activities may remain active between consecutive events. No exogenous time discretization is imposed, although the event count is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real-valued event times determine activity starts and finishes, so timing remains continuous while combinatorial decisions use finitely many ordered events.
assumptions_latex: The scheduling horizon is bounded by \(H<\infty\).
Activities are nonpreemptive with fixed durations.
The event count is sufficient for the represented schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasible solutions encode continuous start and completion times through finitely many ordered event positions.

activity j finishes at event e

The event set contains the malformed token 1,ldots,K rather than 1,\ldots,K, and the unspecified linking and capacity constraints are essential to the claimed encoding, making the mathematical formulation unreliable without a direct source.

children.title: Event-Count Selection
children.top_down_role: Model-size plus feasibility effects of choosing event-point capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Event-Count Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency condition for the number of positions in an event-based model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an event semantics and let \(m(S)\) be the number of distinct modeled occurrences—such as starts, completions, or simultaneous change points—in schedule \(S\). An event count \(K\) is representation-complete for a schedule family \(\mathcal S\) precisely when \[K\ge \max_{S\in\mathcal S}m(S).\] If unused event positions are permitted, any larger count preserves representability by assigning surplus positions no activity. If \(K<m(S)\) for some feasible schedule \(S\), that schedule cannot be encoded unless the formulation permits several relevant occurrences to share one event. Thus the correct bound depends essentially on the chosen event semantics and simultaneity convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The event count must cover the maximum number of distinct modeled occurrences in any target schedule, unless simultaneous occurrences may share an event.
assumptions_latex: The event semantics and simultaneity convention are fixed.
Unused event positions are allowed.
The target schedule family is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\ge\max_{S\in\mathcal S}m(S)\) is necessary and sufficient for representation completeness under the stated semantics.

notation.meaning: distinct modeled occurrences in schedule S

review_flags: The bound is conditional on event semantics, which the taxonomy path does not uniquely determine.

children.title: Temporal Symmetry Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Equivalent event placements or start-time encodings that weaken navigation through the model space.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Symmetry Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between interchangeable event labels and temporally distinguishable event positions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose event positions have times \(\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_K\). A permutation of event labels is a symmetry only if it preserves every event-indexed constraint and objective coefficient. In particular, positions with equal times and identical incidence may be permuted without changing the represented schedule. By contrast, if \(\theta_e<\theta_f\), swapping positions \(e\) and \(f\) violates the prescribed temporal order or changes activity-event incidence and is not a symmetry. Hence lexicographic or activity-order symmetry breaking is valid only within equivalence classes of positions that are indistinguishable under all model data; imposing it across distinct temporal positions can delete feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only event positions identical in time, incidence, constraints, and objective data are interchangeable; ordering non-equivalent positions as symmetry breaking may remove feasible schedules.
assumptions_latex: Event times are nondecreasing.
Symmetry means invariance of the complete feasible set and objective.
All event-indexed data are included when testing equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permutations are valid symmetries only within classes of event positions indistinguishable to the full model.

notation.meaning: time assigned to event position e

review_flags: A scheduling-specific symmetry reference is needed to certify the stated boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits Temporal Symmetry Boundaries, but no scheduling-specific symmetry source is supplied. Invariance must be established for the complete formulation, and invalid symmetry-breaking constraints do not necessarily delete feasible schedules in every instance; they can delete feasible schedules. The unconditional wording is therefore stronger than justified.

children.title: Scheduling Horizon Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of temporal extent for finite-horizon scheduling representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Horizon Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for choosing a finite scheduling horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite-horizon formulation with terminal time \(H\), validity requires that at least one optimal schedule of the untruncated problem completes every modeled activity by \(H\). A sufficient computable condition is \[H\ge U,\] where \(U\) is the makespan of any known feasible schedule when minimizing makespan; then an optimum has makespan at most \(U\). More generally, if activities may start only when completion remains within the horizon, job \(j\) has admissible starts satisfying \(s_j+p_j\le H\). Choosing \(H\) below every optimal completion bound truncates all globally optimal schedules and may destroy feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite horizon is safe when it contains at least one global optimum; a known feasible makespan supplies a valid upper bound for makespan minimization.
assumptions_latex: The instance admits a finite feasible schedule.
Activities must complete within the modeled horizon.
For the sufficient bound, the objective is makespan minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(H\ge U\) for a known feasible makespan \(U\), horizon truncation preserves at least one makespan-optimal schedule.

notation.meaning: makespan of a known feasible schedule
start time and duration of job j

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports finite-horizon validity in scheduling.
