The general validity claim requires a formally specified untruncated problem and existence of an attained optimum; the sufficient H>=U statement is limited to makespan minimization with all activities required to complete within the horizon.

children.title: Time-Grid Resolution
children.top_down_role: Granularity choices for discrete temporal representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Grid Resolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness condition for representing temporal data on a uniform grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the uniform grid be \(G_\Delta=\{k\Delta:k=0,\ldots,H/\Delta\}\) with \(\Delta>0\). A schedule is exactly grid-representable when every required start and completion time belongs to \(G_\Delta\). For integer-indexed data, a sufficient condition is that every release date, deadline, processing time, and permitted time lag is an integer multiple of \(\Delta\); then all temporal constraints can be expressed in grid units. If a mandatory time value is not a grid multiple and rounding is forbidden, exact representation fails. Rounding outward may preserve feasibility but weaken timing, whereas rounding inward may exclude schedules that are feasible in continuous time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grid is exact when all required temporal values align with its spacing; otherwise rounding can weaken constraints or remove continuously feasible schedules.
assumptions_latex: The horizon is a finite multiple of \(\Delta\).
Scheduling times are constrained to a uniform grid.
Temporal data are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact grid representation requires all realized starts and completions, and sufficiently all primitive temporal data, to be multiples of \(\Delta\).
review_flags: A direct temporal-discretization source is required for the exactness and rounding claims.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits Time-Grid Resolution, but no source is cited and the mathematical claim is not reliable as stated. Primitive temporal data being grid multiples does not by itself guarantee that all feasible or optimal continuous-time schedules have grid-aligned starts and completions across arbitrary scheduling models. The effects of inward and outward rounding also depend on whether each datum is a lower bound, upper bound, duration, or lag, so the blanket rounding claims need a sourced, constraint-specific formulation.

children.title: Horizon Truncation Effects
children.top_down_role: Loss of feasible or desirable schedules caused by insufficient horizon length.

assumptions_latex: Jobs have nonnegative processing times and must complete within a modeled horizon \(H\).
The original scheduling problem permits completion times greater than \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_H=F\cap\{S:C_j(S)\le H\text{ for every modeled job }j\}\), so \(F_H\subsetneq F\) whenever some feasible schedule finishes after \(H\).

notation.meaning: Feasible schedules of the untruncated problem
Feasible schedules represented with horizon H
Completion time of job j in schedule S

review_flags: Scheduling-specific source needed for the precise truncation formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon truncation in time-indexed scheduling formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible schedules of an untruncated scheduling problem, and let \(F_H\) be those representable when every start or completion variable is restricted to a finite horizon \([0,H]\). Then \[F_H=F\cap\{S:C_j(S)\le H\text{ for every modeled job }j\}.\] Hence truncation cannot create an original schedule, but it deletes every schedule having some \(C_j(S)>H\). If all optimal schedules satisfy \(C_j(S)>H\) for at least one job, the truncated model either becomes infeasible or reports a strictly worse optimum. Therefore exactness requires a valid horizon bound containing at least one optimal schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite horizon removes schedules extending beyond it. If every optimum crosses the cutoff, the truncated model is infeasible or has a worse optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Truncation Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but no inspectable scheduling source supports the truncation claim. The strict-worsening conclusion also needs an explicit optimization direction, existence of an optimum, and clarification that the retained feasible set is nonempty; otherwise only loss of all original optima is established.

children.title: Discretization Feasibility Loss
children.top_down_role: Exclusion of schedules whose timing cannot be represented on the selected grid.

assumptions_latex: Start times are restricted to a grid \(G_\Delta=\{k\Delta:k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\}\).
Continuous-time feasibility permits arbitrary nonnegative real start times.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The continuous feasible set can be nonempty while its grid-restricted counterpart is empty.
review_flags: Scheduling-specific source needed for the stated counterfamily.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of continuous-time schedules under an incommensurate uniform grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\Delta>0\) and restrict all starts to \(G_\Delta=\{k\Delta:k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\}\). Consider two nonpreemptive jobs on one machine with \(p_1=\Delta/2\), \(p_2>0\), fixed \(s_1=0\), and the exact-lag constraint \(s_2=s_1+p_1\). The continuous-time schedule with \(s_2=\Delta/2\) is feasible. No grid-restricted schedule is feasible because \(\Delta/2\notin G_\Delta\). Thus nonemptiness of the continuous feasible set does not imply nonemptiness after discretization unless relevant durations, releases, deadlines, and exact lags are compatible with the chosen grid or the formulation permits compensating slack.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time grid can destroy feasibility when an exact start, duration, or lag is not a grid multiple, even though a continuous-time schedule exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Discretization Feasibility Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically coherent and fits a discretization failure boundary, but it has no cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Time-Indexed Size Growth
children.top_down_role: Representation growth induced by long horizons or fine time grids.

assumptions_latex: The horizon is \(H\), grid width is \(\Delta>0\), and \(T=\lfloor H/\Delta\rfloor+1\).
A binary variable is created for each feasible job-time pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation has at most \(nT=O(nH/\Delta)\) start variables, with pseudo-polynomial growth when \(H/\Delta\) is numeric input magnitude.

notation.meaning: Binary variable for job j starting at grid index t

review_flags: A direct time-indexed scheduling reference is needed; the inventory only supplies general complexity material.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-count growth for a uniform-grid time-indexed start formulation.

source_refs.locator: Section 1.2. Running Time of Algorithms p. 5

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) jobs, horizon \(H\), and grid width \(\Delta>0\), let \(T=\lfloor H/\Delta\rfloor+1\). A formulation containing one binary start variable \(x_{jt}\) for every job \(j\) and admissible grid index \(t\) has at most \(nT\) such variables, hence \[nT=O(nH/\Delta).\] If capacity constraints are written once per resource and grid point, their count is \(O(mT)\) for \(m\) resources. Consequently, when \(H\) and \(1/\Delta\) are numerically encoded rather than bounded structurally, formulation size is pseudo-polynomial in those numeric values and may be exponential in their binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform-grid time-indexed model uses up to order nH/Delta start variables and mH/Delta capacity rows, so its size may be pseudo-polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Time-Indexed Size Growth

source_witnesses.locator: Section 1.2. Running Time of Algorithms p. 5

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits, but the cited general running-time section does not support the scheduling formulation counts. The pseudo-polynomial conclusion also requires a precise encoding model for H and Delta and a scheduling-specific source.

children.title: Pairwise-Ordering Models
children.top_down_role: Binary precedence choices between pairs of scheduled entities.

assumptions_latex: A finite set \(J\) of nonpreemptive jobs shares one unary resource.
Every distinct pair must be ordered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Binary pairwise variables plus disjunctive timing inequalities represent exactly one temporal order for each job pair.

notation.meaning: Start time and processing time of job i
Indicator that job i precedes job j
Valid upper bound used in the disjunction

review_flags: Direct source for the scheduling disjunctive formulation is absent from the supplied inventory.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Big-M pairwise ordering representation for a single unary resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\subseteq J\), introduce \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), interpreted as job \(i\) preceding job \(j\). With a valid constant \(M\), impose \[s_i+p_i\le s_j+M(1-y_{ij}),\qquad s_j+p_j\le s_i+My_{ij}.\] When \(y_{ij}=1\), the first inequality enforces \(i\) before \(j\); when \(y_{ij}=0\), the second enforces \(j\) before \(i\). Provided \(M\) dominates every feasible start-time difference, these inequalities represent the pairwise nonoverlap disjunction. Additional consistency constraints are required if the ordering variables must themselves encode a global linear order independently of timing feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One binary variable selects the order of each job pair, while two timing inequalities enforce the selected nonoverlap disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Ordering Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but no source is supplied. Validity requires inequality-specific bounds on start times and processing times; saying that M dominates start-time differences alone is not a sufficiently precise condition.

children.title: Position-Indexed Models
children.top_down_role: Sequence representations assigning entities to ordered positions.

assumptions_latex: There are \(n\) distinct jobs and exactly \(n\) sequence positions.
Each job and each position must be used once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The binary matrix \(z\) is a permutation matrix and therefore represents a unique job sequence.

notation.meaning: Indicator that job j occupies position k

review_flags: The supplied polyhedral source is general rather than scheduling-specific.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permutation-matrix representation of a complete single-machine sequence.

source_refs.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) contain \(n\) jobs and let \(K=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Introduce \(z_{jk}\in\{0,1\}\), where \(z_{jk}=1\) means that job \(j\) occupies position \(k\). The assignment equations are \[\sum_{k\in K}z_{jk}=1\quad(j\in J),\qquad \sum_{j\in J}z_{jk}=1\quad(k\in K).\] Every binary matrix satisfying these equations is a permutation matrix, hence determines exactly one sequence, and every permutation of \(J\) determines exactly one such matrix. Scheduling times, setup costs, or resource states may then be linked to positions by separate constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary job-by-position permutation matrix represents a complete sequence by assigning every job to one unique position and filling every position once.
knowledge_statements.title: Position-Indexed Models

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Linear inequality systems and polyhedra p. 136

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The permutation-matrix representation is standard and matches the leaf, but the cited generic polyhedra section does not specifically support the assignment equations or their sequencing interpretation.

children.title: Pairwise Precedence Consistency
children.top_down_role: Global consistency requirements across local pairwise ordering choices.

assumptions_latex: For every two distinct jobs exactly one precedence direction is selected.
The selected precedence relation is intended to be a strict total order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise completeness together with the triangle inequalities is equivalent to acyclicity and transitivity of the selected tournament.

notation.meaning: Indicator that job i precedes job j

review_flags: An exact linear-ordering polytope source is needed for this equivalence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency conditions for pairwise precedence variables on a complete job set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct \(i,j\in J\), let \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate that \(i\) precedes \(j\). Pairwise completeness and antisymmetry require \[y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1.\] Global consistency is enforced by the triangle inequalities \[y_{ij}+y_{jk}+y_{ki}\le 2\qquad\text{for all distinct }i,j,k\in J.\] A complete orientation satisfying every triangle inequality has no directed triangle; a tournament with no directed triangle is acyclic and therefore transitive. Thus these constraints make the selected pairwise precedences coincide with a strict linear order. Without the triangle inequalities, locally valid pair choices may contain a directed cycle and cannot describe any sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise choices form a valid complete sequence exactly when opposite directions are complementary and every directed triangle is excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Precedence Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role and tournament consistency statement fit the container, but the claimed equivalence between triangle exclusion, acyclicity, transitivity, and a strict linear order lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Position–Time Linkages
children.top_down_role: Connections between sequence positions plus temporal scheduling decisions.

assumptions_latex: The assignment variables form a permutation matrix.
Each position has a well-defined start time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equations \(s_j=\sum_k S_kz_{jk}\) are valid under binary assignment but require linearization when both \(S_k\) and \(z_{jk}\) are variables.

notation.meaning: Indicator that job j occupies position k
Start time assigned to position k

review_flags: A scheduling formulation source is needed for the linkage and its linearization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linking job-indexed start times to position-indexed start times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_{jk}\) be a permutation assignment and let \(S_k\) denote the start time of the job occupying position \(k\). The intended linkage is \[s_j=\sum_{k=1}^{n}S_kz_{jk}\qquad(j\in J).\] Because exactly one \(z_{jk}\) equals one for each \(j\), this identity transfers the selected position time to job \(j\). If \(S_k\) is variable, the products are bilinear. Given bounds \(L_k\le S_k\le U_k\), auxiliary variables \(w_{jk}=S_kz_{jk}\) and the standard four bounded-product inequalities provide an exact mixed-integer linear representation, after which \(s_j=\sum_k w_{jk}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Job start time equals the start time of its assigned position; variable position times require an exact bounded binary-product linearization.
knowledge_statements.title: Position–Time Linkages

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits, but no source supports the linkage or exact binary-product linearization. The statement invokes four inequalities without stating them, so their validity cannot be checked from the record itself.

children.title: Ordering Symmetry Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Equivalent sequence encodings arising from interchangeable jobs, machines, or positions.

assumptions_latex: Jobs are indistinguishable only when all model data and objective coefficients are invariant under their permutation.
Ordering variables explicitly distinguish job labels or sequence positions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permuting an interchangeable class preserves feasibility and value; imposing one canonical internal order is valid only within such a class.
review_flags: A source on symmetry in scheduling formulations is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for symmetry breaking among interchangeable jobs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq J\) be a set of jobs such that every permutation \(\pi\in\mathfrak S(E)\) maps each feasible solution in \(F\) to another feasible solution with the same objective value. Then the ordering formulation contains orbits of equivalent labeled solutions. Fixing a canonical order of jobs in \(E\), for example increasing labels, retains at least one representative from every orbit. This symmetry breaking is invalid when jobs in \(E\) differ in any active release date, deadline, processing time, eligibility, setup interaction, precedence relation, or objective coefficient that is not preserved by \(\pi\). Across that boundary, imposing label order can delete every optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical ordering safely removes duplicate solutions only among truly interchangeable jobs; asymmetric timing, resources, setups, precedences, or costs invalidate it.
knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Symmetry Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, but no symmetry source is cited. Outside an invariant interchangeability class, canonical label ordering is not generally valid; however, asymmetry only means it may delete every optimum, not that it necessarily does.

children.title: Linear-Ordering Structures
children.top_down_role: Geometric structure of complete consistent ordering representations.

assumptions_latex: The ground set \(J\) is finite.
A strict precedence decision is made for every distinct pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incidence vectors of strict linear orders are exactly the binary vectors satisfying pairwise complementarity and transitivity.

notation.meaning: Indicator that element i precedes element j
Set of all linear-order incidence vectors on J

review_flags: An exact source for the linear-ordering structure and polytope is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary incidence representation and convex hull of strict linear orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set \(J\), a linear-order incidence vector is a binary vector \(y\) indexed by ordered pairs of distinct elements, where \(y_{ij}=1\) exactly when \(i\) precedes \(j\). It satisfies \[y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\qquad(i\ne j)\] and the transitivity implication \[y_{ij}=y_{jk}=1\Longrightarrow y_{ik}=1\qquad(i,j,k\text{ distinct}).\] The set of all such vectors is \(\mathcal L(J)\). Its convex hull \(P_{LO}(J)=\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal L(J))\) is the linear-ordering polytope. Each vector in \(\mathcal L(J)\) corresponds bijectively to one permutation of \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear order is encoded by binary pairwise precedences that choose one direction per pair and obey transitivity; their convex hull is the linear-ordering polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Ordering Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the linear-ordering structure, and the notation is consistent, but no source with a specific locator supports the incidence-vector characterization or linear-ordering polytope definition.

children.title: Transitivity Structures
children.top_down_role: Consistency structures excluding cyclic precedence selections.

assumptions_latex: Binary variables choose exactly one orientation for each unordered pair.
All indices in each constraint are distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triangle inequalities exclude every directed triangle and thereby enforce transitivity for a complete orientation.
review_flags: An exact source for tournament transitivity and triangle inequalities is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Triangle formulation of transitivity for complete pairwise orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) and impose \(y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\) for all distinct \(i,j\in J\). Transitivity may be written as \[y_{ij}+y_{jk}-y_{ik}\le 1\qquad(i,j,k\text{ distinct}).\] Using pairwise complementarity, the same condition is \[y_{ij}+y_{jk}+y_{ki}\le 2.\] Thus no three elements may form a directed cycle. For a complete orientation, exclusion of every directed triangle is sufficient to exclude every directed cycle and yields a transitive tournament. Integrality is essential: the same linear inequalities imposed on fractional variables describe a relaxation rather than only incidence vectors of linear orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For integral complete pairwise orientations, triangle inequalities enforce transitivity; with fractional variables they provide only a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Transitivity Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits and the integral-versus-fractional boundary is stated correctly, but no inspectable source supports the triangle formulation and transitive-tournament equivalence.

children.title: Cycle-Elimination Structures
children.top_down_role: Ordering restrictions organized around directed cycles.

assumptions_latex: A directed graph represents selected precedence arcs.
A feasible strict ordering must be acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A selected arc set is acyclic exactly when every directed-cycle inequality is satisfied.

notation.meaning: Directed graph of possible precedence arcs
Indicator that arc a is selected
Arc set of a directed cycle C

review_flags: A direct source for directed cycle-elimination inequalities is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cycle inequalities certifying acyclicity of selected precedence arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(J,A)\) be a directed graph and let \(x_a\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether precedence arc \(a\) is selected. For every directed simple cycle \(C\), impose \[\sum_{a\in A(C)}x_a\le |A(C)|-1.\] These inequalities are necessary and sufficient for the selected subgraph to be acyclic: each inequality forbids selecting all arcs of its cycle, while any cyclic selected subgraph contains a directed simple cycle whose inequality would be violated. When the graph is a complete orientation, triangle elimination together with pairwise complementarity suffices; for an arbitrary partial arc selection, longer-cycle inequalities may be necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected precedence arcs are acyclic exactly when every directed cycle is missing at least one arc; arbitrary partial selections may require long-cycle inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Elimination Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits cycle-elimination structures, but the necessity-and-sufficiency claim and the distinction between complete orientations and arbitrary selected subgraphs require a cited source with a specific locator.

children.title: Partial-Order Extensions
children.top_down_role: Extensions from incomplete precedence relations to schedule-compatible orders.

assumptions_latex: The precedence relation is a finite partial order \((J,\prec)\).
Any added comparison must preserve every original precedence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least one strict linear order extending \(\prec\) exists and can be obtained by repeated removal of a minimal element.

notation.meaning: Finite job set with strict partial order
A strict total order extending the partial order
Set of minimal elements of a remaining subset R

review_flags: A precise source for the finite linear-extension theorem is needed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear-extension theorem for precedence-constrained job sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((J,\prec)\) be a finite strict partial order. Then there exists a strict linear order \(\prec_L\) on \(J\) such that \[i\prec j\Longrightarrow i\prec_L j\qquad(i,j\in J).\] Equivalently, every finite acyclic precedence digraph has a topological ordering. Such an extension is produced by initializing \(R=J\), repeatedly choosing any element of \(\min_{\prec}(R)\), appending it to the sequence, and deleting it from \(R\). Different choices among incomparable minimal elements may yield different extensions, but every resulting sequence respects all original precedences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite partial order has a total ordering that preserves all required precedences; repeated selection of a currently minimal job constructs one.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Order Extensions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits Partial-Order Extensions, and the finite linear-extension statement is precise, but neither the theorem nor the stated minimal-element construction has an inspectable citation.

children.title: Ordering Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Fractional or cyclic behavior remaining in weakened ordering representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention for gaps induced by relaxing ordering variables or ordering inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization model, define \(v_F=\min\{c^Tz:z\in F\}\) and \(v_R=\min\{c^Tz:z\in R\}\). The additive ordering-relaxation gap is \[g_{\mathrm{add}}=v_F-v_R.\] If \(0<v_R\le v_F\), the multiplicative gap is \[g_{\mathrm{mult}}=\frac{v_F}{v_R}.\] Thus the gap measures objective degradation caused by admitting fractional or otherwise nonrealizable ordering vectors. If \(v_R\le0\), the additive definition remains valid, while the displayed multiplicative convention is not used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ordering relaxation gap compares the optimal integer schedule with its relaxed ordering model, additively or, when both optima are positive, multiplicatively.
assumptions_latex: The integer scheduling model has feasible set \(F\subseteq\{0,1\}^m\times\mathbb{R}^q\) and objective \(c^Tz\).
The ordering relaxation replaces \(F\) by a tractable set \(R\supseteq F\) and both minimization optima are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{add}}\ge 0\), and \(g_{\mathrm{mult}}\ge 1\) whenever \(0<v_R\le v_F\).

notation.meaning: integer and relaxed optimal objective values

children.title: Big-M Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Disjunctive scheduling encodings controlled by finite bounding constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Big-M Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise nonoverlap on one machine using bounded start times and a binary order variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonoverlap disjunction \[(S_i+p_i\le S_j)\ \lor\ (S_j+p_j\le S_i)\] has the big-M representation \[S_i+p_i\le S_j+M_{ij}(1-y_{ij}),\qquad S_j+p_j\le S_i+M_{ji}y_{ij},\qquad y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}.\] Validity requires the first inequality to be redundant over the start-time domain when \(y_{ij}=0\), and the second to be redundant when \(y_{ij}=1\). Consequently, every feasible integer point satisfies at least one temporal order, and every schedule satisfying either order admits a corresponding value of \(y_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary order variable activates one precedence inequality while a valid big-M constant deactivates the opposite inequality, yielding the union of the two possible orders.
assumptions_latex: Jobs \(i\) and \(j\) have nonnegative processing times \(p_i,p_j\) and start times \(S_i,S_j\).
Valid constants \(M_{ij},M_{ji}\) bound the inactive disjunctive inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\), the projection onto \((S_i,S_j)\) equals the union of the two nonoverlap orders when the constants are valid.

notation.meaning: start time and processing time of job i
one when job i precedes job j

source_refs.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

source_witnesses.locator: Section 13. Application to Project Scheduling p. 165

children.title: Indicator Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Solver-supported conditional scheduling restrictions triggered by binary choices.

assumptions_latex: Jobs \(i\) and \(j\) require the same unary resource.
The modeling system gives indicator constraints their exact logical semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two indicators and \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) are equivalent to the pairwise nonoverlap disjunction.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact binary implication semantics is standard in mixed-integer modeling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact logical representation; solver-specific reformulations and tolerances are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce \(y_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) and impose the indicator implications \[y_{ij}=1\ \Longrightarrow\ S_i+p_i\le S_j,\qquad y_{ij}=0\ \Longrightarrow\ S_j+p_j\le S_i.\] Under exact indicator semantics, fixing \(y_{ij}=1\) enforces that job \(i\) finishes before job \(j\) starts, while fixing \(y_{ij}=0\) enforces the reverse order. Hence the projection onto the start-time variables equals \[\{S:S_i+p_i\le S_j\}\ \cup\ \{S:S_j+p_j\le S_i\}.\] No explicit user-selected big-M constant is part of this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two complementary indicator implications encode exactly which of two jobs precedes the other on a unary resource.
knowledge_statements.title: Indicator Disjunctions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically precise under the stated exact logical semantics, but no inspectable source with a section, page, or definition locator is supplied for indicator constraints.

children.title: Logical Scheduling Disjunctions
children.top_down_role: Native logical alternatives for mutually exclusive temporal arrangements.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical Scheduling Disjunctions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise logical feasibility condition for nonpreemptive positive-duration jobs on unary resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[E=\{\{i,j\}:i\ne j,\ R_i\cap R_j\ne\varnothing\}.\] The logical scheduling-disjunction condition is \[\bigwedge_{\{i,j\}\in E}\bigl((S_i+p_i\le S_j)\ \lor\ (S_j+p_j\le S_i)\bigr).\] For nonpreemptive jobs with positive processing times on unary resources, this condition is equivalent to pairwise nonoverlap of all jobs sharing a resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every pair of positive-duration nonpreemptive jobs sharing a unary resource must satisfy one of the two possible nonoverlap orders.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is a finite job set, and every job \(i\in J\) has start time \(S_i\), processing time \(p_i>0\), and resource set \(R_i\).
Every resource appearing in a set \(R_i\) is unary and cannot process overlapping jobs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule is resource-feasible exactly when every conflicting pair satisfies at least one of its two temporal orders.

notation.meaning: set of unordered job pairs sharing a unary resource
start time, processing time, and resource set of job i

children.title: Disjunction Bound Tightness
children.top_down_role: Relaxation quality associated with temporal bounds plus encoding choices.

assumptions_latex: The start-time bounds \(L_k\le S_k\le U_k\) are valid for \(k\in\{i,j\}\).
The big-M constraints use the pairwise order variable \(y_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The smallest box-valid constants are \(M_{ij}^{\min}=U_i+p_i-L_j\) and \(M_{ji}^{\min}=U_j+p_j-L_i\), truncated at zero if nonnegative constants are required.

notation.meaning: valid lower and upper start-time bounds
smallest valid deactivation constants over the bounding box

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: extrema of affine inequalities over a box
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tightness relative only to independent start-time bounds, not the full scheduling feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[S_i+p_i\le S_j+M_{ij}(1-y_{ij}),\qquad S_j+p_j\le S_i+M_{ji}y_{ij},\] validity over the bounding box requires \[M_{ij}\ge\max(S_i+p_i-S_j)=U_i+p_i-L_j\] when \(y_{ij}=0\), and \[M_{ji}\ge\max(S_j+p_j-S_i)=U_j+p_j-L_i\] when \(y_{ij}=1\). Thus these maxima are the componentwise smallest box-valid constants. Replacing either by a smaller value excludes a bounded start-time vector from the inactive branch; replacing it by a larger value preserves integer feasibility but weakens the continuous relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tight big-M values are the maximum possible violations of the corresponding inactive precedence inequalities over the stated start-time bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction Bound Tightness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box-based maxima and their limited scope are mathematically plausible, but the record supplies no inspectable citation for the minimal big-M formulas or relaxation-strength claim.

children.title: Numerical Scaling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability associated with oversized constants or poorly scaled temporal data.

assumptions_latex: A deactivated big-M row is checked with normalized residual tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\).
The row contains a term \(M(1-y)\) with \(M>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A binary deviation or accepted residual of size \(\varepsilon\) can create time-scale ambiguity proportional to \(M\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite-precision boundary; exact residual scaling depends on solver implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[S_i+p_i-S_j\le M(1-y).\] If numerical processing treats \(y=1-\delta\) as effectively integral with \(0\le\delta\le\varepsilon\), then the right-hand side can retain slack \(M\delta\le M\varepsilon\). Likewise, a normalized row residual of size \(\varepsilon\) translates into an original-unit error governed by the row scaling. Therefore a sufficient warning boundary is \[M\varepsilon\ge\tau,\] where \(\tau>0\) is the smallest time separation regarded as operationally meaningful. Beyond this boundary, nominal logical enforcement need not resolve separations of size \(\tau\) reliably.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When big-M times a solver tolerance reaches a meaningful time unit, numerical acceptance can obscure the intended precedence separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Scaling Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integrality-tolerance calculation is plausible, but normalized residuals and row scaling are solver-dependent. A solver or numerical-analysis source specifying the relevant tolerance semantics is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Machine–Job Assignment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static assignment layer; sequencing feasibility may require additional machine-local constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(i\in J\) and \(k\in E_i\), let \(x_{ik}\in\{0,1\}\). The machine-job assignment equations are \[\sum_{k\in E_i}x_{ik}=1\qquad(i\in J).\] If job \(i\) consumes machine load \(a_{ik}\ge0\), optional aggregate capacities are \[\sum_{i:k\in E_i}a_{ik}x_{ik}\le C_k\qquad(k\in M).\] The equations encode a complete eligible assignment. They do not alone ensure that jobs assigned to the same machine admit a feasible temporal sequence unless the load inequalities or additional machine-local scheduling constraints imply such feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary assignment variables allocate every job to one eligible machine; optional aggregate constraints restrict the assignments to stated machine capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is a finite job set, \(M\) is a finite machine set, and each eligibility set \(E_i\subseteq M\) is nonempty.
Each job must be assigned to exactly one eligible machine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assignment equations describe precisely the complete eligible assignments; when the optional capacity inequalities are imposed, they describe the complete eligible assignments satisfying those aggregate limits.

notation.meaning: one when job i is assigned to machine k

source_refs.locator: Section 11.1. The Assignment Problem p. 278

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Assignment integer program for unrelated-machine makespan
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The natural machine–job assignment formulation for minimizing makespan on unrelated parallel machines, together with the stated failure boundary of its LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For machine set \(M\), job set \(J\), and processing times \(p_{ij}\), let \(x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether job \(j\) is assigned to machine \(i\). The formulation is \(\min t\) subject to \(\sum_{i\in M}x_{ij}=1\) for every \(j\in J\) and \(\sum_{j\in J}p_{ij}x_{ij}\le t\) for every \(i\in M\). The associated natural LP relaxation has unbounded integrality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assign each job to exactly one machine and minimize a variable that bounds every machine's total assigned processing time. The natural LP relaxation of this formulation has an unbounded integrality gap.
assumptions_latex: x_{ij}\text{ indicates whether job }j\text{ is scheduled on machine }i
p_{ij}\text{ is the processing time of job }j\text{ on machine }i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\left\{t:\sum_{i\in M}x_{ij}=1\ \forall j\in J,\ \sum_{j\in J}p_{ij}x_{ij}\le t\ \forall i\in M,\ x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}\right\},\quad\text{and its natural LP relaxation has unbounded integrality gap.}

children.title: Scheduling Configuration Models
children.top_down_role: Models whose columns represent complete feasible configurations.

assumptions_latex: Each resource \(k\) has a family \(\mathcal C_k\) of feasible complete local schedules.
Each configuration records which jobs it executes and its cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting one configuration per resource and covering each job once gives a set-partitioning representation of the global schedule.

notation.meaning: one when configuration c is selected
one when configuration c covers job i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set-partitioning master over feasible resource configurations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dantzig-Wolfe-style representation using complete feasible schedules as columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each resource \(k\), let \(\mathcal C_k\) contain feasible local schedules and let \(a_{ikc}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether configuration \(c\in\mathcal C_k\) performs job \(i\). A configuration model is \[\min\sum_k\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}q_{kc}z_{kc}\] subject to \[\sum_k\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}a_{ikc}z_{kc}=1\quad(i\in J),\qquad \sum_{c\in\mathcal C_k}z_{kc}=1\quad(k\in M),\qquad z_{kc}\in\{0,1\}.\] Empty configurations may be included for unused resources. Each selected column is locally feasible by construction; the master constraints coordinate jobs across resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each binary column represents a complete feasible resource schedule; the master selects columns that partition all jobs.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Configuration Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-partitioning configuration formulation fits the leaf, but no source with an inspectable locator supports the scheduling-column interpretation and master formulation.

children.title: Scheduling Pattern Models
children.top_down_role: Models built from reusable activity, shift, or resource-use patterns.

assumptions_latex: \(T\) is a finite indexed planning horizon.
Each pattern specifies a permitted activity state at every indexed period for one entity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pattern selection converts within-entity temporal rules into column membership and leaves cross-entity requirements in the master constraints.

notation.meaning: activity of pattern p in period t
one when pattern p is selected

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: binary pattern-selection formulation over a finite horizon
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon pattern selection for workers, machines, rooms, or other scheduled entities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each entity \(e\), let \(\mathcal P_e\subseteq\{0,1\}^{T}\) be the admissible activity patterns, with component \(a_{etp}\) for period \(t\). Select exactly one pattern by \[\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_e}z_{ep}=1,\qquad z_{ep}\in\{0,1\}.\] If demand \(d_t\) must be covered, impose \[\sum_e\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_e}a_{etp}z_{ep}\ge d_t\qquad(t\in T).\] Rules involving only one entity, such as consecutive-work or rest restrictions, are enforced by membership in \(\mathcal P_e\); coupling requirements remain explicit master constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pattern model chooses one admissible time-indexed activity vector per entity and couples those choices through coverage constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Pattern Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-horizon pattern-selection formulation fits the leaf, but no inspectable scheduling-pattern source is provided.

children.title: Configuration Coverage Structures
children.top_down_role: Coverage relationships between configurations plus scheduling requirements.

assumptions_latex: Every configuration column has a binary incidence vector over required tasks.
Task requirements specify exact, lower, or upper coverage multiplicities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incidence matrix and multiplicity bounds completely define configuration coverage at the master level.

notation.meaning: lower and upper required coverage of task i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incidence-matrix covering and partitioning constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master-level task coverage, independent of how feasible configurations are generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_{ic}=1\) exactly when configuration \(c\) covers task \(i\), and let \(z_c\) be its selected multiplicity. The general configuration-coverage condition is \[\ell_i\le\sum_c a_{ic}z_c\le u_i\qquad(i\in J).\] Exact partitioning is obtained with \(\ell_i=u_i=1\); set covering uses \(\ell_i=1\) and no finite upper bound; set packing uses \(\ell_i=0\) and \(u_i=1\). Coverage feasibility requires that every task with \(\ell_i>0\) occur in at least one available column and that the complete system admit a common integral selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incidence matrix links configurations to tasks, with multiplicity bounds yielding partitioning, covering, or packing structures.
knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Coverage Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable source is supplied, and the domain of the selected multiplicities \(z_c\) is not stated. Without a nonnegative-integer domain, the claimed integral coverage and partitioning interpretation is incomplete.

children.title: Pattern Compatibility Structures
children.top_down_role: Compatibility among selected patterns sharing jobs, resources, or time.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a finite family of individually feasible scheduling patterns.
Pairwise incompatibility means that two patterns cannot occur together in any global schedule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any compatible pattern selection is a stable set of the incompatibility graph; clique inequalities strengthen pairwise edge constraints.

notation.meaning: one when pattern p is selected

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-graph representation of pairwise pattern incompatibilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(G=(\mathcal P,E)\) with \(\{p,q\}\in E\) exactly when patterns \(p\) and \(q\) are incompatible. Binary selection variables satisfy \[z_p+z_q\le1\qquad(\{p,q\}\in E).\] Therefore the support \(\{p:z_p=1\}\) of every feasible selection is a stable set of \(G\). For every clique \(Q\subseteq\mathcal P\), the valid inequality \[\sum_{p\in Q}z_p\le1\] dominates its constituent edge inequalities in the linear relaxation. Pairwise graph compatibility is sufficient for global compatibility only when all incompatibility mechanisms are captured by graph edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Patterns form vertices of a conflict graph; feasible selections are stable sets, with clique inequalities expressing mutual incompatibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Pattern Compatibility Structures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conflict-graph representation is standard and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports its scheduling-pattern interpretation or clique-strengthening statement.

children.title: Configuration Pool Completeness
children.top_down_role: Representational limits caused by incomplete candidate configuration pools.

assumptions_latex: The full model indexes every feasible local schedule by a column in \(\mathcal C\).
A restricted master uses a pool \(\widehat{\mathcal C}\subseteq\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pool is representation-complete exactly when every globally feasible schedule has an equivalent decomposition using only columns from \(\widehat{\mathcal C}\).

notation.meaning: global feasible sets represented by a column family

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality of projected feasible sets defines representational completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representational completeness of a restricted column pool, not pricing optimality at one objective vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any column family \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal C\), let \(X(\mathcal D)\) be the set of global schedules obtained from integral master selections using columns in \(\mathcal D\). The restricted pool is complete precisely when \[X(\widehat{\mathcal C})=X(\mathcal C).\] Since \(\widehat{\mathcal C}\subseteq\mathcal C\), one always has \(X(\widehat{\mathcal C})\subseteq X(\mathcal C)\); hence completeness reduces to proving the reverse inclusion. If only equality of optimal values for one objective is established, the pool is objective-sufficient for that instance but need not be representation-complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A configuration pool is complete when every schedule representable by all feasible columns is still representable using the pool.
knowledge_statements.title: Configuration Pool Completeness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected-feasible-set equality is a coherent definition of representational completeness, but no inspectable source supports this terminology or its distinction from objective-specific sufficiency.

children.title: Scheduling Set-Partitioning Models
children.top_down_role: Exact-cover scheduling representations using complete feasible columns.

assumptions_latex: \(J\) is a finite set of jobs or coverage requirements.
\(\mathcal S\) is a finite family of feasible schedules, and \(a_{js}=1\) exactly when schedule \(s\) covers job \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected schedules form an exact partition of \(J\) of minimum stated cost.

notation.meaning: Binary selection variable for feasible schedule s.

review_flags: Scheduling-specific formulation is standard, but no supplied locator directly supports the exact-partition model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exact-cover master formulation for selecting complete feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scheduling set-partitioning model is the binary optimization problem
\[
\min_{x}\ \sum_{s\in\mathcal S}c_sx_s
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}a_{js}x_s=1\ \text{for every }j\in J,
\qquad x_s\in\{0,1\}\ \text{for every }s\in\mathcal S.
\]
Each column represents an internally feasible schedule. The equality constraints require every job to belong to exactly one selected schedule; additional master constraints may be appended when schedules also consume shared aggregate resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select minimum-cost feasible schedules so that every job is covered by exactly one selected schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Set-Partitioning Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and exact-cover formulation fit the leaf, but no cited source with an inspectable locator supports the scheduling-specific set-partitioning model.

children.title: Scheduling Path-Based Models
children.top_down_role: Network-path representations of schedules, routes, duties, or resource sequences.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a finite directed acyclic network with source \(o\) and sink \(d\).
Every feasible resource schedule corresponds to an admissible \(o\)-to-\(d\) path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting paths subject to master constraints yields a path-based scheduling formulation.

notation.meaning: Binary selection variable for path p.
Contribution of path p to master row k.

review_flags: Supplied network-flow locators support paths generally but not this scheduling master formulation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acyclic state-network representation of complete schedules as source-to-sink paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) index master requirements, with right-hand sides \(r_k\). A path-based scheduling model has the form
\[
\min_{y}\ \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}c_py_p
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}b_{kp}y_p\ \bowtie_k\ r_k\ \text{ for every }k\in K,
\qquad y_p\in\{0,1\}\ \text{ for every }p\in\mathcal P,
\]
where each \(\bowtie_k\) is one of \(=\), \(\le\), or \(\ge\). Arc states and transitions encode temporal and resource feasibility, while the master rows coordinate the complete paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each complete feasible schedule by an admissible source-to-sink path and coordinate selected paths through master constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Path-Based Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no source supports the asserted scheduling correspondence between admissible paths, complete schedules, and master rows.

children.title: Path-to-Partition Coupling
children.top_down_role: Translation of feasible paths into partitioning columns plus coverage coefficients.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a scheduling network whose admissible paths encode feasible schedules.
Each arc \(e\in A\) has job-incidence vector \(g^e\in\{0,1\}^{J}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The induced column \(a_{\cdot p}\) makes the path formulation and set-partitioning master use the same job coverage data.

notation.meaning: Job-incidence coefficient induced by path p.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly establishes the scheduling-specific path-to-column correspondence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear projection from an admissible scheduling path to its set-partitioning column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every admissible path \(p\), define
\[
a_{jp}=\sum_{e\in A}g_j^e z_e^p\quad\text{for every }j\in J,
\qquad
c_p=\sum_{e\in A}d_e z_e^p.
\]
When path construction ensures \(a_{jp}\in\{0,1\}\), the pair \((a_{\cdot p},c_p)\) is a valid set-partitioning column and its cost. Conversely, a schedule column has a path realization when some admissible \(p\) satisfies these equalities. Thus master coverage constraints can be written directly with path-induced coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sum arc labels along a feasible path to obtain the schedule column's job incidences and cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-to-Partition Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches path-to-partition coupling, but the scheduling-specific path-to-column correspondence and its stated converse lack cited support.

children.title: Resource-Constrained Scheduling Paths
children.top_down_role: Path families carrying temporal, capacity, skill, or sequencing resources.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a finite directed network with source \(o\) and sink \(d\).
Each arc has resource increment \(q_e\in\mathbb R^m\), and resource bounds are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A path is scheduling-feasible exactly when it is structurally admissible and its propagated resources satisfy every prescribed bound.

notation.meaning: Resource state after reaching vertex v along path p.
Lower and upper resource bounds at vertex v.
Resource extension map on arc e.

review_flags: Generic shortest-path hints do not directly support the scheduling resource-extension condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic resource-extension feasibility for scheduling paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An \(o\)-to-\(d\) path \(p=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)\) is resource-constrained scheduling-feasible if its state sequence satisfies
\[
R_o^p=R^0,
\qquad R_{v_k}^p=F_{e_k}(R_{v_{k-1}}^p),
\qquad \ell_{v_k}\le R_{v_k}^p\le u_{v_k}
\quad(k=1,\ldots,r).
\]
For additive resources, \(F_e(R)=R+q_e\). Network admissibility must additionally enforce permitted temporal or sequencing transitions. A feasible path therefore represents a schedule only when both its graph transitions and all propagated resource states are feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling path is feasible when every transition is allowed and all propagated resource states remain within their bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Scheduling Paths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits resource-constrained scheduling paths, but no cited resource-constrained shortest-path or scheduling source supports the resource-extension semantics and exact feasibility characterization.

children.title: Column Pool Sufficiency
children.top_down_role: Coverage limitations arising from restricted or incomplete path collections.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is the full feasible column family and \(\widehat{\mathcal P}\subseteq\mathcal P\) is a restricted pool.
The full master is a linear minimization problem with equality rows and nonnegative variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted pool is LP-sufficient precisely when it admits an optimal restricted solution and no omitted column has negative reduced cost at a corresponding dual optimum.

notation.meaning: Dual vector for the master equality constraints.
Master coefficient vector of column p.

review_flags: The supplied hints do not directly support restricted-master sufficiency in scheduling column generation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for sufficiency of a restricted scheduling column pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the full master be \(\min\{\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}c_px_p:\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_px_p=b,\ x\ge0\}\). A restricted pool \(\widehat{\mathcal P}\) is sufficient for its linear relaxation if a restricted primal feasible solution \(\widehat x\) and a dual vector \(\pi\) satisfy
\[
\sum_{p\in\widehat{\mathcal P}}c_p\widehat x_p=b^{\mathsf T}\pi,
\qquad
\bar c_p:=c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\ge0
\quad\text{for every }p\in\mathcal P.
\]
The first equality certifies restricted primal-dual optimality; the reduced-cost inequalities show that no omitted column improves the full master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted column pool solves the full LP when primal-dual values agree and every omitted column has nonnegative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Column Pool Sufficiency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate and the reduced-cost condition is standard, but the record supplies no source for restricted-master sufficiency. A source should also state the required feasibility and finite-optimum assumptions.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite activity set.
Each activity \(i\) has duration \(p_i\ge0\) and an optional presence indicator \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An interval-variable assignment specifies whether each activity occurs and, when present, its start, end, and duration.

notation.meaning: Start and end variables of activity i.
Fixed or variable duration of activity i.

review_flags: No constraint-programming source locator was supplied for interval-variable semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-programming interval variables with optional presence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An interval-variable model associates each activity \(i\in I\) with \((s_i,e_i,p_i,z_i)\). Its semantics are
\[
z_i=1\ \Longrightarrow\ e_i=s_i+p_i,
\qquad
z_i=0\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{the activity contributes to no constraint guarded by its presence}.
\]
For mandatory activities, \(z_i=1\) is fixed. Scheduling relations such as precedence, alternative selection, and resource use are imposed on these interval variables, with every relation involving an optional activity interpreted only under its specified presence guard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interval variable records an activity's presence, start, end, and duration, with scheduling constraints guarded when the activity is optional.
knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Variable Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the interval-variable leaf, but optional-interval semantics, especially the treatment of absent activities and guarded constraints, are implementation-sensitive and require a constraint-programming source.

children.title: Disjunctive Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Mutual-exclusion structures for activities sharing unary resources.

assumptions_latex: \(Ir\) is the finite set of activities requiring unary resource \(r\).
Each activity \(i\) has start \(s_i\) and processing time \(p_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource feasibility holds exactly when every pair of positive-duration activities assigned to the resource is temporally ordered.

notation.meaning: Half-open execution interval of activity i.
Ordering indicator for activities i and j.
Activities assigned to unary resource r.

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports the disjunctive scheduling constraint family.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise nonoverlap formulation for a unary renewable resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The disjunctive resource constraint on \(I_r\) is
\[
(s_i+p_i\le s_j)\ \lor\ (s_j+p_j\le s_i)
\quad\text{for all distinct }i,j\in I_r.
\]
Equivalently, with a valid upper bound \(M_{ij}\) and binary \(y_{ij}\), one may impose
\[
s_i+p_i\le s_j+M_{ij}(1-y_{ij}),
\qquad
s_j+p_j\le s_i+M_{ji}y_{ij}.
\]
The family models a resource of capacity one: activities of positive duration assigned to it cannot execute simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every pair of activities using a unary resource must be ordered so their execution intervals do not overlap.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Constraint Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and the disjunction is standard, but no supporting source is cited. The assumptions also introduce “Ir” rather than the subsequently used notation I_r.

children.title: Cumulative Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Capacity-profile structures for activities consuming renewable resources.

assumptions_latex: \(I_r\) is a finite set of nonpreemptive activities using renewable resource \(r\).
Activity \(i\) has start \(s_i\), duration \(p_i\ge0\), and demand \(q_{ir}\ge0\).
The resource has constant capacity \(Q_r\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule satisfies the cumulative constraint exactly when concurrent demand never exceeds \(Q_r\).

notation.meaning: Demand of activity i for resource r.

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports the cumulative global-constraint definition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-time cumulative capacity for nonpreemptive activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cumulative constraint for resource \(r\) is the pointwise condition
\[
\sum_{i\in I_r}q_{ir}\mathbf 1[s_i\le t<s_i+p_i]\le Q_r
\quad\text{for every }t\in\mathbb R.
\]
Using half-open execution intervals fixes endpoint convention and permits one activity to start when another ends. Unary disjunctive scheduling is the special case \(q_{ir}=Q_r=1\) for all participating activities of positive duration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every time, the sum of demands of executing activities must not exceed the renewable resource capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Constraint Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cumulative-capacity definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but it has no constraint-programming or scheduling citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: No-Overlap Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Nonintersection structures for temporal or spatial intervals.

assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite family of axis-aligned boxes in \(\mathbb R^d\).
Box \(i\) has origin coordinates \(s_{ik}\) and nonnegative extents \(p_{ik}\) for dimensions \(k=1,\ldots,d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No-overlap holds exactly when each distinct box pair is separated in at least one coordinate dimension.

notation.meaning: Coordinate interval occupied by box i in dimension k.
Finite set of boxes or activities.

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports multidimensional no-overlap semantics.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise separation semantics for one- or multidimensional no-overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The no-overlap constraint requires, for every distinct \(i,j\in I\),
\[
\bigvee_{k=1}^{d}
\left((s_{ik}+p_{ik}\le s_{jk})\ \lor\ (s_{jk}+p_{jk}\le s_{ik})\right).
\]
Thus each box pair must be separated in at least one dimension. For \(d=1\), this is the ordinary temporal disjunction; for \(d=2\), it models nonoverlapping rectangles such as activities simultaneously occupying time and a second placement coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each pair of boxes must be separated along at least one dimension; one-dimensional no-overlap is ordinary temporal disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: No-Overlap Constraint Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly targets multidimensional no-overlap, but the pairwise separation semantics and dimensional specializations lack a cited source.

children.title: Optional-Activity Resource Constraints
children.top_down_role: Global resource constraints involving conditionally present activities.

assumptions_latex: \(I_r\) is the finite set of optional activities that may use resource \(r\).
Each activity has presence \(z_i\in\{0,1\}\), start \(s_i\), duration \(p_i\ge0\), and demand \(q_{ir}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only present activities consume resource capacity or participate in resource-ordering disjunctions.

notation.meaning: Demand of activity i for resource r.

review_flags: No supplied source directly supports presence-guarded global resource constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presence-guarded renewable-resource constraints for optional activities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The optional cumulative constraint is
\[
\sum_{i\in I_r}z_iq_{ir}\mathbf 1[s_i\le t<s_i+p_i]\le Q_r
\quad\text{for every }t\in\mathbb R.
\]
For a unary resource, the corresponding guarded disjunction is
\[
(z_i=z_j=1)\ \Longrightarrow\
((s_i+p_i\le s_j)\ \lor\ (s_j+p_j\le s_i))
\quad\text{for distinct }i,j\in I_r.
\]
Consequently, an absent activity neither consumes capacity nor forces an ordering, while every present activity obeys the same resource semantics as a mandatory activity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guard resource constraints by activity presence so absent activities consume no capacity and impose no ordering.
knowledge_statements.title: Optional-Activity Resource Constraints

children.top_down_role: Propagation limitations caused by interacting resource, timing, plus presence structures.

assumptions_latex: Two global constraints \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) share at least one decision variable.
Each constraint propagator is individually sound for its own feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separate local consistency does not generally imply consistency, feasibility, or complete propagation for the conjunction \(C_1\land C_2\).

notation.meaning: Feasible assignments of global constraint C_k.
Current finite domain of shared variable x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of independent propagation across overlapping scheduling global constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Independent propagation reaches a boundary when each constraint separately supports every remaining value but their conjunction does not. Formally, it may happen that
\[
D(x)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(F_1)
\quad\text{and}\quad
D(x)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(F_2),
\qquad
D(x)\nsubseteq\operatorname{proj}_x(F_1\cap F_2).
\]
Hence separate consistency of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) cannot certify joint consistency. Additional combined reasoning, learned clauses, or search may be required when resource, precedence, sequence, or presence constraints share variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagating overlapping global constraints separately can retain values that have no support in their conjunction.

children.title: Scheduling Automata
children.top_down_role: Finite-state representations of admissible scheduling sequences.

assumptions_latex: \(\Sigma\) is a finite alphabet of scheduling labels.
The scheduling automaton has a finite state set \(Q\), initial state \(q_0\), accepting set \(F\), and partial transition map \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite schedule-label sequence is accepted exactly when its successive labels define a complete run ending in \(F\).

notation.meaning: Extended transition map on finite words.

review_flags: No automata or constraint-programming source locator was supplied for scheduling automata.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state acceptance model for discrete schedule-label sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scheduling automaton is a finite automaton \(\mathcal A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) whose symbols encode discrete scheduling decisions or states. Extend \(\delta\) by
\[
\delta^*(q,\varepsilon)=q,
\qquad
\delta^*(q,wa)=\delta(\delta^*(q,w),a)
\]
whenever the transition is defined. A schedule-label word \(w\in\Sigma^*\) is feasible for the automaton exactly when \(\delta^*(q_0,w)\in F\). Undefined transitions forbid the corresponding local continuation, while the terminal acceptance condition enforces the complete sequence pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling automaton accepts exactly those finite decision-label sequences whose defined state run ends in an accepting state.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence-constraint family over \(\Sigma^T\) is a collection of predicates on \(x\), including: window constraints \((x_t,\ldots,x_{t+k-1})\in W\); counting bounds \(\ell_{a,I}\le N_a(I,x)\le u_{a,I}\); run-length bounds requiring each maximal run of symbol \(a\) to have length in \(R_a\subseteq\{1,\ldots,T\}\); and spacing bounds requiring successive occurrences of \(a\) to be separated by a distance in \(D_a\subseteq\{1,\ldots,T-1\}\). children.title: Regular-Language Schedule Patterns
children.top_down_role: Schedule-pattern families expressible through finite-state acceptance structures.

assumptions_latex: The schedule is encoded as a word over a finite alphabet \(\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A schedule pattern is regular exactly when some finite automaton recognizes its feasible words.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state representation of schedule patterns of arbitrary finite length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A schedule-pattern language \(L\subseteq\Sigma^*\) is regular if there exists a deterministic finite automaton \(A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) with finite state set \(Q\) such that, for every word \(x=x_1\cdots x_T\), \[x\in L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \delta^*(q_0,x)\in F.\] Here \(\delta^*\) is the extension of \(\delta\) to words. Thus a length-\(T\) schedule obeys the pattern precisely when its successive symbols trace a path from \(q_0\) to an accepting state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A schedule pattern is regular when a finite automaton accepts exactly its feasible symbol sequences.

children.title: Automaton–Resource Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between state-based sequence restrictions plus resource feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Automaton–Resource Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-state coupling for finite-state patterns and cumulative bounded resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the augmented state space \(\widehat Q=Q\times\prod_{j=1}^m\{0,\ldots,C_j\}\). From \((q,r)\), a symbol \(a\in\Sigma\) induces a transition to \((\delta(q,a),r+c(a))\) exactly when \(r+c(a)\le C\) componentwise. Starting at \((q_0,0)\), a word \(x\in\Sigma^T\) satisfies both the automaton pattern and the resource bounds if and only if its augmented trajectory is defined at every position and ends in \(F\times\prod_{j=1}^m\{0,\ldots,C_j\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupling pattern states with bounded resource levels converts joint pattern-resource feasibility into path acceptance in a product automaton.
assumptions_latex: Each schedule symbol has a nonnegative integer resource increment, and resource levels are bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility is equivalent to an accepting path in the resource-augmented automaton.
review_flags: Specialized source for automaton-resource product constructions required.

children.title: State-Space Growth Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Automaton expansion caused by numerous counters, histories, or interacting sequence rules.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Growth Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit synchronous products; unreachable-state elimination may reduce the realized size.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For component automata with state sets \(Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\), their explicitly represented reachable synchronous-product state set is contained in \(Q_1\times\cdots\times Q_k\), hence \[N\le\prod_{i=1}^k |Q_i|.\] If every product tuple is reachable, equality holds. In particular, if \(|Q_i|\ge 2\) for every \(i\), instances in which all tuples are reachable have \(N\ge 2^k\). A resource counter with capacity \(C_j\) contributes at most a factor \(C_j+1\), so explicit bounded-counter state spaces can be pseudo-polynomial in numerical capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicitly represented reachable product automaton can contain the product of the component state counts, yielding exponential worst-case growth in the number of components.
assumptions_latex: The coupled construction explicitly stores every reachable combination of component states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit reachable product-state size is bounded by the product of component sizes and can attain that product, causing exponential worst-case growth in the number of coupled components.

notation.meaning: Number of explicitly represented reachable product states
