children.title: Scheduling Propagation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Exchange of domain reductions plus feasibility information across scheduling components.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Propagation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-based finite-domain propagation for scheduling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite-domain store \(D\) and propagators \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\). Initialize \(Q\) with all propagators. While \(Q\ne\varnothing\), remove some \(P_i\), replace \(D\) by \(P_i(D)\), and enqueue every propagator watching a domain changed by that replacement. Stop with failure if any domain becomes empty; otherwise stop when \(Q=\varnothing\). The output store \(D^*\) satisfies \(P_i(D^*)=D^*\) for every \(i\). If all domain lattices are finite and every effective propagation strictly contracts \(D\), the procedure terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling propagation interface repeatedly runs affected sound propagators until domain failure or a common fixpoint is reached.
assumptions_latex: Each propagator is sound: it removes no value extendable to a feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns either a common propagation fixpoint or a detected domain failure.
review_flags: Constraint-programming source with propagation-interface specification required.

children.title: Scheduling Conflict Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Representation plus communication of incompatible scheduling decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Conflict Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause-level conflicts for Booleanized scheduling restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scheduling conflict interface returns a clause \(C=\ell_1\vee\cdots\vee\ell_r\) satisfying \(\mathcal S\models C\), where every \(\ell_i\) is false under the current partial assignment \(A\). The entailment condition makes \(C\) globally valid, while falsification by \(A\) certifies that no completion of \(A\) satisfies \(\mathcal S\). A verifier checks the literal evaluations under \(A\) and validates \(\mathcal S\models C\) through the constraint-specific conflict rule supplied by the propagator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict interface returns a globally valid clause falsified by the current scheduling assignment, certifying infeasibility below that assignment.
assumptions_latex: Every asserted scheduling restriction has an associated Boolean literal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An unsatisfied returned clause is a checkable certificate that the current partial assignment cannot extend to a feasible schedule.
review_flags: Authoritative source for lazy-clause-generation conflict interfaces required.

children.title: Scheduling Explanation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing explanations for propagation outcomes or detected conflicts.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Explanation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Literal explanations for individual scheduling-domain inferences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a propagated literal \(p\), an explanation interface returns antecedents \(E=\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\}\) such that \[\mathcal S\models (e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r)\Rightarrow p.\] Equivalently, it returns the entailed clause \(
eg e_1\vee\cdots\vee
eg e_r\vee p\). The explanation is applicable when every \(e_i\) is true in the current store. For failure, it may return \(\mathcal S\models
eg(e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_r)\), thereby yielding a conflict clause without a consequent literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explanation interface justifies each propagated scheduling literal by an entailed implication from currently true antecedent literals.
assumptions_latex: A propagator performs a sound domain inference under a finite set of antecedent literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned implication or clause certifies the propagated literal and can participate in clause learning.

notation.meaning: Antecedent literals true in the current store

children.title: Propagation–Search Coordination
children.top_down_role: Information flow between scheduling propagators plus search control.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation–Search Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain depth-first search coordinated with propagation and optional learned conflicts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node with store \(D\), compute \(D'=P^*(D)\). Backtrack if \(D'\) contains an empty domain; output the represented schedule if all variables are fixed and all constraints hold. Otherwise choose exhaustive branches \(b_1,\ldots,b_r\) whose disjunction covers every completion represented by \(D'\), and recursively process \(D'\wedge b_j\) for each \(j\). A learned conflict may prune a branch only when it is entailed by the original constraints. Because the domains and branching are finite, the procedure terminates and finds a feasible schedule whenever one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search alternates propagation with exhaustive branching; sound propagation and entailed learning preserve completeness on finite scheduling domains.
assumptions_latex: Propagation terminates at each search node and preserves every feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustive branching with propagation is complete for the finite scheduling model.
review_flags: Constraint-programming source for propagation-search completeness required.

children.title: Explanation Granularity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs in the scope, strength, plus reuse of scheduling explanations.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation Granularity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case size of exact literal explanations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(n\ge 1\), consider a relation \(\mathcal S_n\) in which \(p\) is forced when all antecedents hold: \[\mathcal S_n\models (e_1\wedge\cdots\wedge e_n)\Rightarrow p,\] but, for every \(i\), \(\mathcal S_n\not\models (\bigwedge_{j\ne i}e_j)\Rightarrow p\). Consequently, every sound conjunctive explanation of \(p\) using only these antecedents must contain all \(n\) literals. Thus exact explanations can have linear size in the active reasons, although coarser auxiliary literals may compress them by changing the explanation vocabulary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact explanations may require every active antecedent, so their size can grow linearly unless auxiliary abstractions are introduced.
assumptions_latex: Explanations are clauses over Boolean scheduling literals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is no uniform sublinear bound on exact explanation size without additional structural assumptions.
review_flags: Source required for the explanation-size lower-bound formulation.

children.title: Scheduling Linear Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Continuous relaxations of linear scheduling formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Linear Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous relaxation obtained from a mixed-integer linear scheduling formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X_I=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ x_j\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j\in I\}\), its scheduling linear relaxation is \(X_L=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\), obtained by removing the integrality restrictions while retaining all linear constraints and bounds. Hence \(X_I\subseteq X_L\). For minimization, whenever both optima are well defined, \[\min_{x\in X_L}c^\top x\le \min_{x\in X_I}c^\top x;\] the inequality reverses for maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling linear relaxation drops integrality while retaining linear constraints, producing a polyhedral superset and an optimization bound.
assumptions_latex: The scheduling formulation has linear constraints and designated integrality-restricted variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dropping integrality yields a polyhedral relaxation whose objective value bounds the corresponding integer optimum.

children.title: Scheduling Time-Indexed Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Continuous relaxations retaining discrete time-indexed assignment structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Time-Indexed Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-machine, nonpreemptive, discrete-time start-indexed relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every job \(j\), impose \[\sum_{t\in T_j}x_{jt}=1.\] For every time slot \(\tau\in\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\), impose \[\sum_j\sum_{\substack{t\in T_j:\\ t\le\tau<t+p_j}}x_{jt}\le 1.\] Together with \(0\le x_{jt}\le 1\), these equations define the start-time-indexed linear relaxation. An integral point selects exactly one start for each job and prevents overlapping execution; a fractional point represents a convex distribution of starts subject to aggregate slot capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-indexed relaxations fractionally assign each job to start slots while enforcing aggregate resource capacity in every time slot.
assumptions_latex: Time is discretized as \(\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\), and each job has integer processing time \(p_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed linear system is the standard start-time-indexed relaxation for a single renewable resource of unit capacity.

notation.meaning: Fractional indicator that job j starts at time t
Eligible start times of job j

children.title: Temporal Linking Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxed structures linking assignment, timing, plus resource-use variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Linking Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear links between aggregate temporal variables and time-indexed assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\sum_{t\in T_j}x_{jt}=1\), a first-moment temporal link is \[s_j=\sum_{t\in T_j}t x_{jt}.\] If job \(j\) uses \(a_{jr}\) units of renewable resource \(r\) for \(p_j\) periods, define its slot load by \[y_{r\tau}=\sum_j a_{jr}\sum_{\substack{t\in T_j:\\ t\le\tau<t+p_j}}x_{jt},\qquad y_{r\tau}\le C_r.\] These equalities ensure that aggregate start times and resource loads are projections of the same fractional start assignment; they do not by themselves force any \(x_{jt}\) to be integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal linking equations make aggregate start times and slot loads consistent with the same fractional time-indexed assignment.
assumptions_latex: Both aggregate timing variables and time-indexed start variables describe the same jobs.
Each job \(j\) has processing duration \(p_j\), uses \(a_{jr}\) units of resource \(r\), and resource \(r\) has capacity \(C_r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Moment equations and resource aggregation link the two relaxation layers consistently but do not enforce integrality.

children.title: Time-Indexed Relaxation Strength

assumptions_latex: \(P_{\mathrm{TI}}\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm{TI}}}\) and \(P_{\mathrm A}\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm A}}\) are nonempty scheduling-relaxation polytopes for a minimization problem.
A linear map \(\pi:\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm{TI}}}\to\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm A}}\) satisfies \(\pi(P_{\mathrm{TI}})\subseteq P_{\mathrm A}\).

Objective vectors \(c_{\mathrm{TI}}\in\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm{TI}}}\) and \(c_{\mathrm A}\in\mathbb R^{n_{\mathrm A}}\) satisfy \(c_{\mathrm{TI}}^{\mathsf T}x=c_{\mathrm A}^{\mathsf T}\pi(x)\) for every \(x\in P_{\mathrm{TI}}\).

children.title: Horizon-Driven Relaxation Size
children.top_down_role: Relaxation growth caused by long horizons or fine temporal resolution.

assumptions_latex: Time is discretized as \(T=\{0,\ldots,H-1\}\).
Job \(j\) may start in a set \(T_j\subseteq T\), and one variable \(x_{jt}\) is created for each \(t\in T_j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explicit time-indexed formulation contains exactly \(N_x=\sum_{j\in J}|T_j|\) start variables. Since \(|T_j|\le H\), it follows that \(N_x\le |J|H\). If each resource contributes at most one capacity inequality in each period, the number of such inequalities is at most \(|R|H\). children.title: Scheduling Lagrangian Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-based relaxation of complicating scheduling constraints.

assumptions_latex: The minimization scheduling problem is \(z^*:=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ Ax\ge b\}\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
The Lagrange multiplier satisfies \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[q(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(c^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\bigr)\le z^*,\qquad z_{\mathrm{LD}}:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda)\le z^*.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), the scheduling Lagrangian relaxation obtained by dualizing \(Ax\ge b\) has dual function \[q(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(c^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\bigr).\] Each \(q(\lambda)\) is a lower bound on \(z^*\), and the associated Lagrangian dual bound is \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}:=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m}q(\lambda)\le z^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed vector \(w\ge0\), the surrogate relaxation replaces the system \(Ax\ge b\) by the single inequality \(w^{\mathsf T}Ax\ge w^{\mathsf T}b\), while retaining \(x\in X\). Every schedule satisfying each original inequality satisfies their nonnegative weighted sum; therefore the surrogate feasible set \(X_w\) contains the original feasible set. For minimization, \(z_w:=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X_w\}\) is consequently a valid lower bound on the original optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate relaxation replaces several scheduling inequalities by one nonnegative weighted sum, enlarging the feasible set and yielding a minimization lower bound.

children.title: Resource-Coupling Relaxations

For each \(j\in J\), \(c_j:X_j\to\mathbb R\) is the job-local cost and \(A_j\in\mathbb R^{|R|\times n_j}\) is its resource-use matrix.

children.title: Lagrangian–Surrogate Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Relaxation regimes combining multiplier-based decomposition with surrogate aggregation.

children.title: Dual-Bound Stability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of relaxation bounds to multiplier choices plus decomposition structure.

assumptions_latex: For \(b\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \(q_b(\lambda):=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\}\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\) remain fixed.
The perturbation is \(\delta\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\|\cdot\|_*\) is the dual norm of \(\|\cdot\|\).
The nonempty multiplier set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\|\lambda\|_*\le M<\infty\), and \(q_b(\lambda)\) is finite for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\).

children.title: Convex Quadratic Scheduling Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Convex quadratic relaxations of scheduling interactions or penalties.

assumptions_latex: The relaxed scheduling variables range over a nonempty convex set \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[z_{\mathrm{CQ}}:=\inf_{x\in P}f(x)\le \inf_{x\in F}f(x)\quad\text{for every integral scheduling set }F\subseteq P.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex minimization relaxation with a positive-semidefinite quadratic objective and a convex outer approximation of schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex quadratic scheduling relaxation replaces the integral feasible set \(F\) by a convex set \(P\supseteq F\) and minimizes \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(P\), where \(Q\succeq0\). The positive-semidefinite condition makes \(f\) convex because its Hessian is \(Q\). Since every feasible integral schedule remains feasible in \(P\), the relaxation optimum is a valid lower bound for the original minimization problem. Additional convex quadratic inequalities must likewise have convex sublevel sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic scheduling relaxation minimizes a positive-semidefinite quadratic objective over a convex superset of the integral schedules, yielding a lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Scheduling Relaxations

children.title: Semidefinite Scheduling Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Matrix-based convex relaxations of ordering, assignment, or conflict structures.

assumptions_latex: Binary scheduling decisions are represented by \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), and quadratic products are represented by \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).
All retained linear equalities and inequalities are imposed on \((x,X)\) through a convex set \(\mathcal L\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order semidefinite lifting for binary scheduling variables and quadratic objectives or constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A semidefinite scheduling relaxation replaces the nonconvex identity \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by the convex conditions \[\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\qquad X_{ii}=x_i.\] It retains the chosen linearized scheduling constraints \((x,X)\in\mathcal L\) and replaces every quadratic form \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx\) by \(\langle Q,X\rangle\). Every binary feasible schedule lifted with \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies these conditions, so the lifted feasible region is an outer approximation and its minimization value is a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SDP scheduling relaxation replaces the rank-one product matrix by positive-semidefinite moment and diagonal constraints, preserving all lifted integral schedules.

assumptions_latex: The original decision vector is \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
The lifted matrix is intended to satisfy \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical matrix lifting of pairwise products; rank removal produces a convex outer approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Quadratic monomials \(x_ix_j\) are represented by entries \(X_{ij}\) of a symmetric lifted matrix. Exact lifting requires \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), equivalently the augmented matrix \(Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\) to be positive semidefinite with rank one. Dropping only the rank constraint yields \(Y\succeq0\), which is equivalent by the Schur complement to \(X-xx^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Linear identities valid for products of the scheduling variables may be added to tighten this convex lifted region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic products are represented by a lifted matrix; dropping the augmented matrix's rank-one condition while retaining positive semidefiniteness gives a convex relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise precedence-matrix relaxation using antisymmetry and directed-triangle inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordering-matrix relaxation assigns a continuous variable \(y_{ij}\in[0,1]\) to each ordered pair of distinct jobs. Antisymmetry is imposed by \(y_{ij}+y_{ji}=1\). Every strict total order contains no directed three-cycle, so it satisfies \(y_{ij}+y_{jk}+y_{ki}\le2\) for all distinct \(i,j,k\). Hence the polyhedron \(\mathcal O_n\) containing these bounds and equations includes every integral precedence matrix. Fractional matrices in \(\mathcal O_n\) need not represent total orders, so linking constraints or stronger lifted inequalities may be required for scheduling applications.

children.title: Convex Relaxation Scalability
children.top_down_role: Computational limits associated with lifted quadratic or matrix representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Relaxation Scalability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-model scalability of a lifted convex scheduling relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a convex body, let \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^d\), and let \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose a known rational point \(a\in\mathbb{Q}^d\) and known radii \(0<r\leq R\) satisfy \[B(a,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(a,R),\] and suppose a strong separation oracle for \(K\) has running time \(T_{\mathrm{sep}}(d,L)\), where \(L\) bounds the rational input and oracle-output encoding lengths. The ellipsoid method returns \(x_\varepsilon\in K\) satisfying \[c^{\mathsf T}x_\varepsilon\leq \inf_{x\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x+\varepsilon\] using a number of oracle calls polynomial in \(d\), \(L\), \(\log(R/r)\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). Consequently, the oracle running time is polynomial in these quantities and in \(T_{\mathrm{sep}}(d,L)\). This is polynomial in the lifted dimension, but need not be polynomial in the original scheduling dimension when the lifting has exponential size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With explicit geometric bounds and a strong separation oracle, a lifted convex scheduling relaxation can be optimized to additive accuracy in oracle time polynomial in its lifted dimension and logarithmic accuracy. An exponentially large lifting can therefore remain intractable relative to the original scheduling model.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb{N}\), \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^d\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
\(B(a,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(a,R)\) for a known rational center \(a\) and known radii \(0<r\leq R\).
The rational input and oracle-output encoding lengths are bounded by \(L\).
A strong separation oracle for \(K\) runs in time \(T_{\mathrm{sep}}(d,L)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{oracle}}=\operatorname{poly}(d,L,\log(R/r),\log(1/\varepsilon))\).

notation.meaning: known center of the geometric bounding balls

children.title: Machine-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scheduling partitions organized around individual machines or machine groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Machine-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of a scheduling formulation by machines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be the machine set and let \((M_k)_{k=1}^q\) be a partition of \(M\). A machine-based decomposition assigns to block \(k\) all local variables and constraints involving only machines in \(M_k\), producing a feasible set \(X_k\). Variables duplicated across blocks, job-flow constraints spanning different machine blocks, and other global restrictions are represented by coupling equations \[\sum_{k=1}^q A_kx_k=b.\] The decomposed formulation is \[\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^q f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^qA_kx_k=b\right\}.\] It is separable by machine blocks after the coupling equations are relaxed or assigned to a coordinating master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Machines are partitioned into blocks; each block owns its local scheduling constraints, while job transfers and other cross-machine restrictions remain explicit coupling constraints.
assumptions_latex: \((M_k)_{k=1}^q\) is a disjoint partition of the machine set \(M\).
Every nonlocal constraint is retained in the coupling system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxing \(\sum_{k=1}^qA_kx_k=b\) separates the formulation into the subproblems \(x_k\in X_k\).

notation.meaning: local feasible schedules for machine block k

children.title: Resource-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scheduling partitions organized around shared resource classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition by renewable, consumable, or cumulative resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the resource set and let \((R_k)_{k=1}^q\) partition \(R\). A resource-based decomposition forms a local feasible set \(X_k\) containing scheduling variables and capacity constraints associated with resources in \(R_k\). When an activity uses resources from several blocks, its relevant variables may be copied as \(x_k\), and consistency is imposed by equations \(E_kx_k=z\) for a shared activity representation \(z\). The global formulation is decomposed into local objectives and sets, together with these consistency equations and any constraints involving aggregate consumption across resource blocks. Relaxing the shared equations yields independent resource-block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resources are partitioned into blocks. Each block enforces local capacities, while copied activity decisions and aggregate consumption are reconciled through explicit consistency constraints.
assumptions_latex: \((R_k)_{k=1}^q\) is a disjoint partition of \(R\).
Copies of every cross-block activity decision are linked to a shared representation \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relaxing \(E_kx_k=z\) for all \(k\) separates the resource-block feasible sets \(X_k\).

notation.meaning: local schedules satisfying capacities in block k
shared representation of cross-block activity decisions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits resource-based decomposition, but the copied-variable construction and claimed separation require a scheduling or decomposition source with a specific locator.

children.title: Job-Based Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scheduling partitions organized around jobs, orders, or job families.

knowledge_statements.title: Job-Based Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of a scheduling formulation by jobs or job families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be the job set and let \((J_k)_{k=1}^q\) partition \(J\). A job-based decomposition assigns to block \(k\) the variables, precedence constraints, release dates, deadlines, and route restrictions belonging to jobs in \(J_k\), defining a local set \(X_k\). Machine or resource capacities shared by different job blocks remain as coupling inequalities \[\sum_{k=1}^q A_kx_k\leq b.\] The resulting formulation has the form \[\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^q f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^qA_kx_k\leq b\right\}.\] Dualizing the shared capacities separates optimization by job block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jobs are partitioned into blocks that retain their local routes and precedences; shared machine or resource capacities couple the otherwise independent job-block schedules.
assumptions_latex: \((J_k)_{k=1}^q\) is a disjoint partition of the job set \(J\).
All capacities shared by multiple job blocks appear in the coupling system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dualizing \(\sum_{k=1}^qA_kx_k\leq b\) produces independent optimizations over \(X_k\).

notation.meaning: locally feasible schedules for jobs in block k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and shared-capacity coupling fit job-based decomposition, but the scheduling specialization and dual-separation claim have no cited support.

children.title: Cross-Partition Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of timing, capacity, plus precedence across decomposition blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Partition Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian coordination of partitioned scheduling subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the partitioned problem \[v^*=\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^q f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^qA_kx_k=b\right\}.\] For multiplier \(\lambda\), define \[\theta_k(\lambda)=\inf_{x_k\in X_k}\bigl(f_k(x_k)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_kx_k\bigr),\qquad \theta(\lambda)=\sum_{k=1}^q\theta_k(\lambda)-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b.\] Cross-partition coordination consists of solving the independent block problems defining \(\theta_k\), aggregating their coupling residual \(g(\lambda)=\sum_kA_kx_k(\lambda)-b\), and updating \(\lambda\) to maximize \(\theta\). Every multiplier gives the lower bound \(\theta(\lambda)\leq v^*\); primal feasibility additionally requires zero coupling residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinator prices cross-block constraints, solves independent block schedules, and updates prices from their aggregate residual. Dual values bound the optimum; zero residual restores global feasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_k\) is nonempty and each displayed infimum is finite at the multiplier considered.
The undecomposed problem is a minimization problem with equality coupling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta(\lambda)\leq v^*\), and coordinated block solutions are globally feasible when \(g(\lambda)=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Lagrangian formulas are standard, but no source supports this coordination construction. A source is also needed to determine whether the leaf should contain a dual representation or a fully specified coordination algorithm.

children.title: Shared-Resource Coupling Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Dependencies that weaken separability across machine, resource, or job partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Resource Coupling Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local feasibility fails to imply global shared-resource feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two partition blocks each schedule one unit-duration activity during the same slot \(t\). Both activities require one unit of a shared resource whose global capacity is \(1\). If each block checks only its own local constraint, then its usage satisfies \(u_k(t)=1\leq1\) for \(k\in\{1,2\}\), so both local schedules are feasible. Their union violates the true shared constraint because \[u_1(t)+u_2(t)=2>1.\] Hence a partition boundary may omit a resource only when no capacity row contains decisions from both sides; otherwise that capacity row, or an equivalent allocation or price mechanism, must remain in the coordination interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two locally feasible blocks can simultaneously overuse one shared resource. Any capacity involving decisions from multiple blocks must remain explicitly coordinated.
assumptions_latex: The shared resource has unit capacity in slot \(t\).
Each of two blocks independently schedules one unit of usage in slot \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local feasibility does not imply \(u_1(t)+u_2(t)\leq1\).

notation.meaning: resource usage contributed by block k in slot t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly illustrates a shared-resource coupling boundary and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the general interface claim lacks cited support.

children.title: Time-Stage Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scheduling partitions aligned with successive planning stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Stage Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic scheduling decomposition into ordered decision stages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let decision epochs satisfy \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_K=T\). A time-stage decomposition assigns decisions executed in \([\tau_{k-1},\tau_k)\) to stage \(k\), with local decision \(x_k\), incoming state \(s_{k-1}\), and outgoing state determined by \[s_k=F_k(s_{k-1},x_k).\] The state contains precisely the information needed by later stages, such as unfinished operations, remaining processing, resource inventories, and machine availability. A feasible global schedule is a sequence satisfying every local stage constraint and every state-transition equation. Conditional on the incoming state, each stage contains no decision whose execution lies wholly outside its interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The horizon is divided into ordered stages. Each stage optimizes local decisions and passes sufficient completion, inventory, and availability information to the next stage.
assumptions_latex: \(0=\tau_0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_K=T\).
All cross-stage consequences are encoded in the transferred state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global feasibility requires \(s_k=F_k(s_{k-1},x_k)\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\).

notation.meaning: state at the end of stage k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The staged state-transition definition fits the leaf, but the asserted sufficiency and temporal assignment conditions require an inspectable temporal-decomposition source.

children.title: Horizon Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Scheduling partitions aligned with contiguous or overlapping temporal windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of a finite scheduling horizon into temporal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite horizon \([0,T)\), choose intervals \(I_k=[a_k,b_k)\) whose union covers \([0,T)\); adjacent intervals may be disjoint or overlap. A horizon decomposition assigns activities executed wholly inside \(I_k\) to subproblem \(k\). Activities crossing an endpoint, together with resource inventories, machine states, and precedence information needed beyond that endpoint, are represented by boundary variables \(y_k\). Local feasible sets \(X_k(y_{k-1},y_k)\) are coordinated by requiring equal values for every boundary quantity shared by adjacent subproblems. The decomposition is exact when compatible local solutions can be concatenated bijectively into globally feasible schedules with the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite horizon is covered by temporal subproblems linked through boundary variables. Exactness requires compatible local schedules to concatenate into one global schedule without changing cost.
assumptions_latex: The intervals \((I_k)_{k=1}^K\) cover \([0,T)\).
Every activity or resource state crossing an interval endpoint is represented in boundary data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness holds when compatible members of \(X_k(y_{k-1},y_k)\) concatenate bijectively to globally feasible schedules.

notation.meaning: boundary data shared by adjacent subhorizons
local feasible set on subhorizon k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the version allowing overlapping intervals does not specify ownership and consistency throughout overlap regions; adjacent endpoint variables alone need not ensure exactness.

children.title: Rolling-Horizon Coordination
children.top_down_role: Repeated coordination across moving planning windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Rolling-Horizon Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Receding-horizon scheduling with a fixed commitment window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given current time \(t_0\), look-ahead length \(H>0\), commitment length \(0<\Delta\leq H\), initial state \(s_0\), and terminal surrogate \(V\), repeat for \(n=0,1,\ldots\): solve the scheduling model on \([t_n,t_n+H)\) from state \(s_n\), adding \(V(s(t_n+H))\) to its local objective; select an optimal or prescribed-accuracy solution \(x^{(n)}\); irrevocably implement only its decisions in \([t_n,t_n+\Delta)\); observe the resulting state \(s_{n+1}\); and set \(t_{n+1}=t_n+\Delta\). Stop when the global horizon ends. The output is the concatenation of all committed decision segments, not the discarded tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly optimize a look-ahead window, commit its first segment, update the observed state, and advance. The final schedule concatenates only committed segments.
assumptions_latex: \(H>0\) and \(0<\Delta\leq H\).
Each window is initialized with the state produced by previously committed decisions.
Committed decisions are fixed in all later windows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{\mathrm{out}}=x^{(0)}|_{[t_0,t_0+\Delta)}\mathbin{\Vert}x^{(1)}|_{[t_1,t_1+\Delta)}\mathbin{\Vert}\cdots\).

notation.meaning: observed state at rolling iteration n

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content_kind and receding-horizon steps fit rolling-horizon coordination, but the algorithm and terminal-surrogate formulation lack a cited scheduling source.

children.title: Interstage State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Carryover information linking adjacent temporal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Interstage State Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition linking consecutive temporal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For adjacent stages \(k\) and \(k+1\), let \(s_k^+\) be the state produced at the end of stage \(k\), and let \(s_{k+1}^-\) be the state assumed at the start of stage \(k+1\). Interstage state transfer is consistent exactly when \[s_{k+1}^-=s_k^+=F_k(s_k^-,x_k).\] The state must include every cross-boundary quantity affecting future feasibility or cost, including unfinished operations with remaining processing, machine release times, resource inventories, and carried commitments. If the state is sufficient, the feasibility and continuation cost of later decisions depend on the past only through \(s_{k+1}^-\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consecutive stages must agree on the boundary state, which must retain every past quantity affecting later feasibility or cost.
assumptions_latex: Stage \(k\) has incoming state \(s_k^-\), decision \(x_k\), and transition map \(F_k\).
The chosen state description is sufficient for all later constraints and costs.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality is a suitable interstage consistency condition, but the stronger sufficient-state claim concerning all future feasibility and cost needs a source.

children.title: Temporal Boundary Effects
children.top_down_role: Schedule distortion caused by stage cuts, terminal approximations, or short lookahead.

knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Boundary Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary truncation can make locally optimal temporal schedules globally poor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider one machine, a boundary time \(B\), and a nonpreemptive job \(j\) released at \(B-1\) with processing time \(2\) and deadline \(B+1\). If the first subhorizon is \([0,B)\) and excludes jobs that cannot finish before \(B\), it may leave the machine idle at \(B-1\). A later subproblem starting at \(B\) cannot complete \(j\) by \(B+1\), although the global schedule starting \(j\) at \(B-1\) is feasible. Thus truncation is exact only when crossing activities and their continuation states are represented, or when a valid terminal condition makes their omission immaterial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subhorizon that ignores work crossing its endpoint can reject a globally necessary early start, causing infeasibility or avoidable cost after concatenation.
assumptions_latex: Job \(j\) is nonpreemptive, released at \(B-1\), has processing time \(2\), and deadline \(B+1\).
The first subproblem forbids activities finishing after \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposed policy misses the feasible global interval \([B-1,B+1)\) for job \(j\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The example is internally coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the general exactness condition concerning crossing activities or terminal conditions is unsupported.

children.title: Master-Schedule Coordination
children.top_down_role: Global scheduling choices represented in a coordinating master problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Schedule Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master coordination of schedule columns and pricing subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(k\), let \(S_k\) be its feasible schedules, with column cost \(c_{kr}\) and shared-resource vector \(a_{kr}\) for \(r\in S_k\). Initialize nonempty restricted sets \(R_k\subseteq S_k\). Repeatedly solve \[\min\sum_{k,r\in R_k}c_{kr}\lambda_{kr}\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{r\in R_k}\lambda_{kr}=1,\ \sum_{k,r\in R_k}a_{kr}\lambda_{kr}\leq b,\ \lambda_{kr}\geq0.\] From the master dual variables, solve each block's pricing problem for a minimum-reduced-cost schedule. Add every column with negative reduced cost and repeat. Stop when none exists; the restricted-master solution then solves the full linear master. Integer implementation may require branching or another integrality mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master combines schedule columns under shared capacities, while pricing subproblems generate negative-reduced-cost schedules. Absence of such columns certifies optimality of the linear master.
assumptions_latex: Each block has a nonempty feasible schedule set \(S_k\).
Pricing finds a globally minimum-reduced-cost column for each block.
The displayed master is feasible and bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every omitted column has nonnegative reduced cost, the current solution is optimal for the full linear master over \(S_k\).

notation.meaning: weight assigned to schedule column r of block k
shared-resource use of a schedule column
current restricted column set for block k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm accurately describes restricted-master column generation and distinguishes linear-master optimality from integer implementation, but neither the column-generation result nor its scheduling specialization has an inspectable citation.

children.title: Scheduling Pricing Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Generation of improving schedules, paths, patterns, or configurations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Pricing Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-generation pricing over feasible schedules for a minimization master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be the set of feasible schedules, with column cost \(c_s\) and master-column vector \(a_s\) for each \(s\in\mathcal S\). Given dual multipliers \(\pi\) for the master constraints, the scheduling pricing subproblem is \[z_{\mathrm{price}}(\pi)=\min_{s\in\mathcal S}\{c_s-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_s\}.\] Under the reduced-cost convention for a minimization master, a schedule \(s\) is an improving column exactly when \(c_s-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_s<0\). If \(z_{\mathrm{price}}(\pi)\ge 0\), no omitted schedule has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over feasible schedules; a negative optimum supplies an improving master column, while a nonnegative optimum certifies that none is missing.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) contains precisely the schedules admissible for one generated column.
The restricted master is a minimization problem and \(\pi\) is dual-feasible for its current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{price}}(\pi)<0\) yields an improving column, whereas \(z_{\mathrm{price}}(\pi)\ge 0\) excludes every omitted negative-reduced-cost column.

notation.meaning: Set of feasible schedules represented by columns
Master coefficients and cost of schedule column s

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-cost formulation is mathematically standard and fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation supports its scheduling-specific interpretation or stopping certificate; the local inventory does not supply such evidence.

children.title: Master–Pricing Coupling
children.top_down_role: Information exchange between global coordination plus schedule generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Master–Pricing Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-price interface between a restricted schedule master and its pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For columns \(s\in\mathcal S'\subseteq\mathcal S\), consider the restricted master \[\min\left\{\sum_{s\in\mathcal S'}c_s\lambda_s: \sum_{s\in\mathcal S'}a_s\lambda_s\ge b,\ \lambda_s\ge0\right\}.\] If \(\pi\ge0\) is an optimal dual vector, pricing evaluates \(\bar c_s=c_s-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_s\) over \(\mathcal S\). A column with \(\bar c_s<0\) is appended to \(\mathcal S'\), changing the next master solution and hence the next price vector. Termination occurs when the minimum reduced cost is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master sends dual prices to pricing; pricing returns a negative-reduced-cost schedule, and the enlarged master produces new prices until no improving column remains.
assumptions_latex: The displayed restricted master is feasible and bounded.
Pricing is solved exactly over the full schedule set \(\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master–pricing loop terminates only when \(\min_{s\in\mathcal S}(c_s-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_s)\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Current restricted set of schedule columns
Master weight assigned to schedule s
Reduced cost of schedule column s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard restricted-master and pricing coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes the restricted-master/pricing interface under the stated exact-pricing assumptions, but it has no source with a specific locator.

children.title: Pricing Decomposition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Pricing partitions by machine, resource, job family, route, or time block.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Decomposition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient structural criterion for independent solution of schedule-pricing blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb N\) with \(K\ge 1\), let the pricing decision be \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_K)\), and suppose \[X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_K,\qquad \bar c(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\bar c_k(x_k).\] Then \[\inf_{x\in X}\bar c(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K\inf_{x_k\in X_k}\bar c_k(x_k).\] If all infima are attained, independently optimal block decisions form an optimal joint pricing decision. Constraints or reduced-cost terms that genuinely couple two or more blocks invalidate this product-additive regime and require joint pricing or an additional coordination decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product feasibility and additive reduced cost are sufficient for independent block pricing. Constraints or cost terms that genuinely couple blocks require joint pricing or another coordination layer.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb N\) and \(K\ge 1\).
Each block set \(X_k\) is nonempty.
Each function \(\bar c_k:X_k\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is bounded below if a finite optimal value is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Product feasibility and additive reduced cost imply independent block pricing and an additive infimum; attained block minima combine into a joint minimizer.

notation.meaning: Feasible decision set for pricing block k
Contribution of block k to reduced cost

children.title: Pricing Tractability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural features that make scheduling pricing subproblems difficult.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Tractability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundary induced by the exact reduced-cost scheduling oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) encode a scheduling-pricing instance and let the decision problem ask whether \[\min_{s\in\mathcal S(I)}\{c_s-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_s\}<0.\] If this decision and a witnessing schedule are computable in time polynomial in \(|I|\), each exact column-generation pricing call is polynomial-time. If the decision problem is NP-hard for a scheduling subclass, then an exact pricing oracle for that subclass is NP-hard unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\). This boundary concerns a pricing call and does not by itself imply polynomial total column-generation time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial pricing makes each oracle call tractable; NP-hard negative-column detection makes exact pricing NP-hard, without determining the total number of master iterations.
assumptions_latex: Instances and dual prices have finite rational encodings.
Pricing ranges over the full feasible schedule family represented by the formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: NP-hardness of negative-reduced-cost detection is a tractability boundary for exact pricing, while polynomial detection controls only per-call complexity.

notation.meaning: Binary encoding length of the instance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: oracle complexity follows the pricing decision problem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The per-call tractability boundary and warning about total column-generation time fit this failure-boundary leaf, but the complexity claims lack an inspectable scheduling or column-generation source.

knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based Benders Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master assignment decisions coordinated with a combinatorial scheduling subproblem through valid logical cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given master variables \(y\in Y\), initialize a master containing the linking objective and no subproblem cuts. At iteration \(t\), solve it for \(y^t\), then solve the scheduling subproblem \(Q(y^t)\). If \(Q(y^t)\) is infeasible, add a valid feasibility cut excluding \(y^t\) and every other assignment certified infeasible by the same explanation. If it is feasible with value \(q^t\), update the incumbent and add a valid optimality cut \(\theta\ge B_t(y)\), where \(B_t(y^t)=q^t\) and \(B_t(y)\le Q(y)\). Stop when the master bound meets the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master proposes assignments; a scheduling solver returns infeasibility explanations or objective bounds, which become valid cuts until lower and upper bounds coincide.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is finite, or the generated cuts ensure finite convergence.
Every feasibility and optimality cut is valid for all \(y\in Y\).
Each scheduling subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon equality of the master bound and incumbent value, the incumbent is globally optimal for the decomposed model.

notation.meaning: Optimal scheduling-subproblem value, infinite if infeasible

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm gives a coherent logic-based Benders scheme with valid global cuts and an appropriate bound-equality stopping condition, but no authoritative source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reported limitations of AMD's Real Time Dispatch implementation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded, case-specific account of AMD's historical RTD implementation; these limitations are not asserted for all priority-dispatching systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{AMD's RTD dynamically selected work using priority rules including ERD, EDD, and minimum slack. Reported limitations were insufficient scheduled-time visibility, inability to react to changes or unforeseen events, lack of compliance tracking, insufficient assessment of rule impacts, and inability to comprehend and respond to relevant factory events.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AMD's Real Time Dispatch tool dynamically selected work using priority rules such as earliest release date, earliest due date, and minimum slack. Its reported limitations concerned scheduled-time visibility, reactions to changes or unforeseen events, compliance tracking, assessment of rule impacts, and responses to relevant factory events.
assumptions_latex: \text{The claim is restricted to the described historical AMD RTD implementation.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{That implementation exhibited the five reported operational limitations.}

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Attribute Dispatching Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonpreemptive local dispatching using one operation attribute at each decision epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J\) be a finite operation set. At a decision epoch \(t\), choose an idle machine \(m\) and form the set \(E_m(t)\subseteq J\) of unscheduled operations that are eligible to start on \(m\). Fix one scalar attribute \(a_j(t)\) and a direction \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\). When \(E_m(t)\ne\varnothing\), select \[j^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in E_m(t)}\sigma a_j(t),\] resolve ties by a fixed deterministic rule, and start \(j^*\) nonpreemptively on \(m\). Update the state after each scheduling event. When no operation is eligible, advance to the next event that can change eligibility, if one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each decision epoch, an idle machine ranks its eligible operations by one scalar attribute, starts the best-ranked operation using a fixed tie-breaker, and updates the state at later events.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite.
Processing is nonpreemptive.
\(E_m(t)\) contains exactly the operations permitted to start on machine \(m\) under the rule's modeled eligibility constraints.
The machine-selection and tie-breaking conventions are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The specified ranking, machine-selection, event-advance, and tie-breaking conventions define a deterministic local dispatch policy that starts only eligible operations.

notation.meaning: Operations eligible to start on machine m at time t
Single priority attribute of operation j

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Dispatching Rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dispatching by an explicit aggregation of multiple normalized scheduling attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each decision epoch \(t\), let \(E(t)\) be the eligible operations. For each \(j\in E(t)\), compute attributes \(a_{jr}(t)\) for \(r=1,\ldots,m\), normalize them by fixed maps \(g_r\), and form \[P_j(t)=\sum_{r=1}^m w_r g_r(a_{jr}(t)),\qquad w_r\in\mathbb R.\] Dispatch an operation in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in E(t)}P_j(t)\), using a fixed tie-breaker; then update all state-dependent attributes. The scaling maps and weights are part of the rule and must remain specified for reproducibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite rule normalizes several operation attributes, combines them with fixed weights, and dispatches the eligible operation having the best aggregate score.
assumptions_latex: Every normalized attribute is defined for every eligible operation.
The score direction and tie-breaking convention are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The specified normalized score defines a reproducible priority ordering on each finite eligible set.

notation.meaning: Attribute r of operation j at time t
Normalization or transformation of attribute r
Weight assigned to transformed attribute r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted normalized score is a valid algorithmic instance of a composite dispatching rule and the conclusion is appropriately limited to reproducible ordering, but no inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Apparent Tardiness Cost dispatching rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite priority heuristic for the single-machine total weighted tardiness problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1\parallel\sum_j w_jT_j\), whenever the machine becomes free at time \(t\), compute for every remaining job \(j\)
\[
I_j(t)=\frac{w_j}{p_j}\exp\!\left(-\frac{\max\{d_j-p_j-t,0\}}{K\bar p}\right),
\]
where \(K>0\) is a look-ahead scaling parameter and \(\bar p\) is the average processing time of the remaining jobs, and process next a job attaining the maximum index. For very large \(K\), ATC reduces to WSPT. For very small \(K\), it reduces to minimum slack when no jobs are overdue; otherwise, overdue jobs are ranked according to WSPT. Instance-dependent selection of \(K\) may use
\[
\tau=1-\frac{\sum_j d_j}{nC_{\max}},\qquad R=\frac{d_{\max}-d_{\min}}{C_{\max}}.
\]
Values of \(\tau\) near one indicate tight due dates and values near zero indicate loose due dates, while larger \(R\) indicates a wider due-date range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever the single machine becomes free, ATC assigns each remaining job its weighted-shortest-processing-time factor multiplied by an exponential penalty for positive slack, then selects a maximum-index job. A very large look-ahead parameter yields WSPT. A very small parameter yields minimum slack when no jobs are overdue and WSPT ranking for overdue jobs otherwise. Due-date tightness and range statistics may guide instance-dependent parameter selection.
assumptions_latex: p_j>0\quad\text{for every remaining job }j
\bar p=\frac{1}{|U|}\sum_{j\in U}p_j\quad\text{for the nonempty remaining-job set }U
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in U}I_j(t)\quad\text{is processed next.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite dispatching rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic-scheduling ranking expression assembled from elementary job- or machine-attribute rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A composite dispatching rule is a ranking expression combining elementary dispatching rules. Each elementary rule is a function of constant or time-dependent job or machine attributes and has its own scaling parameter. A scaling parameter may be fixed or may vary with time or with the job set. Job-set-dependent parameters are obtained by applying predetermined functions to instance statistics, which usually do not depend on the schedule. For each instance, the required statistics are computed, the scaling parameters are set, and the resulting ranking expression is applied to generate a schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite dispatching rule combines elementary ranking rules based on job or machine attributes. Each component has a scaling parameter that may be fixed, time-dependent, or determined from instance statistics. These statistics usually do not depend on the schedule; predetermined functions map them to parameter values before the combined rule is applied.
assumptions_latex: \text{Each elementary rule is a function of job and/or machine attributes.}
\text{Each elementary rule has an associated scaling parameter.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The scaled elementary rules form a ranking expression used to generate a schedule.}

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Priority Indices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-dependent priorities recomputed whenever scheduling events alter urgency or eligibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x(t)\) denote the scheduling state at decision epoch \(t\). For every eligible operation \(j\in E(x(t))\), evaluate a prescribed index \(P_j(x(t),t)\). Dispatch \[j^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{j\in E(x(t))}P_j(x(t),t),\] apply the selected operation until the next permitted decision epoch, update \(x(t)\), and recompute all affected indices. A priority index is dynamic when there exist an operation \(j\) and two reachable states or times for which its index values differ despite unchanged static job data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic rule recomputes eligible operations' indices after relevant events, allowing priorities to change with time, queues, remaining work, or machine state.
assumptions_latex: Decision epochs and the state-transition rule are specified.
The eligible set is finite at every decision epoch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repeated state updates and index recomputation define the resulting event-driven dispatch policy.

notation.meaning: Scheduling state at decision epoch t
Operations eligible in the current state
Dynamic priority index of operation j

children.title: Scheduling Enumeration Trees
children.top_down_role: Tree representations of partial scheduling decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Enumeration Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted search-tree representation of partial schedules and their feasible completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scheduling enumeration tree is a rooted tree \(T=(V,E)\) whose node \(v\in V\) represents a partial schedule \(S_v\) and a completion set \(F(v)\subseteq\mathcal F\), where \(\mathcal F\) is the finite set of complete feasible schedules. The root \(r\) satisfies \(F(r)=\mathcal F\). For every nonterminal node \(v\) with child set \(C(v)\), exact coverage requires \[F(v)=\bigcup_{u\in C(v)}F(u).\] Duplicate-free branching additionally requires \(F(u)\cap F(w)=\varnothing\) for distinct \(u,w\in C(v)\). Enumeration is terminally complete when every leaf \(\ell\) satisfies \(|F(\ell)|\le 1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each node represents a partial schedule and its feasible completions. Children cover the parent's completions, disjoint children prevent duplicates, and leaves must contain at most one completion for individual schedules to be enumerated.
assumptions_latex: The complete feasible-schedule set \(\mathcal F\) is finite.
Branching preserves every feasible completion unless a sound pruning certificate removes its node.
Every unpruned leaf \(\ell\) satisfies \(|F(\ell)|\le 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Visiting every unpruned terminal leaf enumerates every completion not removed by sound pruning, and enumerates it exactly once when sibling completion sets are pairwise disjoint.

notation.meaning: Partial schedule represented by node v
Complete feasible schedules extending node v

children.title: Scheduling Bounding Families
children.top_down_role: Lower or upper bound families used within exact scheduling search.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Bounding Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid objective bounds attached to partial schedules in minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization scheduling problem with objective \(f\), a lower-bounding function assigns each search node \(v\) a value \(L(v)\) satisfying \[L(v)\le \min_{S\in F(v)}f(S),\] with the minimum interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(F(v)=\varnothing\). Any feasible complete schedule \(\widehat S\) supplies the upper bound \(U=f(\widehat S)\). Consequently, \(L(v)\ge U\) certifies that no completion below the incumbent exists at \(v\). Relaxation, resource-capacity, precedence, and objective-component bounds are valid only when they satisfy the displayed inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node lower bound underestimates every completion's objective, while an incumbent supplies an upper bound; comparison can certify that a subtree cannot improve.
assumptions_latex: The scheduling objective is minimized.
\(F(v)\) is the set of feasible completions of node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(v)\ge U\) certifies that node \(v\) contains no solution strictly improving the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound at search node v
Objective value of an incumbent feasible schedule
Feasible completions represented by node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower- and upper-bound certificates are correct for minimization and fit the bounding-family leaf, but no authoritative scheduling branch-and-bound citation is provided.

children.title: Scheduling Branching Schemes
children.top_down_role: Branching choices based on jobs, machines, positions, times, or conflicts.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Branching Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for branching on scheduling decisions in exact search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a search node \(v\), a branching scheme selects predicates \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) on complete schedules and creates children with \[F(v_i)=\{S\in F(v):B_i(S)\}.\] The branching is complete when \(F(v)=\bigcup_{i=1}^kF(v_i)\), and it is nonredundant when these child sets are pairwise disjoint. Examples include fixing the next operation, imposing one orientation of a machine-order disjunction, or partitioning a start-time domain. Exact search requires completeness; pairwise disjointness is optional for correctness but prevents duplicate exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid branch partitions or covers all completions using decisions such as next-operation choice, precedence orientation, or start-time-domain splitting.
assumptions_latex: Each branching predicate is decidable for a complete schedule.
Child constraints are consistent with the partial schedule at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coverage of \(F(v)\) preserves exactness, and pairwise disjoint child sets additionally eliminate duplicate enumeration.

notation.meaning: Child node associated with predicate i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Coverage is correctly identified as necessary for exact branching, while disjointness is correctly treated as optional for correctness. The record nevertheless lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Scheduling Node-Pruning Criteria
children.top_down_role: Dominance, infeasibility, plus incumbent-based pruning regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Node-Pruning Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound fathoming tests for a minimization scheduling search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let node \(v\) represent completion set \(F(v)\), let \(L(v)\) be a valid lower bound, and let \(U\) be the incumbent objective. Node \(v\) may be pruned if at least one certificate holds: \[F(v)=\varnothing,\qquad L(v)\ge U,\qquad\text{or}\qquad \exists w\;\forall S\in F(v)\;\exists S'\in F(w):f(S')\le f(S),\] where node \(w\) is retained or already resolved. These are respectively infeasibility, bound, and dominance certificates. Each removes only completions that cannot yield a strictly better feasible schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search node is safely pruned when it is infeasible, its bound cannot beat the incumbent, or another retained node dominates all its completions.
assumptions_latex: The objective \(f\) is minimized.
\(L(v)\) is valid for every completion in \(F(v)\).
Any dominance relation used is valid over the complete represented sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pruning under any displayed certificate preserves at least one globally optimal schedule outside the discarded subtree.

notation.meaning: Feasible completions represented by node v
Valid lower bound at node v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard infeasibility, bound, and dominance fathoming tests

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The infeasibility, bound, and setwise-dominance certificates are mathematically coherent and appropriately classified as pruning certificates, but no authoritative source with a specific locator supports them.

children.title: Bound-Quality Search Limits
children.top_down_role: Search growth caused by weak scheduling bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Quality Search Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential search caused by a valid but non-discriminating lower bound when no other rule fathoms internal nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a complete binary branch-and-bound tree of depth \(n\in\mathbb N\) for a minimization problem with optimum \(z^*\). Suppose every nonterminal node \(v\) has the valid lower bound \(L(v)=L_0<z^*\), every incumbent value satisfies \(U\ge z^*\), and no nonterminal node is fathomed by infeasibility, integrality, dominance, or any rule other than the bound test \(L(v)\ge U\). That bound test fails at every nonterminal node, so the search visits all \(2^{n+1}-1\) nodes and inspects all \(2^n\) leaves. Thus validity of node bounds alone gives no polynomial search-size guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a complete binary tree with no other internal-node fathoming, a uniformly weak valid lower bound makes every bound-pruning test fail and forces exponentially many nodes to be explored.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\), and the search tree is complete and binary with depth \(n\).
\(L(v)=L_0<z^*\) at every nonterminal node, while \(U\ge z^*\).
No nonterminal node is fathomed by any rule other than \(L(v)\ge U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{visited}}=2^{n+1}-1\) and \(N_{\mathrm{leaves}}=2^n\).

children.title: Scheduling Enumeration Frameworks

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Enumeration Frameworks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact branch-and-cut framework for a finite mixed-integer scheduling formulation under explicit finite-termination conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization scheduling formulation, initialize a root node containing its relaxation and no incumbent. Repeatedly select an open node \(v\), solve its current relaxation exactly to obtain the lower bound \(L_v\), and discard the node if the relaxation is infeasible or \(L_v\ge U\), where \(U\) is the incumbent value. Otherwise, add valid scheduling cuts and reoptimize until the node's finite cut phase ends. If the resulting solution is integer feasible, update \(U\); otherwise apply a branching disjunction whose children cover the parent node's integer-feasible completions and strictly fix at least one previously unresolved choice. If there are finitely many such choices, the process terminates when no node remains and returns an optimal schedule, or correctly reports infeasibility when no incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under exact relaxation solves, finite cut phases, and branching that strictly resolves finitely many scheduling choices, branch-and-cut terminates with an optimal schedule or a correct infeasibility report.
assumptions_latex: The scheduling formulation has finitely many integer-feasible completions and finitely many discrete choices to resolve.
Every node relaxation is solved exactly, and every generated cut is valid for all integer-feasible schedules represented at that node.
Each node's cut phase terminates after finitely many additions.
Every branching disjunction covers the parent's integer-feasible completions and strictly resolves at least one previously unresolved discrete choice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination returns an optimal feasible schedule or correctly reports infeasibility.

children.title: Scheduling Cutting-Plane Families
children.top_down_role: Valid-inequality families targeting scheduling relaxation weaknesses.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Cutting-Plane Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid-inequality families for strengthening a scheduling relaxation without removing feasible schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) be the feasible scheduling vectors and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a relaxation with \(S\subseteq P\). A scheduling cutting-plane family is an indexed collection \(\mathcal{F}=\{(a^k,\beta_k):k\in K\}\) such that \((a^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_k\) for every \(x\in S\) and every \(k\in K\). Its strengthened relaxation is \(P_{\mathcal F}=P\cap\bigcap_{k\in K}\{x:(a^k)^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_k\}\). Hence \(S\subseteq P_{\mathcal F}\subseteq P\); the family is separating at \(\bar x\in P\) when some member is violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling cut family consists of inequalities valid for every feasible schedule; intersecting them with a relaxation preserves feasibility while potentially excluding fractional points.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d\) is the feasible set.
\(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) satisfies \(S\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq P_{\mathcal F}\subseteq P\).

children.title: Cut Separation for Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Detection of violated scheduling inequalities during exact search.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Separation for Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or heuristic separation of a specified valid-inequality family at a relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a relaxation point \(\bar x\in P\) and a valid family \(\mathcal F=\{(a^k,\beta_k):k\in K\}\), solve the separation problem \(k^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{k\in K}\{(a^k)^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta_k\}\). If the maximum violation is positive, return the cut \((a^{k^*})^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta_{k^*}\); otherwise certify that no inequality in \(\mathcal F\) separates \(\bar x\). A heuristic separator may return any positively violated member, but failure by a heuristic does not certify absence of a violated member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation searches a valid cut family for a maximally violated inequality; only exact nonpositive optimization certifies that the family contains no violated cut.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in P\).
Every member of \(\mathcal F\) is valid for the feasible scheduling set.
The maximum is attained when exact certification is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive optimum yields a separating cut; a nonpositive exact optimum certifies none exists in \(\mathcal F\).

children.title: Cut–Tree Integration

knowledge_statements.title: Cut–Tree Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct integration of node-local and globally valid cuts into branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each branch-and-bound node \(v\), form a relaxation from the original formulation, the branching restrictions on the root-to-\(v\) path, globally valid cuts, and cuts valid under those path restrictions. Separate and add cuts before evaluating the final node bound. A cut valid for every feasible schedule may be shared throughout the tree; a conditionally valid cut may be used only at nodes whose feasible sets satisfy its conditions. Prune only after reoptimization. If branching partitions every unresolved node's integer-feasible set, this integration preserves all feasible schedules and retains branch-and-bound exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global cuts may be shared across the tree, while conditional cuts remain local; reoptimized bounds and exhaustive branching preserve exactness.
assumptions_latex: All global cuts are valid for the original feasible set.
Every local cut is valid under its node's path restrictions.
Branching children cover the parent's integer-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No feasible schedule is removed, and exhaustive termination certifies the optimum or infeasibility.

children.title: Cut Scalability Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Scalability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational boundaries arising from large cut families and difficult exact separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_n\) be a valid scheduling-cut family for instances of size \(n\). If \(|\mathcal F_n|=2^{\Omega(n)}\), explicitly generating and storing every member requires exponential output space in the worst case. If deciding whether a given relaxation point violates some member of \(\mathcal F_n\) is NP-hard, then an exact polynomial-time separator for \(\mathcal F_n\) would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\). Therefore, absent additional structure, neither full cut enumeration nor polynomial-time exact separation is scalable; implementations must restrict the family, use implicit formulations, or accept heuristic separation without a completeness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential cut families preclude compact explicit enumeration, and NP-hard separation precludes a general polynomial exact separator unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \(|\mathcal F_n|=2^{\Omega(n)}\) for the enumeration boundary.
The separation decision problem for \(\mathcal F_n\) is NP-hard.
Complexity is measured in the standard deterministic polynomial-time model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full enumeration is exponential, and polynomial-time exact separation would imply \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\).

notation.meaning: cut family for size-n scheduling instances

children.title: Scheduling Column Generation
children.top_down_role: Generation of schedule columns for restricted master formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column generation for the linear relaxation of a schedule-pattern master formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the master problem \(\min\{\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}c_p\lambda_p:\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_p\lambda_p=b,\ \lambda_p\ge0\}\), choose a finite initial set \(R\subseteq\mathcal P\) yielding a feasible restricted master. Solve it and obtain an optimal dual vector \(\pi\). Find a pattern minimizing reduced cost \(\bar c_p=c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\). If \(\bar c_p<0\), add such a column to \(R\) and repeat. If the minimum reduced cost is nonnegative, the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation repeatedly solves a restricted schedule-pattern master and adds a negative-reduced-cost pattern until pricing certifies full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is finite.
The initial restricted master is feasible.
Restricted masters and pricing problems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_p\ge0\) certifies optimality for the full master relaxation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is standard and internally coherent, but no source supports the reduced-cost optimality certificate or its master-dual conventions.

children.title: Scheduling Pricing Problems

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Pricing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost optimization over feasible schedule patterns for a fixed master dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be the feasible schedule-pattern set, with column vector \(a_p\) and cost \(c_p\) for each \(p\in\mathcal P\). Given a master dual vector \(\pi\), the scheduling pricing problem is \[\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bigl(c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}\pi\bigr).\] A pattern attaining a negative value is an improving column for a minimization restricted master. If the optimum is nonnegative and the dual corresponds to an optimal restricted-master solution, then no omitted pattern violates the associated dual constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing minimizes reduced cost over all feasible schedule patterns; a negative optimum supplies an improving column, while a nonnegative exact optimum certifies no omitted dual violation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is the complete feasible pattern set.
\(\pi\) is a dual vector for the current restricted master.
Pricing is solved globally for certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative optimum gives an improving column; a nonnegative optimum excludes omitted dual violations.

children.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching structures that preserve manageable scheduling pricing problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Compatible Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring branch decisions preserve a tractable, exact pricing oracle at every child.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_v\) be the integer-feasible schedules represented at branch-and-price node \(v\), and let children impose restrictions \(D_1,\ldots,D_q\). The branching rule is pricing-compatible when \(S_v=\bigcup_{i=1}^q(S_v\cap D_i)\), the sets \(S_v\cap D_i\) are pairwise disjoint, and each restriction \(D_i\) can be enforced directly in the pricing problem without enumerating the full pattern set. Under exact child pricing, these conditions preserve exhaustive enumeration and valid column-generation bounds throughout the branch tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch is pricing-compatible when its disjoint children cover all parent schedules and each child restriction can be enforced by the pricing oracle.
assumptions_latex: \(S_v\) is the parent node's integer-feasible schedule set.
Each child pricing problem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children partition \(S_v\) and retain exact pricing-based bounds.
